section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56
text: Iced-Cream/analoghealth (README), a diagnostics mod that passed on an A4 MKII unit. Key {analoghealth}. Projects: [../../catalog/analog-four-keys.md](../../catalog/analog-four-keys.md). The short version: a ColdFire-only machine. There is no DSP chip; the effects and every digital part of the audio run on the ColdFire's EMAC inside one audio interrupt. The voices are analog. The interrupt is ~71 % busy before you add anything. Same platform family as the Analog Rytm (see [analog-rytm.md](analog-rytm.md)).

section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / Silicon and memory
text: CPU: ColdFire V4e with EMAC, no FPU, on both generations. analog-emu identifies MCF5441x by code and peripheral use. The A4 MK1 mods assemble with `-mcpu=5475 -mno-float`: that is a V4e ISA setting, and with `-mno-float` an FPU instruction becomes an assembly error instead of a crash on the unit. `[hw]` {a4mods} {analog-emu-a4}

section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / Silicon and memory
text: No DSP. No DSP56k strings, no second-CPU loader, no DSP firmware section. `[doc]` {analog-emu-a4}

section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / Silicon and memory
text: MK1: only `0x40000000-0x43ffffff` is cached. ACR0 covers that range and the default is cache-inhibited, so the effect delay lines (`0x468xxxxx` and up) and any mod state placed beside them are uncached: every access is a full bus round trip. An early chord-oscillator build made ~1,000 such accesses per block per voice; the UI slowed and the unit could crash. Copy state to the stack once per block, work there, write it back. `[hw]` {a4mods} ([I11](../INCIDENTS.md#i11-uncached-state-in-a-chord-oscillator-slowed-the-ui-and-could-crash-the-unit))

section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / Silicon and memory
text: On-chip SRAM is fully used. The OS fills the whole 64 KB SRAM from its image at boot, so the Digitakt mk1 trick of running audio code from free SRAM (digihealth's FAST AUDIO) has no room here. `[doc]` {analoghealth}

section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / Silicon and memory
text: MKII flash part on one unit: Winbond W25Q64 (8 MB, 256-byte pages, 64 KB sectors), reported by the factory console; the Rytm MKII uses an S25FL128S. Compare conflict O8 in [../CONFLICTS.md](../CONFLICTS.md). `[hw]` {analog-emu-a4}

section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / Audio engine (MK1 OS 1.55 names; layout the same on 1.56)
text: One interrupt does all digital audio, per 32-sample block (`[doc]` code reading, confirmed by a probe build on a unit) {a4mods}: 1. pick the DMA buffer; 2. run the control block: envelopes, LFOs and per-track levels, which turn each volume into (a) a send gain plus pan and (b) the analog dry VCA words; 3. generate the four digital noise sources; 4. run the FX block: the codec's receive frames (eight slots per sample, six used: four voices and the stereo input) are mixed into three stereo send buses, then chorus, delay and reverb run, and only their summed returns go out to the DAC; 5. send the CV/voice frame to the hardware.

section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / Audio engine (MK1 OS 1.55 names; layout the same on 1.56)
text: The dry voice is analog to the outputs. The digital side gets a captured copy and returns only the effects.

section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / Audio engine (MK1 OS 1.55 names; layout the same on 1.56)
text: The capture point is before the analog output VCA (`[hw]`, a probe build that muted track 1's dry in software while its sends still carried the voice). A mod can therefore silence a track's dry path and process its digital copy instead. hugz202's "digital path" mod does exactly that. {a4mods}

section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / Audio engine (MK1 OS 1.55 names; layout the same on 1.56)
text: The MKII has the same structure: RX slots 0-3 are the four voices before their VCA, RX 4/5 most likely EXT IN, TX 4/5 the effect returns. `[emu]` {analog-emu-a4}

section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / Load budget (measured on an A4 MK1 with a probe build, 2026-10-09)
text: The effects run whether anything plays or not, so the cost is mostly fixed; the peaks come from block-to-block variation and preemption. Worst case left: ~11 %, and the UI and sequencer run in that remainder too. `[hw]`

section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / Load budget (measured on an A4 MK1 with a probe build, 2026-10-09)
text: Their budget rule: stay well under ~5 % at peak for new blocks, and prefer *replacing* work (the chorus slot) to adding it. A per-track drive/bit-crush insert is ~1-2 % per processed track. `[hw]` Same lesson as rule A34.

section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / Where mod code can live (MK1 OS 1.56)
text: Almost no free space. Mods use the padding between the C++ constructor table and `__bss_start`, a 1 KB gap between chorus lookup tables that no index can reach, and runs of code the firmware contains but never calls.

section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / Where mod code can live (MK1 OS 1.56)

Hash the stock bytes before writing there. `[hw]` (these builds have run on units)

section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / Where mod code can live (MK1 OS 1.56)
text: Keep a registry with every patched address, its expected stock bytes and its owner. Refuse to build when the stock bytes don't match, and verify every detour's return path on the finished `.syx`. This is the same method as rule A31: prove both sides. `[doc]`

section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / The bootstrap is inside MAIN OS (MK1) - never write into it
text: The MK1 `.syx` has one section. The bootstrap (STARTUP menu plus DIN-MIDI OS UPGRADE) is carried inside MAIN OS: on 1.56 its version words are at `0x40226958` and its image at `0x40226960..0x40233a30` (53,456 B).

section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / The bootstrap is inside MAIN OS (MK1) - never write into it
text: At every boot the startup code compares that version with the one in flash at `0xfff8`. If the embedded one is newer, it erases the bootstrap sectors and writes the embedded image. So a mod byte in that range could one day become the recovery path. `[doc]` (code reading)

section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / The bootstrap is inside MAIN OS (MK1) - never write into it

section: Analog Four / Analog Keys (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.56 / OS update and recovery
text: MKII update in the emulator (`[emu]` {analog-emu-a4}): The OS saves its working state to the card, erases 17 x 64 KB from flash `0x80000` and programs the container page by page, then resets. From the first erase to the last page there is no bootable OS in flash; a power cut then needs the DIN recovery. The power-fail handler waits for a running erase.

text: SysEx device byte 0x13. Container ELE3, build "S0063", version "1.02", 969,776 B. No trailer and no HMAC seal. The byte-exact round trip works, and a second, independent unpacker (digikit elz) agrees.

section: Analog Heat (MKI, MKII, +FX) / Analog Heat +FX OS 1.02 - first firmware facts (findings by 70b185, owner of this repo)
text: Sections: 5 meta: 15 B, timestamp "241008 20:29:59", not packed. 2 bootstrap: 26,638 B, runs from SRAM `0x80000400`, stack `0x80010000`, entry `0x80000ddc`. It holds the STARTUP MENU (TEST MODE, EMPTY RESET, FACTORY RESET, OS UPGRADE) and the bootstrap upgrade. 1 FPGA: Xilinx bitstream, 54,664 B, sync `aa 99`. It is loaded by the OS ("INITB WENT LOW..."); its role is unknown. 3 MAIN OS: 2,174,964 B, destination `0x40000400`, entry `0x40001384`. 4 updater: 29,384 B, not packed, destination `0x80000400`.

section: Analog Heat (MKI, MKII, +FX) / Analog Heat +FX OS 1.02 - first firmware facts (findings by 70b185, owner of this repo)
text: The updater copies section 3 with its 8-byte header to `0x40200000` and unpacks it in place to `0x40000400` (aPLib). The image ends at `0x402133F4`. The smallest write/read pointer gap is 825,529 B for stock and 774,349 B for a repack.

section: Analog Heat (MKI, MKII, +FX) / Analog Heat +FX OS 1.02 - first firmware facts (findings by 70b185, owner of this repo)
text: After boot: `0x40000400-0x40206000` stays in DDR. `0x40206000-0x4020b4fc` is copied to SRAM `0x80000000`, and `0x4020b4fc-0x402133f4` to SRAM `0x80008000`. DDR from `0x40206000` up to `0x426383d0` is then cleared. Custom code therefore only lives below `0x40206000`. Unreferenced zero runs of 2 KB or more: `0x402057c4-0x40206000` (2,108 B) and `0x4019efbc-0x4019f7cf`.

section: Analog Heat (MKI, MKII, +FX) / Analog Heat +FX OS 1.02 - first firmware facts (findings by 70b185, owner of this repo)
text: Audio runs on the ColdFire itself: SSI1 with eDMA channels 52 and 54. Channel 54 raises the interrupt (vector 174, priority 6). Its handler (`0x400a3e84`) timestamps the block, counts it and raises a software interrupt (vector 191, priority 5, handler `0x400a3ee6`). The software interrupt processes a 4 x 512-byte ring in SRAM. Hypothesis, not verified: 32 frames x 4 channels x 4 bytes = 1,500 blocks/s.

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Platform (MKII, OS 1.74)
text: Sections of 1.74: 2 bootstrap (42,302 B, loads at `0x07020000`, runs in SRAM `0x80000000`), 1 FPGA (Xilinx bitstream, 149,516 B, sync `AA99`), 3 MAIN OS (3,005,432 B), 8 the shared ARM Cortex-M image (159,948 B, identical across several devices; see [firmware-container.md](../common/firmware-container.md)), 5 meta. `[doc]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Platform (MKII, OS 1.74)
text: The display is driven through the FPGA: a byte-FIFO bridge at `0xec07xxxx` (status `0xec070004`, data `0xec07000c`). The 128x64 panel uses two static 1,024-byte planes with diff flush. `0xec074xxx` is the MIDI UART (divisor 132 MHz / (31,250 x 32)). The LED engine is fed through the same FPGA SRAM family. `[doc]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Platform (MKII, OS 1.74)
text: Boot contract: The bootstrap unpacks MAIN to `0x40000400`, sets VBR = `0x40000000` and calls the word at `0x40000400` as an entry function pointer with one stack argument. It is not a reset SP/PC header. The stock entry sets SP to `0x48000000`, fills 256 vectors, sets up INTC/GPIO and caches (CACR `0xa50ce100`), then starts the kernel. `[hw]` (a from-source replacement OS booted on a unit)

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Platform (MKII, OS 1.74)
text: Which ColdFire is open: rytm-fw-re builds with `-mcpu=54455` (MCF5445x), while analog-emu identifies the Rytm MKII as MCF5441x (same entry code, CACR/ACR values and peripheral blocks as the A4 MKII). Both are V4 cores with EMAC and no FPU, so code built for either runs; peripheral addresses are what to check. See CONFLICTS O14. `[?]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Platform (MKII, OS 1.74)
text: A 16.3 MB unreferenced hole at `0x41ad0000` passed a memory probe on a unit (7 candidate regions all passed). `[hw]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Flash and recovery
text: SPI NOR on DSPI `0xfc05c000`; layout: `0x00000-0x7FFFF` bootstrap + FPGA (never write), `0x80000+` the MAIN OS image. Images are staged in DDR at `0x3FF80008` with the same `size / checksum (i ^ word[i])` header as the small boxes. `[doc]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Flash and recovery
text: The bootstrap supports several flash vendors and picks the geometry from the RDID: | Vendor | Page | Erase block | |---|---|---| | Spansion `0x01 2018` | 0x200 | 0x40000 | | Winbond `0xEF` | 0x100 | 0x10000 | | Macronix `0xC2` | 0x100 | 0x10000 | | ISSI `0x9D` | 0x100 | 0x10000 | | EON `0x1C` | 0x100 | 0x10000 | The geometry therefore differs per unit. This very likely explains the two geometries reported for DT2/DN2 (CONFLICTS O8) and why a Spansion-only protection command does nothing on a Winbond unit (O9). `[doc]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Flash and recovery
text: The bootstrap also gates on a version-date field (image +0x10, 4 ASCII chars) per chip family, and refuses older versions. `[doc]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Flash and recovery
text: Recovery is FUNC at power-on, OS UPGRADE, DIN MIDI only. The startup-menu receiver never enumerates USB (verified: no USB events while it shows READY TO RECEIVE). USB updates are received only by the running OS. Once a custom OS that does not implement the USB update is on the unit, the only way back is DIN ("one USB shot per custom-OS cycle"). `[hw]` rytm-fw-re rebuilt a DIN sender from an FT232RL (2 x 200 ohm) and streamed stock 1.74 back in about 10 minutes. `[hw]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Flash and recovery
text: Rule for every device: a replacement or heavily modified OS should keep the in-OS USB update working, or the user needs a DIN interface. See rule A36 in [`../AGENT-RULES.md`](../AGENT-RULES.md).

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Analog Rytm MK1 (OS 1.73 / 1.74)
text: Board (static analysis, `[doc]`): same CPU family and OS framework as the MKII; ELE2 file with one section (MAIN OS); 128 MB DDR, boot/config flash as parallel NOR on FlexBus CS0 (8 MB at 0); voice SPI on DSPI2 with eDMA ch 29 (492-word frame, as the MKII); codec on SSI0 + SSI1 (8 words each); 122x32 LCD, 1-bit LEDs; USB full speed only.

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Analog Rytm MK1 (OS 1.73 / 1.74)
text: The bootstrap is inside MAIN OS, as on the A4 MK1 (rule A38): On 1.74 its version words are at `0x4028c768` and its image at `0x4028c770..0x402a1b84` (87,068 B, ending in its USB descriptors). On 1.73 the same image sat 0x60 lower. At every boot the startup code compares that version with the one in flash at `0x1fff8`. If the embedded one is newer, the OS shows BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE and rewrites the bootstrap sectors. `[doc]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Analog Rytm MK1 (OS 1.73 / 1.74)
text: Container pitfall: elektron-firmware-tool padded ELE2 containers to 2 bytes; the stock MK1 file pads to 4. A "no change" rebuild therefore came out 2 bytes short and failed the null-repack check. hugz202 patches the tool to pad to 4. Always run a null repack of the stock file first (rule A23). `[hw]` ([I40](../INCIDENTS.md#i40-a-no-change-rebuild-came-out-2-bytes-short))

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Analog Rytm MK1 (OS 1.73 / 1.74)
text: Load (measured with a probe build on a MK1, OS 1.73): Stock audio alone is about 77 % of the CPU with nothing playing. One readout showed CPU 78.3 %, the audio interrupt at 61.2 % average and 74.0 % peak. With a first chorus-plus-comb send on, the CPU reached 100 %. The CPU runs at roughly 120 MIPS. A one-to-one port of the A4's chorus (~8,000-9,000 instructions per block) would cost ~10 % of the unit and was rejected. Same lesson as A34: replace work, and keep added effects idle when no track sends. `[hw]` Idle mods add up (Modwerk, 2026-11-06, OS 1.74, sequencer stopped, block timed on DTIM0): in a 16-module set the idle block took 72.9 %; making three modules return early when they have nothing to do (Ping Pong Loop's voice gates in stock's sample prefetch, Sample Playback Rate's block handler, QPERF) brought it to 70.6-71.1 %. Each module's idle path is part of the budget. `[hw]` {modwerk-rytm-idle} ([I49](../INCIDENTS.md#i49-idle-paths-of-sixteen-mods-cost-two-percent-of-a-rytm-block))

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Analog Rytm MK1 (OS 1.73 / 1.74)
text: Cached vs uncached DRAM: the chorus's delay line moved to a cached DRAM address (`0x428a0000`) in v2. The same rule applies as on the A4 MK1: don't touch uncached memory per sample. `[doc]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Analog Rytm MK1 (OS 1.73 / 1.74)
text: RAM is not cleared at power-up in the regions the mods use: clear your own buffers before use. `[hw]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Analog Rytm MK1 (OS 1.73 / 1.74)
text: Dead code to reuse: The machine table (53 entries at `0x402543d0` on 1.73) holds 19 hidden machines whose voice-mask byte is 0, so no list offers them. They look like earlier development versions of the shipped machines, and none has been played on hardware. TEST machines (SD/RS/CY/CB) also exist. hugz202 reuses their code space. Its only reference is its own table entry, which the mod repoints, and the build checks the stock bytes. A kit received over SysEx that names a hidden machine then plays the mod's machine or nothing. `[hw]` (the `full` image ran on a MK1)

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Analog Rytm MK1 (OS 1.73 / 1.74)
text: Recovery: FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4 (OS UPGRADE), stock `.syx` over DIN MIDI (Transfer's legacy mode). `[doc]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Mod machines in hidden slots (MKII OS 1.74, elekloader core-ar2 0.5; Modwerk's SDK guide, 2026-11-05)
text: Slots and claims: a mod machine takes one of the hidden slots 34-43 through `core_machines` and claims it as `machine:<slot>` (rule D6c). Kits store the slot, so a kit naming it loads as DISABLE on a build without the mod. `[doc]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Mod machines in hidden slots (MKII OS 1.74, elekloader core-ar2 0.5; Modwerk's SDK guide, 2026-11-05)
text: From core-ar2 0.13 (2026-11-10) also slots 44-52, the TEST machines. Their records carry no MIDI, so core copies each used knob's CC and NRPN from slot 35's record at the same sound index; the records' list-kind word (+0x24) stays 0, so a knob there is not offered as an LFO, velocity or aftertouch destination. Fewer knob records than 34-43 on several voices (e.g. SD TEST 9-12, 15, 16). `[doc]` {elekloader-core-ar2}

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Mod machines in hidden slots (MKII OS 1.74, elekloader core-ar2 0.5; Modwerk's SDK guide, 2026-11-05)
text: Per-voice trig and velocity (0.13): core's trampoline per slot latches the owner track (`0x40291138[v]`), the trig state (`0x8000e508 + 4t`, 1 trig, 2 release) and the velocity word (`0x800067c4 + 2t`) before the engine runs; `core_voice_trigged(v)` and `core_voice_velocity(v)` read it. A knob on a record that is 14-bit in stock keeps a fraction in its engine word: read the high byte for the shown value. `[doc]` {elekloader-core-ar2}

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Mod machines in hidden slots (MKII OS 1.74, elekloader core-ar2 0.5; Modwerk's SDK guide, 2026-11-05)
text: Knob ids: mods get their own parameter ids from 555 on; a mod declares `"knobs": n` and the linker hands out n ids in a row (`__knobs`). `[doc]` {elekloader-format}

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Mod machines in hidden slots (MKII OS 1.74, elekloader core-ar2 0.5; Modwerk's SDK guide, 2026-11-05)
text: Screen calls (0.13): text, fonts, bitmaps, the level read-out field, progress boxes and keys go through stock's own routines (font objects at `0x417e381c + 8i`, text `0x4007154c`, progress window as COPYING SOUNDS uses it); no stock code or glyphs are copied. `[doc]` {elekloader-core-ar2}

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Mod machines in hidden slots (MKII OS 1.74, elekloader core-ar2 0.5; Modwerk's SDK guide, 2026-11-05)
text: Fixed knob positions per slot (SYNTH page, sound indices): slot 40 A10 B13 C12 D11 / E14 F16 G15 H9; slot 41 A10 B13 C15 D11 / E16 F14 G12 H9; slot 42 A10 B12 C13 D11 / E16 F14 G15 H9. `knobs[k]` in `machines.h` is sound index 9 + k, not the panel order. Indices 9 (LEV), 10 (TUN) and 11 (DEC) keep stock's MIDI CCs. `[doc]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Mod machines in hidden slots (MKII OS 1.74, elekloader core-ar2 0.5; Modwerk's SDK guide, 2026-11-05)
text: Where it appears in the machine list: a 34-byte section table at `0x40257d70` (read by `0x400df664`) files stock machines 0-33 under a section; slots 34+ have no entry and sort above every stock machine of their group. A machine with `home` -1 lands after DISABLE in slot order. Core 0.5 adds a 4-byte entry (slot, section, 0, 0) so a mod machine sits under its section's header. The SY comparators (`0x400bdc5e`, `0x400bde1c`) rank only SY DUAL VCO, SY CHIP and SY RAW, so a mod SY machine sorts after them. `[doc]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Mod machines in hidden slots (MKII OS 1.74, elekloader core-ar2 0.5; Modwerk's SDK guide, 2026-11-05)
text: Driving a dual-oscillator voice (BD, SD, RS; control frame `0x800063c0`, TUNE1/TUNE2/LEVEL1/LEVEL2 at `+90`, `+98`, `+106`, as SY RAW `0x4011aa4c` writes them). Measured on a unit: A tune word is 16 x Hz after stock's trim `0x401197f4`. Write it every block and force it on the trig; without that the oscillator crawls at a few Hz. Below about 40 Hz oscillator 1 runs sharp and oscillator 2 flat. A LEVEL word acts within its block. Its loud end saturates mostly after AMP VOL, so it is not a drive control. An amp record at -128 still passes about -45 dB: write the LEVELs to 0 when a note ends. `[hw]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Mod machines in hidden slots (MKII OS 1.74, elekloader core-ar2 0.5; Modwerk's SDK guide, 2026-11-05)
text: FUNC + turn drops its first detent on the sound page (flag `0x417e32b8`); jumps come from a std::function in the parameter's RAM record (`0x419a4888 + 84 * id`, manager `+0x4c`, invoker `+0x50`). `[doc]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / More from the MKII mod and research projects (rytm-mods-src OS 1.73, analog-rytm-mkii-research OS 1.72)
text: A zero run is not a free cave until it survives a hard run on the unit. octatrack-mods had shipped code into a region that came from someone else's survey. The mod worked with the sequencer stopped and failed during playback, because the region was really `.bss` that the audio engine wrote. rytm-mods-src's check: fill the candidate with a known pattern, flash, run playback, sampling, Overbridge and +Drive access, then read it back. See rule A43. `[hw]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / More from the MKII mod and research projects (rytm-mods-src OS 1.73, analog-rytm-mkii-research OS 1.72)
text: Pick the narrowest assembler target that assembles. The project went from `-mcpu=5407` (ISA_A) to `-mcpu=5475` (ISA_B + EMAC) only when a mod needed EMAC, and checked that the earlier mods rebuilt byte-identically. Too narrow a target fails at assembly time; too wide a one silently accepts instructions the chip lacks (rule A42). `[doc]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / More from the MKII mod and research projects (rytm-mods-src OS 1.73, analog-rytm-mkii-research OS 1.72)
text: Sections 5, 2, 1 and 8 must come back byte-identical, and the bootstrap (section 2, 42,302 B at `0x07020000`) is checked by hash. Elektron's own bootstrap upgrade, which runs on the first restart after some OS updates, is the one moment the safety net is down: don't cut power then. `[doc]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / More from the MKII mod and research projects (rytm-mods-src OS 1.73, analog-rytm-mkii-research OS 1.72)
text: The master compressor is analog (after the analog mix and the master distortion). The MKII firmware never reads its gain back (the MK1 did, through the on-chip ADC input AN1), so any gain-reduction display on the MKII is an estimate. A CC beyond an enumeration's last value makes the unit show ERR instead of clamping. `[doc]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / More from the MKII mod and research projects (rytm-mods-src OS 1.73, analog-rytm-mkii-research OS 1.72)
text: Sample bit reduction is not done on the ColdFire. The BR knob becomes a per-voice command word, `0xB31407FF + ceil(BR x 0x40000 / 127)`, sent over DSPI1/eDMA to the external audio hardware. The main OS contains no mask or shift that would apply it to PCM. So sample playback processing on the Rytm MKII likely sits in the FPGA/voice hardware: a lead for research map T12. Static and emulator work only. `[doc]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / More from the MKII mod and research projects (rytm-mods-src OS 1.73, analog-rytm-mkii-research OS 1.72)
text: A third reading of the CPU: analog-rytm-mkii-research models the Rytm MKII as MCF5441x (conflict O14), with MAIN at `0x40000400` (2,903,032 B on 1.72) and the stack at `0x48000000`. `[doc]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / More from the MKII mod and research projects (rytm-mods-src OS 1.73, analog-rytm-mkii-research OS 1.72)
text: Porting MKII mods to the MK1: same code base, different data (gdeo607/rytm1_mods, OS 1.73) {rytm1-mods}: Most routines are byte-identical, but the parameter info record is 88 bytes on the MK1 and 84 on the MKII. UI glyphs and the screen differ (122 px wide on the MK1, 128x64 on the MKII), so anything that draws its own pixels needs a redesign, not new addresses. Every RAM address (`0x41xxxxxx`, `0x8000xxxx`) has to be found again. Each of these would have been a silent bug. `[doc]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Modwerk Rytm modules and stock behaviour (OS 1.74, 2026-11-10)
text: Encoder events: byte +20 of an encoder event is set while that knob's own push-button is held. It is not FUNC; read FUNC from the key table. `[hw]` (I55)

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Modwerk Rytm modules and stock behaviour (OS 1.74, 2026-11-10)
text: Machine list: stock loads each machine as the list scrolls (UP, DOWN or any knob, with or without FUNC); YES only confirms, NO restores the machine the list opened with, and there is no undo for a machine change. rytm-emu does not pass emulated knob turns through stock's knob accumulator, so knob behaviour cannot be tested there. `[emu]` {modwerk-rytm-machines}

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Modwerk Rytm modules and stock behaviour (OS 1.74, 2026-11-10)
text: FX edit save: stock maps live FX words 38-41 to stored slot 0, so a setter edit of those hidden words overwrites the delay's saved TIME (SB18). Modwerk's base redirects them to its own kit storage. `[emu]` {modwerk-rytm-machines}

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Modwerk Rytm modules and stock behaviour (OS 1.74, 2026-11-10)
text: Lock saves keep bits 14-8 of a lock word; bits 7-1 survive only in a fine lane, one per track and word, which stock writes when the parameter row's fine flag (row word `+0x14`, read at `0x400071a6`, lane write `0x40009216`) is set: STA, END, LFO DEP and the machines' tunings have it, sample TUN and FIN do not. Bit 0 is always lost; test with odd values. (Corrects the earlier "bits 14-1", CONFLICTS S19.) `[emu]` {modwerk-rytm-machines} {modwerk-rytm-smpl}

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Modwerk Rytm modules and stock behaviour (OS 1.74, 2026-11-10)
text: Shared voices: the amp-envelope record is at `0x40109c24`, 18 bytes per voice per block. A trig still takes a shared voice (CH/OH, RS/CP, MT/HT, CY/CB) even when its amp is held silent, so the partner is cut; dropping the trig in the audio-block trig loop (command byte `0x8000e508[track]`) keeps a track silent without that. A pad's light is a running mean of its own voice's level, so a dropped trig leaves the pad dark. `[doc]`, the silencing route `[hw]` (Silent Pad+Trig 0.8.0, run AT04)

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Modwerk Rytm modules and stock behaviour (OS 1.74, 2026-11-10)
text: CV input: EXP/CV IN 1 in CV mode read raw `0x3fcc` at 0 V, `0x6048` at about 2.5 V and `0x7fff` at 5 V; with nothing plugged in it reads below CV ZERO. `[hw]` (run T221, driven from an A4 MKII CV out)

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Modwerk Rytm modules and stock behaviour (OS 1.74, 2026-11-10)
text: Stock mutes and MIDI: on stock 1.74 a muted or soloed-out track still plays incoming MIDI notes (AUTO and its own channel, USB and DIN), and a held note keeps ringing after a CC 94 mute. By design, not a bug. `[hw]` (MIDI Mute's stock baseline)

text: Kit list: on a unit the kit list draws a marker after kits 02-16 that rytm-emu's screen lacks (I56). `[hw]`

text: Load on Modwerk's base (core-ar2 0.7 plus its health meter): about 74-75 % idle; 85 % with Compressor Preview open while playing; 92.9 % (DSP 86 %) with four Voice DAC voices beside LFO RND. `[hw]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / +Drive mods loaded at boot (elekloader drive-loader-ar2 0.4, core-ar2 0.12, OS 1.74)
text: A third Data route. The loader adds a `/mods` route to stock's Data router (the one Transfer and Elektroid use for `/projects` and `/soundbanks`), registered at `0x400a005e` in the resolver's getter; uploads travel in stock's data container (31-byte header, 12-byte footer with CRC-32; a stock 1.74 project reads family 2, device 5). Folders go three deep; stock's rename moves a folder only within its parent, so a move elsewhere is mkdir plus one move per item, as SAMPLES' MOVE does. `[doc]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / +Drive mods loaded at boot (elekloader drive-loader-ar2 0.4, core-ar2 0.12, OS 1.74)
text: Files on the +Drive need a 16-byte zero header. The files share the sample filesystem, and stock's SAMPLES browser lists every folder, `/mods` too. LOAD TO PROJECT reads a file's first 16 bytes as a sample header: a raw `.elemod` there hangs stock, and a project that holds one stalls the next OS upgrade at PREPARING until CREATE NEW (SB19). The loader writes 16 zero bytes in front of every file, which stock loads as an empty sample. `[doc]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / +Drive mods loaded at boot (elekloader drive-loader-ar2 0.4, core-ar2 0.12, OS 1.74)
text: The link runs at boot from a site at `0x401009e0` in `main()`, after the +Drive is mounted and before audio and the UI task start; it skips when [NO] is held at power-on, when the eMMC or filesystem did not come up, or when a crash flag `/mods/.armed` from the last start is there (deleted about 10 s after the mods' inits ran). Its working memory (about 270 KB for the 4.3 MB area) comes from stock's heap and goes back after the link. The area runs from the flashed build's RAM end to `0x47FFF000`. `[doc]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / +Drive mods loaded at boot (elekloader drive-loader-ar2 0.4, core-ar2 0.12, OS 1.74)
text: Keep UI-task work small. Reading 13 files of 484 KB when a page opened held the key path and USB for over 5 s, and reading 257 small files for their sizes lost a key on a unit; the loader now reads 32 KB per tick, rests three times as long as it worked (timed with DTIM0) and waits 1 s after any key or encoder turn. Past 16 queued UI events, a remote key is refused as busy. `[hw]` (key loss) / `[doc]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / +Drive mods loaded at boot (elekloader drive-loader-ar2 0.4, core-ar2 0.12, OS 1.74)
text: Stock's two-pane file view (the one SAMPLES and PROJECTS use, `0x400734f2`) hangs the UI when it is first shown with no row at all; stock's own lists never are empty (`..`, or 128 RAM slots). `[doc]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Queued trigs: what a mod can see before a trig fires (Modwerk, OS 1.74, read from the code)
text: The sequencer queues a track's next trig one step ahead, its probability already rolled, in the lowest free of three event slots per track (state at `0x42ac5fb0 + 224*track + 56*slot`, fire time at `0x8000fd50 + 12*track + 4*slot` on the clock at `0x8000fe54`, which moves 2 x tempo per block). A trig queued while an earlier one still waits (swing, micro timing) lands in the second or third slot. Pads, MIDI notes and the first trig after PLAY take a fourth slot at once and cannot be seen ahead. `[doc]` (a trig that will not play is not queued: rytm-emu at 50 %, a unit for FILL and 2:2 `[hw]`)

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Queued trigs: what a mod can see before a trig fires (Modwerk, OS 1.74, read from the code)
text: Stock fires one event per track per block, so two due in one block take that block and the next. Mutes and a track's held word apply when the trig fires, not when it is queued. Retrigs are not queued: they run on their own tick counter. A pattern change clears queued events from the change on. `[doc]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Modwerk Rytm findings (OS 1.74, 2026-11-11)
text: Keys: `Brain::key` is at `0x400a0336`; calling it directly skips the `ev_key` handlers after it, so a mod plays actions through the base's `core_key`. `[emu]`

text: Stored records are read only by their load serializers. In a cold boot watched over the whole stored project image (`0x405c8f20`, 0x1f9f32 B), the only readers were each record's loader, the project-load code, and whole-image copies. Dumps are serialised from live objects. `[emu]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Where a MKII mod can keep its own data (rytm-mods-src `re/subsystems`, OS 1.73, checked in 1.74 by byte match; static plus rytm-emu, nothing on a unit)
text: 37 stored kit bytes stock never reads or writes: kit `+0x832..+0x841` (16 B) and `+0x902..+0x916` (21 B), on either side of the performance block (whose loader and saver start at `+0x842`). Mod 0018 keeps its scene mute masks there, behind a tag byte `0x53` at `+0x90c`. Whole-image copies carry them; kit copy/paste and SysEx kit transfer go through a live buffer and drop them. `[emu]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Where a MKII mod can keep its own data (rytm-mods-src `re/subsystems`, OS 1.73, checked in 1.74 by byte match; static plus rytm-emu, nothing on a unit)
text: A 140-byte gap in the power-fail image: `0x405c8e84..0x405c8f0f`, between the end of the checksummed `COKI` global block and a saved random seed (`0x405c8f10`). The whole 2,096,059-byte image from `0x405c8e10` is written to eMMC (slots `0x7a000` / `0x7c000`) on power-fail and read back at boot. No code reference lands in the gap, and a marker survived a power-off and a cold boot in the emulator. Not yet checked: project and kit saves, OS upgrade, factory reset. Nothing initialises the gap, so give your data a tag (mod 0017 uses `CIPF`). `[emu]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Where a MKII mod can keep its own data (rytm-mods-src `re/subsystems`, OS 1.73, checked in 1.74 by byte match; static plus rytm-emu, nothing on a unit)
text: "Loosened" bytes have a cost on stock: bytes that stock reads but always holds at one value (for example the 8 low bytes of the velocity and aftertouch route amounts, sound `+0x71/+0x74/+0x77/+0x7a` and `+0x8d/+0x90/+0x93/+0x96`) can carry mod data only if every stock reader is hooked. A project or dump using them is then not safe on unhooked firmware: a changed version long makes the record load at defaults, and a level LSB at 127 loads as 100. Bytes stock never reads are harmless there. See rule E3. `[doc]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Where a MKII mod can keep its own data (rytm-mods-src `re/subsystems`, OS 1.73, checked in 1.74 by byte match; static plus rytm-emu, nothing on a unit)
text: Performance macros are engine state, not kit data: 12 words at `0x8000e57c + 2k` (0..`0x7f00`), glided each block (~22 ms) into `0x8000f774[0..11]`. Their setter `0x400b2bfe` raises no change notice, so the kit is not marked edited. CTRL IN 1/2 are ADC slots 0 and 1, smoothed and mapped each block by `adc_pedal_update` (`0x4013f1c8`). `[doc]`

section: Analog Rytm (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.73 / 1.74 / Where a MKII mod can keep its own data (rytm-mods-src `re/subsystems`, OS 1.73, checked in 1.74 by byte match; static plus rytm-emu, nothing on a unit)
text: Track mutes belong to the project, scenes to the kit. Every UI and MIDI mute goes through `track_mute_set` (`0x400b786c`); Overbridge uses `track_mute_set_silent` (`0x400b6d6c`), which has no guard and bypasses hooks on the main setter. All scene engages (pads, CC 92, NRPN `0xE8`, Overbridge) go through `kit_scene_set_active` (`0x400a7d04`). `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 1. Two hangs on silicon that the emulator ran bit-exactly `[hw]`
text: H-opt1, RINGS as a hand-written SIMD kernel: the DSP hung on the first block, and all audio died. ([I14](../INCIDENTS.md#i14-dag-registers-stored-through-their-own-dag-hung-the-dsp)) Cause, confirmed with a one-variable probe image: DAG registers stored through their own DAG (`DM(I7, M7) = M4` and similar, used to save I0/I1/M4/M6/L0/L1/L4). The PRM forbids it for Types 3 and 15. Stock loads such registers through their own DAG thousands of times but never stores one. The probe was `probe-samedag-store`, a single `DM(I4, M6) = M4` and no SIMD. Fix: push DAG registers through R0.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 1. Two hangs on silicon that the emulator ran bit-exactly `[hw]`
text: SIMD-mode loads and stores (the implicit PEy access at +4 bytes) into L2 byte space have no stock precedent: stock does SIMD data accesses only in L1 normal-word space, and SIMD stores to DDR at most. The manual allows them, but they are unproven on silicon. The shipping kernel does SIMD compute only and moves every load and store in SISD, toggling PEYEN per sample as stock does. Cost: 125,766 -> 31,472 instructions per block versus the C version. The full-SIMD version would have been 27,404.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 1. Two hangs on silicon that the emulator ran bit-exactly `[hw]`
text: Lesson: an instruction word with a stock precedent is necessary but not sufficient. How stock combines operands also matters: which registers go through which DAG, and which access mode in which memory region. The encoding gate now refuses same-DAG stores and any data transfer while PEYEN is set.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 1. Two hangs on silicon that the emulator ran bit-exactly `[hw]`
text: Emulator gaps seen here: It wraps immediate-offset accesses circularly when L != 0, so own the L register of every I you use that way. It treats never-written L2 as unknown per 32-bit word, which halts code that legitimately reads half of such a word.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 2. Encoding traps (selas), each caught by a gate before it reached a unit
text: `JUMP (PC, label)` assembled to a jump to itself; the kernel spun forever. Write `JUMP label` as selcc does.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 2. Encoding traps (selas), each caught by a gate before it reached a unit
text: selas does not compress inside a DO loop. Under `.COMPRESS` it can merge or drop a statement after a loop end or a `(DB)` branch. Write delayed-branch code under `.NOCOMPRESS` and cross-check statements against instructions.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 2. Encoding traps (selas), each caught by a gate before it reached a unit
text: `Rn = Rn + Rm` and `Rn = Rn XOR Rm` compress to 16-bit forms that stock never uses, so write integer adds under `.NOCOMPRESS`. Stock contains no plain XOR at all.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 2. Encoding traps (selas), each caught by a gate before it reached a unit
text: A label defined in two sources resolves to one of them in the merged object. Each kernel's own test passed, but the merged image jumped into the wrong file. Use unique label prefixes per file.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 2. Encoding traps (selas), each caught by a gate before it reached a unit
text: Delay slots: after a delayed branch, the two slots must not hold a branch, a DO, a PC-stack operation, IDLE, or a write of the indirect branch's I/M. After a conditional branch, they should also not hold a flag writer (stock does that, but it is avoided as a precaution).

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 2. Encoding traps (selas), each caught by a gate before it reached a unit
text: The last 11 instructions of every DO loop are 48-bit, and the loop end is an instruction ([rule A45](../AGENT-RULES.md)). The other code can be compressed. Compression shrank the kernels by 10-30 %, which matters because the instruction cache is the bottleneck (section 3).

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 3. Where the cycles go on the SHARC+ (calibrated cycle model)
text: Instruction-cache misses are the largest stall class (33 %). Every model touches 150-300 code lines (10-19 KB) of L2 code per voice block, near or above the 16 KB 2-way cache. The lever is code size (compression, kernels instead of selcc C, fewer calls), not code order.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 3. Where the cycles go on the SHARC+ (calibrated cycle model)
text: DAG write-to-use stalls are 32 %, almost all in selcc C (`In = Rm` or `In = DM(..)` followed directly by a use). selcc has no optimiser, so only hand kernels remove them.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 3. Where the cycles go on the SHARC+ (calibrated cycle model)
text: Data-cache misses are 18 % (cold) and only a few % warm: the tables mostly hit. Float forwarding is 14 %, taken branches 4 %.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 3. Where the cycles go on the SHARC+ (calibrated cycle model)
text: This core has no load-to-use stall, and a cache miss stalls whatever the distance. Scheduling loads earlier only helps to free registers.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 3. Where the cycles go on the SHARC+ (calibrated cycle model)
text: Fewer instructions are not fewer cycles. One kernel cut instructions by 46 %, but the calibrated load fell by only 1.2 points. Code-size changes alone move a measurement by about 1 point (layout noise).

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 3. Where the cycles go on the SHARC+ (calibrated cycle model)
text: Stock 1.17 with one trigged track sits at ~48.6 % on the high bound. The calibration on the unit: 8 KICK tracks measured 91.7 %, and the sound turned choppy above ~87 %.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 4. Optimisation rules the project enforces (worth copying)
text: Lazy clear: skipping a large memory clear at init is exact only if the write-before-read structure is proven per delay line. It removed one model's 70k-cycle spike on the model-change block.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 5. Practical numbers
text: The calibrated estimate of clean tracks (about 87 % or less) for 8 tracks of one model: SQUARE 10; ASYM-TRI and 2FM 9; KICK, NOISE and most DX7 banks 8; RINGS, HIHAT and ADDITIVE 7; most others 6; VA 5.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 5. Practical numbers
text: The per-voice cost is 3.5-6.8 % of the DSP. Mixed kits add up per voice. `[emu]` calibrated

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
text: L2 data is cached by a 16 KiB cache that maps lines 16 KiB apart to the same set. Buffers spaced at 16 KiB multiples thrash it, so pad or interleave them. Branches and calls are expensive: unroll small loops into hardware loops, avoid calls in per-sample code, and fill delay slots.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
text: One block measured 666,582 cycles median on DT2 (666,784 on DN2), jittering by ±2.7 % (sd 0.5 %); the emulator does not jitter. With `digikit/remote` and `digikit/debug` loaded, a DN2 showed DSP 57 % average (61 % peak) and ColdFire 26 %.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
text: Registers read on silicon (DT2 and DN2 alike): IMASK `0x8040801b`, MODE2 `0x42000021`, SHDBG_REVID `0x20`, CMMR_SYSCTL `0x6004`, SHL1C_CFG `0x00010101`, SHL1C_CFG2 `0xf0`; two non-cacheable ranges: `0x200fa000-0x200fe000` and `0x28240000-0x283a0000`, with exclusive end addresses. SHL1C_CFG2 `0xf0` enables ranges 2 and 3 with `RRnSEL = 1` (non-cacheable); L2 and DDR outside them are cached ([finding 103, section 4](https://github.com/ElekLabs/digikit/blob/main/docs/findings/103-dsp-facts-on-a-digitakt-ii.md#4-registers-read-on-silicon-d)); the core timer period differs per device (DT2 `0x0025f280`, DN2 `0x00268538`). Float and saturation rules the chip follows (some contradict the PRM):

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
text: A float ALU operation with a NaN input returns `0xFFFFFFFF` with AI set and AN clear. Inf - inf also returns `0xFFFFFFFF`. The float multiplier's invalid result (NaN operand, inf x 0) is `0x7FFFFFFF` with MI set and MN clear.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
text: The sticky bits (AIS, AVS, AUS, AOS) latch on every float ALU operation, so a NaN once produced leaves a mark you can read.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
text: FIX of ±0.5 returns 0 and sets AUS.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
text: With MODE1.ALUSAT, fixed add/sub/neg/abs saturate to `0x7FFFFFFF` / `0x80000000`. The short compute forms (Type 2c), the multifunction ALU halves and the dual add/subtract may still wrap; this is unmeasured.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
text: Reading an MR word into a register keeps the multiplier flags (the PRM says it clears them).

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
text: The RECIPS/RSQRTS seeds come from two 128-entry tables, all measured; the low 15 mantissa bits are zero. Stock's divide helper uses RECIPS plus Newton steps, so the last bit of a division depends on the exact seed. Diagnostic reply publication ([finding 101](https://github.com/ElekLabs/digikit/blob/main/docs/findings/101-module-step-word-on-hardware.md)): the DSP's SPI2 is a slave and its transmit DMA walks two descriptors. Timing of the suspected overlap between DMA and diagnostic writes on silicon remains unmeasured. {digikit-f101}

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
text: On a real DT2 (OS 1.17), digikit's diagnostic word 25 arrived as 0 in 3,995 of 4,000 collected records. The old scheme delivered every second record in the emulator. `[hw]` {digikit-f101}

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
text: Digikit's own `core/fx` and `core/dsp-voice` diagnostic clears overwrote the previous block's reply word. Removing those clears restored delivery in the DN2 1.12 emulator; this does not identify stock firmware as the writer or establish silicon DMA timing. `[emu]` {digikit-f101}

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 6. Measured on silicon: cycles and float rules (digikit findings 101-103, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, 2026-10-31/11-01)
text: Keep hook diagnostics in a static word and copy it into the reply at the block tail, after all module calls. The revised design clears the static word rather than either reply record and passes the emulator regression; finding 101 says it had not yet run on a real DT2. A mark stored in the call that hangs the DSP cannot reach a tail that never runs, so the fault record retains the last completed block's mark. `[emu]` {digikit-f101}

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / What the stock SHARC kernels look like (digikit finding 72, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, static)
text: Calling convention: a delayed `CALL` with a frame; arguments in R4, R8, R12, more on the stack; result in R0. Most kernels come as a pair: `reset(record)` and `process(record, in, out, n)`, one 32-sample block per call. The prologue and epilogue cost ~20 instructions, about 0.6 per sample.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / What the stock SHARC kernels look like (digikit finding 72, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, static)
text: Every sample loop is a hardware `DO ... UNTIL LCE`. The loops are software-pipelined (the last stores come after the loop) and have a fast exit for n = 0 or 1.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / What the stock SHARC kernels look like (digikit finding 72, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, static)
text: Idioms worth copying: multiplier + ALU + data move in one instruction; post-modify DAG access with constant M6 = 1 and M5 = 0; RECIPS/RSQRTS seed plus Newton steps, using FAVG to halve; branch-free CLIP/ABS/MIN/MAX; FEXT to wrap an index; SIMD around copy loops; parameter ramps as "accumulator += step per sample"; MODE1 saved and restored around RND32 or SIMD.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / What the stock SHARC kernels look like (digikit finding 72, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, static)
text: Same code, different address: the shared kernels are byte-identical on DT2 and DN2 but sit at different addresses (biquad DT2 `0x1ccbd8`, DN2 `0xb81368`). Only the float divide `0x1c06ba` has one address on both. Calling a stock kernel therefore needs a per-device address row.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / What the stock SHARC kernels look like (digikit finding 72, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, static)
text: Hidden dependencies of stock kernels: The envelope reads a rate table at a device-specific absolute address. powf reads three tables and writes error words. Divide and rsqrt flip MODE1 bit 16 and restore it, so don't call them with SIMD or a loop active.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / What the stock SHARC kernels look like (digikit finding 72, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, static)
text: The DSP sections are byte-identical between DT2 1.16 and 1.17 and between DN2 1.11 and 1.12 (digikit finding 53), so SHARC code and addresses carried over between those OS versions. `[doc]` {digikit-f53}

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / What the stock SHARC kernels look like (digikit finding 72, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, static)
text: digikit's recommendation: write your own kernels for the hot path; they can be faster (its estimate: interpolated delay 41 -> 15 instructions per sample, half-band 25 -> 10). Call stock only for the divide.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 1. Timing - the numbers that matter
text: The core runs at 1.000 GHz (DSP clock against the host's wall clock: 1000.1 MHz median). A block is 32 samples at 48 kHz = 666,667 cycles, 1,500 blocks/s. Earlier "~650k / ~975 MHz" figures were a unit error (counted in units of 1,024). Guards built on 650k are about 2.5 % too strict. `[hw]` {own-dt2-notes}

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 1. Timing - the numbers that matter
text: Stock load with nothing playing: about 43-49 % (word 0 ~280-320k cycles, idle-task measure 48.6-49 %). `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 1. Timing - the numbers that matter
text: On the Digitakt II, reply word 0 is a true load figure. It tracks an idle-task measure second by second, about 6.5k cycles/block below it (interrupts, RPC, timers outside the frame handler). This differs from the Digitone II, where dn2_firmware_explore found word 0 misreading. Add ~6.5k for the whole DSP. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 1. Timing - the numbers that matter
text: Device cycles are about 2x the emulator's instruction count for this project's own code, which reads samples from DDR. The emulator models no memory stalls. Stock render code is reported at ~9 cycles/instruction on the DN2. A hard stop that the emulator showed overshooting by ~25k overshot by ~75k on the unit. `[hw]` ([I36](../INCIDENTS.md#i36-the-emulator-undercounted-dsp-time-by-2x-to-12x))

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 1. Timing - the numbers that matter
text: Free budget with one plain stock track: about 330k cycles per block (calibration burn builds). `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 2. FreeRTOS on the DT2 SHARC (static, confirmed by a task-switch hook on the unit)
text: Priorities 2-4 and 6 are unused, probably with configMAX_PRIORITIES = 7. A task at priority 2-4 runs only after Audio finishes its block and is preempted by the next one, so it cannot make Audio miss a block. Only work inside Audio, or at priority 6, can. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 2. FreeRTOS on the DT2 SHARC (static, confirmed by a task-switch hook on the unit)
text: Kernel globals: `pxReadyTasksLists` `0x2ca2e8` (20 bytes each), `pxCurrentTCB` `0x2ca3e0`, `uxCurrentNumberOfTasks` `0x2ca3e8`, `uxTopReadyPriority` `0x2ca3f0` (bit mask, `31 - leftz`), `xSchedulerRunning` `0x2ca3f4`, `uxSchedulerSuspended` `0x2ca414`. The TCB is 88 bytes and statically allocated (`xTaskCreateStatic` sw `0xb86014`). Stack overflow check method 2 (`0xa5a5a5a5`). No run-time stats are compiled in. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 2. FreeRTOS on the DT2 SHARC (static, confirmed by a task-switch hook on the unit)
text: `prvIdleTask` is at sw `0xb863ca` with no idle hook; its back edge is at sw `0xb863df`. `vTaskSwitchContext` sw `0xb85af7` stores `pxCurrentTCB` at sw `0xb85b6b`. Both are workable hook points for an idle counter or a task map, at ~250 device cycles per switch (~0.1 %). L2 code loads at byte `0x20000000` (sw `0xb80000`). "Audio" and "RPC" are created from internal-memory code (sw `0x1c3f6a`, `0x1c7775`). `[hw]` (hooks ran on the unit)

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 3. Missed blocks, overload and "bitcrush until reboot" (what the runs showed)
text: A late block is always a whole missed block. Audio is locked to the block interrupt. If one block's work runs past the next interrupt, that interrupt is lost and Audio runs one block later: an exactly one-block dropout, never drift. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 3. Missed blocks, overload and "bitcrush until reboot" (what the runs showed)
text: The stock engine governs its own per-block load. With 8 heavy stock tracks the Audio task ran at 99-100 % for whole 4 s windows and missed no block. Misses happen only when extra code inside the Audio task adds work the stock governor doesn't know about. So a custom engine must stop on a per-block deadline measured from the block start, with margin, not on an average budget. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 3. Missed blocks, overload and "bitcrush until reboot" (what the runs showed)
text: Provoked missed blocks (54 in one boot, three back to back) did NOT cause the sticky bitcrush. Neither did stock overload, nor sample loading at low load. The sticky "everything bitcrushed until reboot" appeared only with several custom-engine tracks at extreme settings. An emulator write audit showed no stray stores, so the cause is still open. Proven causes of a sticky whole-mix bitcrush from earlier builds: a render call much longer than a block with interrupts off; NaN/Inf reaching stock FX feedback; a value routed through a "free" stock parameter slot; overrunning the L2 area. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 3. Missed blocks, overload and "bitcrush until reboot" (what the runs showed)
text: Reading load by sampling word 0 (~17 reads/s = ~1 % of blocks) misses single late blocks. Count late blocks on the DSP side instead (task-switch gaps > 1.25 blocks). `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 4. The ColdFire <-> SHARC reply record
text: The SHARC writes two copies, at DM `0x266220` and `0x267220`. A selector at `0x261ca4` picks the copy being written (`0x266220 + (sel << 12)`), so write both. The ColdFire copies it every frame to `0x8000488C` (2,748 bytes, at most 687 words). The 16-bit halves arrive swapped. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 4. The ColdFire <-> SHARC reply record
text: Word k is at `0x266220 + 4k`, not `+ k`. Two test builds wrote to the wrong place because of this; copy addresses from the compiler's disassembly. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 4. The ColdFire <-> SHARC reply record
text: Which words are free (DT2 1.17, measured): 670-676 arrive untouched. heavylight's engine uses 672-676. Words 1-6 are rewritten by the firmware after the block, so writes there never arrive. Word 5 is the firmware's while a track plays (unlike the DN2). 677-686 are the firmware's. From word 7 on there is a per-track table: 21 words per track at `0x8000488C + 0x1C + 84*track`. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 5. STRETCH machine contract (measured in the emulator, used on the unit)
text: Render `FUN_1c5576 -> FUN_1c5615`, only caller `FUN_1c642a` (selector 2). Replace the body. Do not patch the call at `0x1c6af1`. The stock renderer costs ~1,720 instructions per 32-sample call. `[emu]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 5. STRETCH machine contract (measured in the emulator, used on the unit)
text: Call: R4 = voice record (`0x2412cc + v*0x1d8`, 32 records), R8 = output (32 floats, 48 kHz, int16/32768 scale), R12 = 32. Voices are rendered in ascending order 0..31, so a new block starts when v <= last v. Record words: w00 sample pointer (int16 mono, L = voice 2t, R = 2t+1), w62/63 length, w64/65 loop start, w68/69 end (Q31), w6a/6b step (Q31, 96 kHz units), w6c/6d phase, bytes 0x1b8 active / 0x1b9 stop / 0x1bb reverse / 0x1bc loop, w72 = a (tempo fit, float) and w73 = b (pitch ratio). A trigger is visible as w70 == w71 == 0. +4 is a 96 kHz work buffer and +0x104 is decimator state, not scratch. Tempo is a float BPM at DM `0x252d50`. `[emu]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 5. STRETCH machine contract (measured in the emulator, used on the unit)
text: Stock STRETCH: fixed 2,048-sample grains, 128-sample crossfade, linear interpolation. `a = BPM*(end-start)/(96000*120*2^bars)`, grid speed `clamp(a, 0.125, 4) + P - b`. `[emu]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 5. STRETCH machine contract (measured in the emulator, used on the unit)
text: Knob frame working copy: short at `0x2558dc + 0xde + 0x60*track` (the hidden CFADE slot, 0..0x7f00). Routing a value through this "free" slot also feeds a stock per-voice flag that acts on the delay feedback (`FUN_1c24e9`, slot struct `0x2506ec + v*0xdc + 0x10`). That leaked into the delay and once caused a sticky bitcrush. Check every reused slot with a memory-write diff of the stock chain. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 5. STRETCH machine contract (measured in the emulator, used on the unit)
text: The SHARC upload in MAIN OS checks only `length <= 1 MiB` (no fixed size). Insert new boot blocks before FINAL. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 5b. How a sample reaches a SHARC voice (digikit finding 15, DT2 1.16, emulator)
text: Samples go to the DSP over link port 0 (LP0_CTL `0x30FFE000`; SEC sources 81/82/168), not over the frame link. LP1 is unused. One transfer is 0x401 words: a tag and 1,024 payload words. Tag `0xFFFFFFFF` means a slot header: slot, startL, startR, rate, len. Stereo means startL != startR. A tag below `0x19200` is a page number into the 400 MiB DDR sample pool at `0x8422B9C8`. This is the RPC-task work the owner saw while samples load.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 5b. How a sample reaches a SHARC voice (digikit finding 15, DT2 1.16, emulator)
text: Slot table: 0x14-byte records at DM `0x257810 + slot*0x14` (start L/R relative to the pool, length, ...), at most 0x401 slots.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 5b. How a sample reaches a SHARC voice (digikit finding 15, DT2 1.16, emulator)
text: Track t owns voices 2t and 2t+1, with no dynamic allocation (unlike the DN2). The frame's trig mask is at payload `0x22` (bit t = track t). `[emu]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 6. Memory rules learned the hard way
text: L2: the static analysis says `0x2001ab7c..0x20100000` minus `0x200fa000..0x200fe000` is free, but going past `0x200f5a74` gave clicks and leaks into the delay on the unit. Keep your data at or below that. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 6. Memory rules learned the hard way
text: External DDR: the stock output buffer (`0x8045b3c0`) and the sample data are in DDR. Per-sample stores to the DDR output buffer crashed the unit (continuous tone), although the emulator was bit-identical. Render into L2 and copy once per block. Read int16 samples two at a time. `[hw]` ([I17](../INCIDENTS.md#i17-per-sample-stores-to-the-ddr-output-buffer-crashed-the-unit))

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 6. Memory rules learned the hard way
text: DM and PM data caches are not coherent on DDR (DN2 finding). Don't write through one bus and read through the other. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 6. Memory rules learned the hard way
text: Keep long calls short with interrupts off: a watchdog of at most ~1M cycles per call. Burns of ~1.27M with interrupts off left no lasting harm; longer calls knocked the audio stream out of step for good. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 6. Memory rules learned the hard way
text: Save MODE1 on entry and restore it on exit. A changed MODE1 alters the whole stock DSP until reboot. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 6. Memory rules learned the hard way
text: Never let NaN/Inf/huge values leave the machine: per-sample guard `!(|x| < 1e6)` -> 0 and restart the voice, clip to ±2. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 7. selcc/selas (selache) traps, each seen on the unit or in the emulator
text: `double` is 32-bit float. A read position in float loses resolution from ~22 s into a sample, which sounds like sample-rate reduction. Use Q32.32 fixed point for positions. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 7. selcc/selas (selache) traps, each seen on the unit or in the emulator
text: No integer `/` or `%` where the operand can be 0 (`___umod32` runs LCNTR = 32 - leftz(x); 0 means a hang).

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 7. selcc/selas (selache) traps, each seen on the unit or in the emulator
text: No loops with early exit (`break`/`return`): they become DO loops left by a jump.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 7. selcc/selas (selache) traps, each seen on the unit or in the emulator
text: `int more = a < b; while (more)` compiled into an endless loop. Write a counted `for` with an `if` body.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 7. selcc/selas (selache) traps, each seen on the unit or in the emulator
text: Large initialised `static const float` tables arrive as garbage, so compute them at run time. Complex float expressions passed as arguments lost terms. `static int a = 1, b;` lost `b`. Keep compound conditions simple. Pass at most 3 arguments (stack arguments are passed wrongly) or a struct pointer.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 7. selcc/selas (selache) traps, each seen on the unit or in the emulator
text: selas: multifunction (MUL+ALU) and dual-load forms are encoded wrongly; `Ia = MODIFY(Ib, ..)` becomes `Ib = ..`; system registers (MODE1, LCNTR, EMUCLK) moved in 48-bit form are wrong, so use compressed code. Negative shift immediates are wrong (`023e 0000` vs stock `023e 7800`: ILOPI on the unit). Shift by a register.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 7. selcc/selas (selache) traps, each seen on the unit or in the emulator
text: selcc treats R3, R5-R7 as scratch where the ADI ABI preserves them: save them at the bridge.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 7. selcc/selas (selache) traps, each seen on the unit or in the emulator
text: A selcc peephole bug (frame-reload forwarding clobbering the reload register) was patched locally. The patch also added a `SELCC_SAFE=1` switch that skips the post-allocation peepholes. If code misbehaves only when optimised, try that.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 7. selcc/selas (selache) traps, each seen on the unit or in the emulator
text: DAG registers moved via the same DAG's addressing hang the unit; move them through R registers. Same rule as the DN2 skill.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 8. Measuring on the unit without a debugger
text: Read-only USB SysEx probe in MAIN OS (heavylight's dt2-keyframer, derived from irpina/digihealth via dn2_firmware_explore): `F0 00 20 3C 7D 00 <pack7> F7`. Commands: HELLO 1 (returns word 0) and PEEK 3 (address, up to 256 bytes). There is no write command. It hooks the SysEx router at `0x40120006` (router `0x4011ffda`, header `0x4021e5d2`, send `0x40121d2a`, USB port 2), and the router itself drops device id 0x7D. It fits in 532 bytes of a free 896-byte run in MAIN OS 1.17 (`0x402e4f64`, `0x402e609c`) and coexists with Deja Vu V5.1, Musical V4 and Zoom V11. It also went into an elekloader-built image. It is built with plain binutils (`m68k-linux-gnu-as -mcpu=5475`). Overbridge suspected of conflicting: keep the probe build separate. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 8. Measuring on the unit without a debugger
text: Telemetry as audio: a DSP track outputs one constant level per block (frame of 47 blocks with sync levels), recorded via an Overbridge track output. Overbridge applies a DC-blocking highpass (one pole, a = 0.9981 at 48 kHz) that the decoder must undo. About 50 % of frames decode. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 8. Measuring on the unit without a debugger
text: Load display build: show peak cycles per call on the playhead. This is the only figure that includes real DDR stalls without a probe.

section: Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 8. Measuring on the unit without a debugger
text: Recovery used throughout: FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4, stock `.syx` over DIN. Bootstrap 0x0201 is the same on 1.16 and 1.17, so the 1.16 <-> 1.17 update is reversible. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II / Hardware test evidence for the mods
text: digikit's flash rungs on a real DT2 1.17 (finding 47, 2026-10-18/19): each step was flashed through SETTINGS > SYSTEM > OS UPGRADE with Transfer and logged over USB SysEx. `[hw]` {digikit-f47} Rung A, the runtime in section 3 only, booted with a DIGIKIT menu. Rung B added the DSP link and voice hook (sections 3 and 7) and played stock audio. Rung C, a machine loaded at run time (pluck, 4,484 B uploaded over SysEx), halted the SHARC at the first trig. Breadcrumbs narrowed it to the step after the type match. The fix (C3d2) was to route 17 DAG-register stores through an R register, the same-DAG rule. With it, pluck played at ~1,500 dispatches/s with DSP load 41.5 -> 42 %.

section: Digitakt II / Hardware test evidence for the mods
text: A second SHARC stop on a real DT2: `fx/freqshift` on the send route froze the unit at boot; the emulator showed nothing (findings 77, 91). Two causes were found. `[hw]` {digikit-f91} ([I15](../INCIDENTS.md#i15-a-frequency-shifter-froze-the-unit-at-boot)) A selas defect left the end of a nested hardware loop compressed (VISA). The last 11 instructions of every hardware loop must be 48-bit ISA, so wrap nested loops in `.NOCOMPRESS` ([rule A45](../AGENT-RULES.md)). Code copied into L2 at run time was not written back from the data cache. After both fixes, freqshift ran on the send and master routes (2026-10-30).

section: Digitakt II / ColdFire facts from digitakt-ii-research's research notes (DT2 **1.16**, emulator)
text: LFO tick `0x40139342` (caller `0x4002e912`): Parameter rows relative to A3: SPD -6, MULT -4, FADE -2, DEST 0, WAVE +2, SPH +4, MODE +6, DEP +8. WAVE is clamped to 0-6 at `0x401393c6`. WAVE 0-5 dispatch through a 6-entry table at `0x4022231c`; WAVE 6 is RAND. The table cannot be extended by appending: the RAND slew data sits right after it. The shared RNG is `(A,B) -> (B, A+B)` at `0x402b62c8/cc`. The phase increment is in D5 (signed); the stored phase is in D2. Raw WAVE 7/8 clamp to 6 and play RAND on stock. This is why Deja Vu needs two paired hooks, not one dispatch hook. `[emu]`

section: Digitakt II / ColdFire facts from digitakt-ii-research's research notes (DT2 **1.16**, emulator)
text: Firmware heap: `malloc` at `0x4011e674` (size at `4(A7)`, pointer in D0, mutex `0x44e08654`), `free` at `0x4011e87a` (it checks bounds and 16-byte alignment with `illegal`). The heap is a 32 MiB buddy heap `0x44f39c40-0x46f39c40` with metadata at `0x402b406c`. It sits inside the reset clear and initialises on first call. An 8 KiB block allocated once stayed untouched for 10 M emulated instructions. `[emu]`

section: Digitakt II / ColdFire facts from digitakt-ii-research's research notes (DT2 **1.16**, emulator)
text: A persistent flashed cave `0x403117c4-0x40312000` (2,108 B) ends exactly at the reset clear and survives boot. `0x4031be59-0x4031ff60` is inside the clear and cannot hold flashed code. The priority-6 task entry `0x40133646` is a candidate one-shot startup hook, after the heap is initialised. `[emu]` Deja Vu, the All-in-One, dt2-machine-lab and 70b185's private project all use it; who holds which bytes: [memory-maps.md](../common/memory-maps.md); one freeze report: [CONFLICTS O18](../CONFLICTS.md).
