section: Digitakt II / Architecture map from static analysis and simulation (lalzart, OS 1.15C)
text: SHARC part: ADSP-21569. Section 7 holds ADSP-2156x loader/application records (104 records mapped). FreeRTOS, an Audio task and a recurring block loop are traced. The hand-off from the boot kernel to that startup is not.

section: Digitakt II / Architecture map from static analysis and simulation (lalzart, OS 1.15C)
text: The ColdFire <-> SHARC frame is the same shape as on the Digitone II: A full-duplex `0xabc`-byte DSPI2 frame carries a `0x802`-byte state payload: 16 records of `0x60` bytes, track n to SHARC unit n. ColdFire eDMA29 sends and eDMA28 receives; the SHARC uses SPI2 with completed-image double buffering. The send is driven from a level-5 interrupt that a level-6 eDMA-completion path forces in software. Link settings: SPI mode 1, 16-bit MSB-first, one `0x55e`-word window. The meaning of the SHARC-to-ColdFire return content is open. Compare the DN2's frame and reply words in [digitone-2-internals.md](digitone-2-internals.md). This is a second, independent reading of the shared design (research map T19).

section: Digitakt II / Architecture map from static analysis and simulation (lalzart, OS 1.15C)
text: Project samples reach the SHARC over a different path: ColdFire Rapid-GPIO byte/strobe/ready endpoint -> SHARC link port 0 (LP0_RX, DMA30). Samples are described by five-word resource descriptors with 4 KiB pages. This agrees with digikit finding 15 ([digitakt-2-sharc-measured.md](digitakt-2-sharc-measured.md)). The physical bridge between the two endpoints is not identified.

section: Digitakt II / Architecture map from static analysis and simulation (lalzart, OS 1.15C)
text: Audio output: two 64-word banks are selected, then sent by a two-bank circular DMA descriptor (DMA10) to SPORT4 half A. Codec and pin are not identified.

section: Digitakt II / Architecture map from static analysis and simulation (lalzart, OS 1.15C)
text: Update path: MAIN validates checksum, minimum version and the cryptographic trailer before it erases and programs the staged ELE3 slot at flash `0x80000`, then requests a reset. Which updater copy runs after reset, and whether recovery is independent of it, is marked opaque.

section: Digitakt II / Architecture map from static analysis and simulation (lalzart, OS 1.15C)
text: Offline modifications proven in the simulator only: a byte-exact selector reroute, and a 3-byte change that turns an output-bank negation into pass-through. Re-encoding a modified section and running it on hardware are explicitly unproven.

section: Digitakt II / What happens on a ColdFire fault (digikit finding 37, DT2 1.16/1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12, static, checked by a second agent) `[doc]`
text: The main OS's default exception handler prints `EXCEPTION ...` with the vector, format, PC and twelve stack words, then executes `halt` with interrupts masked. It never returns.

section: Digitakt II / What happens on a ColdFire fault (digikit finding 37, DT2 1.16/1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12, static, checked by a second agent) `[doc]`
text: The core watchdog is not used anywhere in the main OS, so a fault hangs the whole device until the power is cycled. Messages like the DT2's `V04 M0 P40311A64` (dt2-machine-lab) are this handler's output.

section: Digitakt II / What happens on a ColdFire fault (digikit finding 37, DT2 1.16/1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12, static, checked by a second agent) `[doc]`
text: digikit's runtime counts bad boots: the counter is raised at boot start and cleared only after 30 s of stable running. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
text: The intro is its own task, priority 7, created once by the installer before the main-OS task (DT2 `0x400d1448`, DN2 1.12 `0x400d3920`) and woken by a PIT3 tick. A higher number is more urgent here, so the intro preempts the main-OS task (priority 6). A frame callback that never returns starves the main OS until power-off.

section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
text: Five scene tables at `0x402a1b64`, `0x402a1b74`, `0x402a1b84`, `0x402a1b94`, `0x402a1ba4`. Each boot picks one with an LCG; the first is picked about 99.9 % of the time and has 175 frames. An entry is `{callback, frame count}`, ended by a 0.

section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
text: One pointer drives it: the current entry is at DT2 `0x43153a00`, DN2 1.12 `0x42c4cacc`, DN2 1.11 `0x42c4bacc`. Only the setup function (DT2 `0x400d1832`, DN2 1.12 `0x400d3d0a`) and the tick function (DT2 `0x400d18f0`, DN2 1.12 `0x400d3dc8`) touch it. Each frame calls `callback(index, count, bitmap)`; count 0 ends the intro the normal way: the pointer is cleared, PIT3 stops and semaphore `0x43149550` releases the main-OS task.

section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
text: Swapping the intro: a hook before the setup function's argument load (`move.l (0x24,SP),D0; movea.l D0,A0`, DT2 `0x400d183a`, DN2 1.12 `0x400d3d12`, DN2 1.11 `0x400d3bae`, the same 6 bytes on all three) can point it at an own table. In digikit's emulator the UI was then reached after 115 audio blocks instead of 5,973 (DT2) and 6,180 (DN2). Stock's frame clear is `0x40113700` (DN2 1.12 `0x40115074`, DN2 1.11 `0x40114d94`), called as `(bitmap, 0, 1)`. `[emu]`

section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
text: Frame rate unresolved: digikit's timer model gives 30 Hz (175 frames = 5.8 s); its earlier emulator notes derived 15 Hz. Open conflict [O20](../CONFLICTS.md). Module code first runs at about frame 53-57 of the intro (emulator); almost all of that delay is stock setup.

section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
text: Faults during the intro reach stock's halting handler (see the section above): digikit installs its own crash handler only from the UI loop.

section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
text: Frame layout on the panel (measured on one DT2 1.17): with y = 0 at the top, the intro bitmap holds pixel (x, y) at byte `8*x + (63-y)/8`, bit `7 - (63-y)%8`, flipped vertically only. digikit's emulator shows these frames the other way up. `[hw]` ([I53](../INCIDENTS.md#i53-boot-screen-frames-were-upright-in-the-emulator-and-flipped-on-the-panel))

section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
text: Safe mode is digikit's, not stock's: REC (key `0x13`, state byte 2 bit 2; key state array at DT2 `0x44dc8644`, DN2 `0x445a2e30`) held from power-on skips all modules. On one DT2 1.17 it worked, and a custom boot screen started about 1.8 s after the stock intro. `[hw]` ([I54](../INCIDENTS.md#i54-safe-mode-by-rec-at-power-on-tested-on-a-digitakt-ii))

section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
text: With the black intro patch set, the bootstrap's logo, "B" and the OS version stay until the main OS first writes the display, then about 1-2 s of black, then the boot screen. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II / Memory map for samples and voices (dt2-machine-lab, OS 1.16, static plus emulator)
text: ColdFire heap: a 32 MiB buddy allocator at `0x44f39c40-0x46f39c40` (16-byte minimum, power-of-two blocks), parameters at `0x402b406c`.

section: Digitakt II / Memory map for samples and voices (dt2-machine-lab, OS 1.16, static plus emulator)
text: Allocating from the stock heap at startup (digitakt-ii-research, OS 1.16, emulator, byte-verified sites) {dt2-research-heap}: `malloc` is at `0x4011e674` (size at `4(A7)`, pointer in D0, mutex at `0x44e08654`, lazy init on first call). `free` is at `0x4011e87a`. It traps with `illegal` on a pointer outside the heap or not 16-byte aligned, the same rule as the Digitakt mk1's operator delete. The OS clears `0x40312000-0x47e28470` at reset, so static data placed there does not survive boot. A startup hook at `0x40133646` (`link.w` + `movem`) made exactly one 8 KiB allocation that stayed untouched for 20 M instructions. This is the cleanest way to own memory without a cave.

section: Digitakt II / Memory map for samples and voices (dt2-machine-lab, OS 1.16, static plus emulator)
text: Sample pool: Logical range `0x400-0x19000400`, 400 MiB, allocations rounded to 8 KiB. The ColdFire's allocation records decide admission; no SHARC malloc is involved. In the SHARC's view the pool is a window at DSP byte address `0x8422b9c8 + (offset - 0x400)`, ending at `0x9d22b9c8`. Capicola reserves the top 8 MiB.

section: Digitakt II / Memory map for samples and voices (dt2-machine-lab, OS 1.16, static plus emulator)
text: Recorder: the main OS fetches recorder data in chunks of at most `0x800` bytes over DSPI1 from a service whose physical owner (ColdFire, SHARC DDR or a third part) is not established. Staging buffers are at `0x4fe79340` / `0x4fe7a340`.

section: Digitakt II / Memory map for samples and voices (dt2-machine-lab, OS 1.16, static plus emulator)
text: SHARC side: Sample-slot table at `0x257810 + slot*0x14`: 1,025 entries, slot `0x400` is the preview. Voices at `0x2412cc + lane*0x1d8`, 32 lanes: `+0` PCM pointer, `+0x188` length, `+0x1b8` active. Link-port 0 receive staging at `0x268220` (descriptor) and `0x268240` (a tag plus 4 KiB of payload).

section: Digitakt II / Memory map for samples and voices (dt2-machine-lab, OS 1.16, static plus emulator)
text: Once published to the SHARC, PCM keeps playing after the ColdFire source is freed, as long as the stock allocation stays owned. Saving, however, needs the source, and no read-back path from sample memory was found.

section: Digitakt II / Three Digitakt II mod routes side by side (T21, 2026-11-02)
text: digikit's patchkit (used by digitakt-ii-research's All-in-One and dt2-machine-lab), elekloader's core-dt2 (used by digitakt2-perform) and the hand-placed builds share the flash cave `0x403117c4-0x40312000`. elekloader's RAM `0x47f00000-0x47f40000` lies inside digikit's `cf.expansion` `0x47e8b000-0x47fe0000`. Full table of ranges and hook sites: [memory-maps.md](../common/memory-maps.md). `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / Three Digitakt II mod routes side by side (T21, 2026-11-02)
text: A decoded section 7 over 1 MiB crashed a unit (dt2-machine-lab, OS 1.16): [firmware-container.md](../common/firmware-container.md), rule A46. `[hw]` {dt2-lab-capicola} ([I16](../INCIDENTS.md#i16-a-decoded-section-7-over-1-mib-crashed-the-unit))

section: Digitakt II / Sound parameters, overdrive and run-time machines (digikit, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12, 2026-11-10)
text: Reading a track's Sound parameter words needs no fixed address: get the project singleton, its ProjectSettings at project + `0x30` (static analysis only), the selected track from `view_track` (clamped 0-15), then `native_track_sound(active kit, track)` = kit + `0x6c` + `0x3c0` x track; vtable slot `0x28` of that Sound object returns the record pointer `*(sound + 0x10)` (0 when none is bound), and word i is a big-endian s16 at record + `0x14` + 2i. Anchors: settings `0x40041d18` (DT2 1.17) / `0x4003e40e` (DN2 1.12); `native_track_sound` `0x40035cca` / `0x40030e66`. The array holds 71 words on the DT2 and 101 on the DN2. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / Sound parameters, overdrive and run-time machines (digikit, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12, 2026-11-10)
text: On the DN2 a track's Sound record can sit at an odd address (kit stride `0x48b`), so read it byte by byte. A parameter code maps to its array index through the descriptor table (rows of `0x3c` bytes, index as s32 at row + 4, -1 = no word); the same index means another parameter on another machine. P-locks, sound lock, LFO and MIDI CC writes go through other paths, and a latched parameter of a run-time machine changed no word in the array (where it is stored is open). `[doc]`/`[emu]`

section: Digitakt II / Sound parameters, overdrive and run-time machines (digikit, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12, 2026-11-10)
text: Track overdrive (stock): the curve clamps to +-1 and applies y*(2-|y|) three times; the blend is x + mix*(y-x) with stock ramps for drive and mix. OVR Routing is parameter `0x103` (Sound mirror index 68; 0 = pre, `0x100` = post). The per-track stage is called twice per track from the voice chain. `[doc]` {digikit-overdrive}

section: Digitakt II / Sound parameters, overdrive and run-time machines (digikit, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12, 2026-11-10)
text: Run-time machines: on the DT2 they can use knob slots B C E F G H; a parameter on the seventh slot replaces LEV, whose level is then fixed at 100. The run-time module stage is limited to 64 KB; a TB-303 port costs about 8,000 SHARC instructions per 32-sample block. `[doc]` {digikit-tb303}

section: Digitakt II / Sound parameters, overdrive and run-time machines (digikit, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12, 2026-11-10)
text: ColdFire jump targets must be even: a jsr/jmp to an odd address faults with an address error on the unit while the emulator runs on; a byte-aligned mod section froze a DT2 at boot (I61). `[hw]` {elekloader-oddjump}

section: Digitakt II / Sound parameters, overdrive and run-time machines (digikit, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12, 2026-11-10)
text: Modwerk's DT2 base: a combined image booted on a DT2 (OS 1.17, 2026-11-08) and restored saved module kit data after a project reload. Its audio scheduler (grid callbacks and phrase replacement at the stock audio submission call `0x400d82f8`) is a proposal checked only in digikit fixtures. `[hw]` / `[emu]` {modwerk-dt2-base}

section: Digitakt II / +Drive file writes from mod code (digikit finding 120, DT2 1.17)
text: The firmware's own file calls can write samples: open (`0x40158902`, mode "w"), write (`0x4015866a`), reserve, hash (`0x4015b3aa`), close (`0x401588c0`), info, delete (`0x40157078`), mkdir and rename (`0x40156f6c`, which keeps the inode, size and stored hash). Each takes the recursive filesystem mutex itself and blocks, so call them from a task, never an interrupt. The sampler's recorder `0x40153c70` is a complete stock caller. `[doc]` (static)

section: Digitakt II / +Drive file writes from mod code (digikit finding 120, DT2 1.17)
text: Open does not truncate: an existing file opens at position 0 with its old size and data; stock deletes first. Whole 32 KiB pages at multiples of `0x8000` are written straight from the buffer, the rest goes through the page cache. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / +Drive file writes from mod code (digikit finding 120, DT2 1.17)
text: The 16-byte trailer: files carry 16 zero bytes after the data, and the stored hash covers them; the C calls do not add them (the recorder and stock's MidiRpc close do), so a writer adds them before the hash. File info reports size minus 16. `[emu]` (card read back on the emulator) Elekloader's Rytm loader meets the same 16 bytes as a header at the start of each file on the Analog Rytm MKII ([analog-rytm.md](analog-rytm.md)).

section: Digitakt II / +Drive file writes from mod code (digikit finding 120, DT2 1.17)
text: Power cut: a cut mid-write leaves a visible file with a partial size and no hash; the mount was not seen to repair it. Delete refuses an open file (open-file bitmap at `0x46f4ded0`). Only `/factory` is RAM-backed; user files always go to the card, and a failed card write is not reported. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / +Drive file writes from mod code (digikit finding 120, DT2 1.17)
text: On a unit (2026-11-11) digikit's bulk uploads through these calls left only complete files after a pulled cable, and the stock sample browser did not list the staging folder `/.dkstage`. `[hw]` {digikit-usbfast}

section: Digitakt II / Project and kit storage (digikit finding 121, DT2 1.17)
text: In RAM: the project object is at `0x41776c9c`; 128 patterns from `0x41776cb8` (stride `0x1db8c`), 128 kits from `0x426532b8` (stride `0x5574`). Serializer `0x400df66c` (flag bits pick the parts), loader `0x400df95a`. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / Project and kit storage (digikit finding 121, DT2 1.17)
text: Bytes the serializer never writes: pattern record `0x15acc-0x15c00`, kit record `0x573e-0x5800`, file header `0x1c-0x200`. Pattern RAM `+0x1cef0..0x1db60` is not saved but is in use: pokes there hung the UI. `[doc]` (the hang `[hw]`)

section: Digitakt II / UI surfaces for mods (digikit finding 122, DT2 1.17)
text: Pointer returns: the firmware returns pointers in d0, while GCC's m68k ABI reads them from a0; a C prototype returning a pointer froze the UI. Declare such routines as returning a 32-bit integer. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II / UI surfaces for mods (digikit finding 122, DT2 1.17)
text: Sites: encoder filter `0x40111cda`; per-frame value block `0x80005b50`; modulator call site `0x4002e90c`; LED frame `0x4003117c`, LED setter `0x400308e0`; NameView wrapper `0x40117c70`. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / UI surfaces for mods (digikit finding 122, DT2 1.17)
text: LED colour byte: on a unit `0x31` looked deep blue and `0x41` yellow (one observer, by eye); this disagrees with digikit's own finding 19 (CONFLICTS O25). `[hw]` `[?]`

section: Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
text: USB mode switch: `FUN_40006c16` has the same address and bytes on DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12. It takes no lock and cuts a MIDI reply in flight; USB restarts after a 30-tick counter (about 1 s in the emulator; counter DT2 `0x40965a38`, DN2 `0x4058f280`). The stored USB CONFIG byte (0 MIDI, 1 Overbridge, 2 AUDIO/MIDI; DT2 `0x4099d5c4`, DN2 `0x405ce898`) is written only by the menu actions (DT2 `0x4010331a`/`30`/`48`, DN2 `0x40104dc2`/`d8`/`f0`), never by the switch, so a reboot returns to the stored mode; an Overbridge disconnect (`FUN_400f2ce0`) is the only path that re-applies it by itself. DT2 connection-state word `0x40965a40`. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
text: Take-over on units (2026-11-11): digikit's Fast USB switched both units from USB AUDIO/MIDI to USB MIDI in RAM for an upload over its bulk interface and back (SysEx TAKEOVER `0x1e`, RELEASE `0x1f`); the stored mode byte stayed unchanged and USB audio was heard working afterwards. The project's plan and finding still say "hardware test open", so this rests on the hardware handover alone. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
text: +Drive internals: close hash `0x4015b1e8` under the filesystem mutex `0x46f4deb0` (recursive lock `0x400015a0`, unlock `0x400016d2`); inode get/put/write `0x4015b92a`/`0x4015b846`/`0x4015b868`; extent lookup `0x4015813c`; hash-table rebuild `0x4015b0ee` (about 300 ms per file on a unit); event post `0x4015a6aa`. Data page 0 is card sector `0x5ee180` (page p at base + p x `0x40`), the first hash page sector `0x5ee980`. Every file write reaches the card before the call returns. The eSDHC read/write is clamped to 64 KiB (DT2 `0x4012e3c4`, DN2 `0x4012ca8a`). `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
text: Measured ceilings (8 MiB, 2026-11-11): DT2 +Drive file write 2.6 MB/s with 64 KiB calls, 7.8 MB/s with 256 KiB, 10.3 MB/s with 1 MiB; the firmware's close-hash re-read 4.2 MB/s; store writes DT2 about 7.2 MB/s, DN2 6.3 MB/s; raw card reads 15.3 MB/s on both; CPU hash 16-18.7 MB/s. A whole 8 MB upload: DT2 2.99-6.15 s (varies a lot between runs), DN2 1.75 s. Per file about 0.18-0.19 s fixed cost. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
text: Fast close: digikit hashes from a card read-back and then runs the firmware's own close steps, byte-identical to the stock close, falling back to the firmware close if the read-back fails. After such uploads the stock browser listed the files, a sample loaded and played, and a project that referenced an uploaded sample reloaded and played it. Creating the staging folder `/.dkstage` cost about 420 ms and removing a file from it about 150 ms, so it now stays for the session. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
text: SHARC cycle counter: each image has exactly one EMUCLK reader, the block handler (DT2 `0x1c74cd`, DN2 `0x1c9d6b`), which keeps a low-word delta for reporting only; nothing branches on it. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
text: eMMC EXT_CSD copy in RAM: DT2 1.17 `0x4fe69100`, DN2 1.12 `0x4e6f9100`; bytes are reversed within each 32-bit word because the eSDHC runs little-endian. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / MIDI notes from whiplash (DT2, OS 1.17 manual, 2026-11)
text: NRPN numbers disagree between the OS 1.17 manual and midi.guide's data for track mute and level, pattern mute, master overdrive, filter env depth, filter base/width and portamento; all CCs agree (CONFLICTS O24). `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / MIDI notes from whiplash (DT2, OS 1.17 manual, 2026-11)
text: CC 80 (amp HOLD) at 127 switches HOLD to NOTE; it is not the longest hold. A sound ends on note-off only with AMP MODE = ADSR or HOLD = NOTE. Note 60 plays a sample at its own pitch only with TUNE 64 and the preset OCTAVE unchanged. No CC or NRPN selects the machine type. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / MIDI notes from whiplash (DT2, OS 1.17 manual, 2026-11)
text: CC 19 selects the sample slot from the project pool; it switched slots audibly on a unit (2026-11-11). MIDI Start also starts the unit's own sequencer, so the selected pattern's trigs play on top of an external part. `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II / MIDI notes from whiplash (DT2, OS 1.17 manual, 2026-11)
text: USB audio: class-compliant audio exists only in USB AUDIO/MIDI mode, with one stereo USB OUT pair; track outputs over USB carry no effects; INT TO MAIN = AUTO mutes the internal outs while USB audio streams. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt (mk1) / Where the audio runs (Digiwerk prior-art survey, 2026-10)
text: The Digitakt mk1 renders all its audio on the ColdFire itself, in the render interrupt (vector 191). It has no DSP chip. New machines and filters (DigiFilter, digistring, digisophie, digineighbor, digislicer) are ColdFire C built with `m68k-elf-gcc -mcpu=54455`, hooked in the render ISR through elekloader. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt (mk1) / Where the audio runs (Digiwerk prior-art survey, 2026-10)
text: Measuring load the digihealth way: read DMA timer 0's counter (`DTCN0`, `0xFC07000C`) at render entry and exit, and add the idle task's time at the RTOS context switch (`0x40000438` on DT mk1). `[doc]`

section: Digitakt (mk1) / Memory and code placement (core 2.x, elekloader)
text: Budget shared by all mods (ADAPTING.md, core 2.x era): 128 KB for `.run` + `.bss`, 2304 bytes of fast SRAM (`.fast`). Newer cores differ: elekloader kit 0.6.0 gives 4.0 cores a 256 KB Digitakt area, DEVICES.md lists `core_ddr` at `0x47BC0000-0x47C00000` (256 KB) for Digitakt mk1 - see [`../common/memory-maps.md`](../common/memory-maps.md). `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting} {elekloader-devices}

section: Digitakt (mk1) / Memory and code placement (core 2.x, elekloader)
text: Main OS ends at `0x4025CA40` (1.53); an appended blob runs there (`__run_start`, `__bss_end`, `__fast_start`, `__fast_len`). `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}

section: Digitakt (mk1) / Memory and code placement (core 2.x, elekloader)
text: FAST AUDIO copies the render block `0x400716c0-0x4007629a` to SRAM; hook sites inside it must be absolute, not PC-relative. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}

section: Digitakt (mk1) / Memory and code placement (core 2.x, elekloader)
text: Relocations supported: 32-bit absolute, 32/16-bit PC-relative; 16-bit absolute is refused. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}

section: Digitakt (mk1) / Memory and code placement (core 2.x, elekloader)
text: Core-owned hook sites (1.53): `0x40000538, 0x4000a770, 0x4000a7d6, 0x4000b770, 0x4000b7ba, 0x40058800, 0x40077428, 0x400784c8`; core 2.1 owns about 30 more (listed in `mods/core/mod.json` of elekloader). Never patch them, subscribe to events. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}

section: Digitakt (mk1) / Render path, injection point and key tables (digigrain's platform skills, OS 1.53, Ghidra plus digiemu)
Digitakt (mk1) / Render path, injection point and key tables (digigrain's platform skills, OS 1.53, Ghidra plus digiemu)
text: The cleanest place to add a machine: each voice's mono block at `0x80001a18 + 128*v` (32 x int32, Q31). Anything written there before the per-voice processing step gets the stock filter, amp, pan, level, mute and effects for free, and resampling records it too. Bit reduction acts *inside* the stock voice synth, before that point. `[emu]`

section: Digitakt (mk1) / Render path, injection point and key tables (digigrain's platform skills, OS 1.53, Ghidra plus digiemu)
text: Samples: table at `0x403193a0`, 16 bytes per slot `{PCM ptr, ?, length, ratio Q30}`, valid slots 0..130 (`0x82` is the audition slot); PCM is s16 mono. A voice advances its position by 32 x the pitch ratio per block. `[emu]`

section: Digitakt (mk1) / Render path, injection point and key tables (digigrain's platform skills, OS 1.53, Ghidra plus digiemu)

text: Recorder (static reading, not yet run in an emulator; digigrain's recorder skill): the record buffer holds 1,584,000 frames (33.0 s at 48 kHz mono) as two planes written together, the top 16 bits at `0x4237DF90 + 2n` and bits 8-15 at `0x421FB410 + n`, so the reassembled sample is 24-bit. The source selector fills a mono capture block at `0x800032c4`; sources 9-16 (TRK1-8) are a straight copy of the voice block `0x80001a18 + 128*(t-1)`, so a machine that writes the voice block can be resampled for free. Sample slot `0x82` is the recorder's preview slot; a sample-table setter at `0x400763b4` fills a slot and, below `0x80`, its 255-entry slice table. `[doc]` {digigrain-skills}

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / DSP code room and load on the DN2 (Digiwerk DT01, DC01/DC02, SC01)
text: Their safety lesson: stock code never puts a load into an I register directly before a 48-bit instruction that uses it (0 of ~14 cases; there is always work in between). The SHARC emulator does not model the pipeline, so the cautious pass refuses that pairing. Copy the rule: do not create instruction pairings the stock code never has. `[doc]`

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / DSP code room and load on the DN2 (Digiwerk DT01, DC01/DC02, SC01)
text: Where DSP code may live, after the probe study (Digiwerk PB01 findings, static, 2026-10-23) {dn2-cfw-pb01}: L1 block 1 above `0x2e4f46` gives about 12 KB, not the 45 KB of the static map, because the build keeps the edge for a 32 KB DM cache. Block 3's tail is the 16 KB I-cache. `0x315f8c-0x318000` in block 2 depends on whether the PM cache there is 16 or 32 KB. Code placed there stopped the DSP on a unit (CMP2's LOW MUP stop), so builds refuse it. L2 candidates: `0x2008823c-0x200918c0` (38,532 B) and `0x200c2000-0x200fa000` (229,376 B). `0x200918c0-0x200c2000` is kept free of data by the build. Other projects use part of that range on units: [CONFLICTS O19](../CONFLICTS.md). Section 7 can grow ~150 KB before its 1 MiB limit. `[doc]`

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
text: Frame: 0xa80 bytes from `0x80005e60`, sent by DSPI2 (16-bit DMA, 1,374 halfwords); the reply arrives at `0x800053a4`, every block (1,500/s). All send-FX, compressor, external-input and master parameters are one block of big-endian words at `0x9fa + 2*(k-25)` (`k` = the parameter row's mirror index; chorus is k 25-31). Compressor routing is at `0xd4` (track bits) and `0xd6`. 16 per-voice rows of `0x92` bytes start at `0xda`. A row is a voice, not a track: a track parameter goes to every row whose owner (`0xa5a + 2r`) is that track. `[emu]`

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
text: Audio clock: SSI0 with eDMA 48 (RX) / 50 (TX), 96,000 requests/s. One major loop is one 32-sample block, and vector 170 forces vector 191 (the frame handler). The emulator needs this clock for PLAY to run the sequencer. `[emu]`

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
text: Panel and MIDI: Panel MCU on UART8 at 156,250 baud, sent through eDMA 35. LED messages: `B9 i v` (LED i, palette entry v) and `B5 i r g b` (palette entry); see also [`../common/sysex-and-midi.md`](../common/sysex-and-midi.md). DIN MIDI on UART9 at 31,250 baud: out by eDMA 37 (bulk) plus direct writes for realtime bytes, in by eDMA 36. `[emu]`

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
text: Notes: MIDI tracks have no voice limit in the output engine; the "4 notes" are only the UI's NOT2-NOT4 rows. A pattern's note pool holds 8,192 notes, with at most 16 notes per step. The MIDI note-output length is a byte counter over a 1,024-byte buffer. Stock 1.12 plays more than 4 notes per trig from a modded project. `[doc]`

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
text: DSP free memory (static): L1 block 2 is never written by the stream (128 KB), the L1 block 1 tail `0x2dd52c-0x2effff`, and L2 from `0x2008823c`. Correction: the startup turns on all three L1 caches, so `0x39c000-0x39ffff`, `0x2ec000-0x2effff` and `0x31c000-0x31ffff` are cache, not free. dnfw's proven code area is `0x2dd600-0x2e7000`. `[doc]`

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
text: The frame is longer than its data (elekloader core-dn2 0.3). The driver sends a 0xabc-byte frame but writes data halfwords only for the first 0xa80 bytes; for the rest it writes only command halfwords. So the tail from byte 0xa80 keeps whatever you write there before the call, and stock leaves it zero and ignores it on the DSP side. The driver's transmit queue is at `0x80002510` (one 32-bit entry per frame halfword, command half first); the frame sender calls the driver at `0x40025e9e`. The DSP reads tail word k as halfword 2k+1 above halfword 2k. `[hw]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2}

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
text: Reply word 2 (record offset 8) is free on DN2 1.12: no stock code writes or reads it. elekloader's DSP peek uses it (one halfword per block, ~3 KB/s), and so do digikit's `core/dsp-link` and the `sharc` branch's metrics core, so only one of them can be in a build. `[hw]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2}

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
text: DSP load on a unit (DN2 1.12, elekloader's idle-task meter, Nov 2026): 666,706 cycles per block measured (the nominal figure is 666,667). Time outside FreeRTOS's idle task: about 80 % with nothing playing, 65 % with 64 notes held. Stock's own block-handler span (reply word 0) shows the same pattern (79 % and 68 %). Neither figure is headroom. Stock's audio task holds the DSP for most of each block and holds it *less* under load, so the share counts waiting. Do not read "80 % busy at idle" as "20 % left". `[hw]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2}

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
text: elekloader DN2 machine budget (core-dn2 0.3, experimental): each SHARC machine kind gets 64 KiB of L2 and its own guarded 4 KiB L1 stack. The callback may declare at most 2,048 stack bytes; the rest is shared with interrupts. The peek reads only L1 blocks 0-3 below their caches and L2 below the special window. On a unit, it read the machine stacks' guard words and its own code back exactly. `[hw]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2} {elekloader-adapting}

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Image identity
text: MAIN OS = section id 3 of the ELE3 container; load address `0x40000400` on Digitone II and Digitone mk1; big-endian; 16-byte header, first instruction `46 FC 27 00` (`MOVE #$2700,SR`) at `0x40000410`. section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Hardware map and budgets (OS 1.12 unless noted)
text: The in-place loader is the hidden size limit. Section 4's loader (`0x8000357c`, stage `0x40200000`) has a stock margin of +31,182 bytes; elektron-firmware-tool's default compression level (`-l 3`) gives -39,318 and corrupts the image. Every build needs a margin >= 0 at both loader stages; elekloader's default packer produced a container too large for the receive buffer, so the DN2 build uses a dense packer (`codec/dense.py`). Stock Digitakt II 1.17 also fails the in-place path (margin -31,912). `[hw]` {dn2-cfw-handoff} ([I39](../INCIDENTS.md#i39-the-default-compression-level-corrupted-a-dn2-image))

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / ColdFire / MIDI side findings
text: The 4-note MIDI limit is code only (NOTE/NOT2-NOT4 rows, `FUN_40055606`, a 4-byte default chord, 4-note SHAPE chords); the engine and pattern format are not limited; the note pool is 8,192 six-byte entries. Traps: the lock-clear path writes -1 to notes 1-4; the 8-bit MIDI output counter at `0x44600ca0` can wrap on large note-off bursts and leave notes stuck. The arp is kept off MIDI tracks by structure (not fully confirmed). `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-handoff}

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / +Drive and storage (digikit findings 14, 23-24, 35, 43-47)

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / More from dnfw's notes (read 2026-11-02)
text: The SHARC's filter accelerators, read on a DN2 (accelprobe, 2026-10-17). The ADSP-21569 has IIR0 and FIR0; the DN2 1.11 engine uses neither. Only 22 of 76 result words matched the models built from the hardware reference; the chip differs in three ways: IIR0 feeds stored word 5 of a biquad into the output: y = A0 x + s1, then s1 = (A1 x + s2) + B1 y and s2 = A2 x + B2 y, each step rounded to float32 (all 40 outputs and 4 states match). FIR0 adds its four partial sums in pairs, (acc0 + acc1) + (acc2 + acc3). In ACM mode the chip writes `0xFFFFFFFF` to a TCB's INIDX and 0 to OUTIDX after a window, the other way round from the hardware reference. Speed bounds, including setup: at most about 22 cycles per biquad-sample and 4.5 per tap-sample. ADI's application note gives the theoretical rates as 6 cycles per biquad (one MAC unit) and about 0.25 cycles per tap and sample (four MAC units), and says the coefficient and state preload dominates small jobs, which fits these bounds from jobs of 8-16 samples {adi-ee408}. The INIDX/OUTIDX write-back in ACM is not described there. digikit's models were corrected to match all 76 words. Same silicon on the DT2 ([crosscheck](../common/dt2-dn2-sharc-crosscheck.md)). `[hw]` {dn2-accel}

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / More from dnfw's notes (read 2026-11-02)
text: ColdFire tasks on a unit (DN2 1.11, read with the USB probe): The context switch is at `0x40000410-0x40000458`; the ready table at `0x4664ac9c` holds one list head per priority; higher numbers run first. Prio 0 never runs; prio 1 is the real idle loop (entry `0x400cec98`, parked at `0x400cf0e2`); the MIDI task (prio 7) answers the probe. Stack high-water marks after a busy pattern and a save: the fullest is a 2,048-byte prio-10 stack at 27 %; the main application's 160 KiB stack peaked at 1.5 %. Interrupts run on the current task's stack. ColdFire CPU 58-61 % whatever plays, almost all of it the audio ISR; a pattern raises the ISR's worst frame (75-83 % in a busy one), and SAVE PROJECT takes 100 % for about a second. `[hw]` {dn2-cftasks}

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / More from dnfw's notes (read 2026-11-02)
text: Stock 1.11 trusts a stored song row count. The song LOAD (`0x400dea6a`) copies `count` stored 29-byte rows into 37-byte live rows without checking it. One project held 21,503 instead of at most 99 and crashed stock and modded builds alike when opened; the damage had entered between two exports. A mod that writes project data must keep every count in range, and a repair tool must use the storage-version-4 offsets (row count at record `+0x147`). `[hw]` {dn2-oldproject} ([I2](../INCIDENTS.md#i2-stock-song-load-trusts-a-stored-row-count))

text: Reference disassembler: `m68k-linux-gnu-objdump` 2.42, `-m m68k:cfv4e -z`; objdump prints indexed-mode displacements in hex without `0x` and `d16(An)` displacements in decimal - confirm against raw bytes. Padding `0x0000` words appear as clusters. Bootstrap needs `--adjust-vma=0x800003fc`. `[doc]` {dn2-mainos-image} {dn2-cfw-handoff}

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Disassembly pitfalls (agents will hit these)
text: Capstone has no ColdFire mode: 98.95 % of boundaries right over `0x40001000` + 64 KB with 201 divergences (it assigns two bytes to each failed instruction and desyncs; it decodes `00 00 2f 0a` as `ori.b`, which ColdFire removed). Stock Ghidra `68000:BE:32:Coldfire` reached 99.76 % over 512 KB but lacks `movclr.l ACCy,Rx` (flow stops at words `a1c0 a3c1 a5c2 a7c3`, so decompilations of the frame ISR and modulation module may be truncated) and gets MSAC-with-load wrong (accumulator selection inverted). digikit's `68000:BE:32:ColdfireEMAC` module fixes this - re-import rather than switching language on an existing program. Auto-analysis of the 3.19 MB 1.11 MAIN OS takes about 128 s; close the Ghidra GUI before headless runs; some large switches report "Could not recover jumptable" and must be read as assembly. `[doc]` {dn2-mainos-image}

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 findings v0.45-v0.48 (OS 1.11, 2026-11-11)
text: Front-panel LEDs: the LED driver `0x40132148(id, value)` remembers the last value per LED and sends only changes; `LedManager` (pointer `0x446478e0`) is the only route to it, and on each refresh (`0x4002c854`) the first write to an LED wins. Trig keys are logical LED ids 26-41. The palette is uploaded in three sets (one per LED INTENSITY): index 0 off, 1 backlight white, then eight hues of 16 levels each (red 2-17, green 18-33, blue 34-49, yellow 50-65, cyan 66-81, magenta 82-97, white 98-113, orange 114-129), 130-135 special. Modes: 1 unlit, 2 steady, 3 and 4 blink. `[doc]` (read from disassembly) {dn2mk2-leds}

The TRK SETUP PLAY MODE and MONO NOTE PRIO setters are `0x4004b6d6` and `0x4004b786`. `[doc]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2} {elekloader-machines-dn2}

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 findings v0.45-v0.48 (OS 1.11, 2026-11-11)
text: Coupled emulator (v0.48): dn2mk2 now runs the ColdFire image (digikit's emulator) and the SHARC image together, one audio block of 32 frames at a time: the audio interrupt once per block, the sequencer timer at its exact rate but up to one block late in phase, one ColdFire packet per block to the DSP and the DSP's status one block later. Its own audit calls this faithful in order and content, not in timing: an interrupt never lands mid-UI code, a DSP overrun is not modelled, and the default "fast" mode runs the UI's 60 Hz tick about 90x too often (the "faithful" mode gets 59 of 60 ticks a second). The unit's ColdFire spends about 56 % in the audio interrupt with the sequencer stopped. `[emu]` {dn2mk2-v048} (I66)

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / USB transfer speed on the units (digikit, 2026-11-11)
text: The SysEx route is CPU-bound. On a Digitone II (OS 1.12, high-speed USB) the firmware's receive chain in the deferred-call task (priority 9) takes at most 0.857 MB/s of SysEx bytes even when nothing handles the message; digikit's store reaches 0.60 MB/s of payload, two requests in flight gain nothing, and its card VERIFY runs at 7.4 MB/s. Receive work and MIDI-task work do not overlap. About 53 M instructions a second are left free. `[hw]` {digikit-usbfast}

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / USB transfer speed on the units (digikit, 2026-11-11)
text: A vendor bulk interface fits beside USB MIDI. In USB MIDI mode the port uses EP0 and EP1 only, so a patched configuration descriptor can add an interface with a bulk pair on EP2; in USB AUDIO/MIDI mode EP2 and EP3 are taken (audio and its clock feedback), and the controller has only EP0-EP3. Stock serves the configuration from a pointer in its port table, so a copy in free flash space needs no code change. `[hw]` (enumerated on macOS) {digikit-usbfast} {digikit-f42}

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / USB transfer speed on the units (digikit, 2026-11-11)
text: Program IN endpoints for 64-byte packets. The controller's transmit buffer is 64 bytes per endpoint: two 512-byte IN packets back to back wedged it until a power cycle (I70). Stock declares bulk 512 but programs its IN queue heads for 64. `[hw]` {digikit-usbfast}

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / USB transfer speed on the units (digikit, 2026-11-11)
text: Measured over the bulk route (64-byte IN packets): echo about 2.3 MB/s each way on a DN2 and 2.9 MB/s on a DT2; an 8 MB sample 3.86 MB/s on the DN2 (0.68 over SysEx), 0.94-1.60 MB/s with verify on the DT2 (0.11 over SysEx); for many small files the per-file overhead dominates. A cable pulled mid-file left only complete files. On the DT2 a sample loaded on a track keeps playing while its file is replaced, since it plays from sample RAM. `[hw]` {digikit-usbfast}

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 v0.49 FLEX (OS 1.11, 2026-11-11)
text: FLEX replaces BOUNCE (machine type 17, BOUNCE's, so older projects open their BOUNCE track as FLEX with no conversion code). Recorder trigs record a track, IN or MAIN into one of 8 buffers for R.LEN steps; the FLEX track plays the take. BOUNCE had two faults FLEX fixes: its engine read three sound slots the panel never wrote, so a take ignored its panel, and it waited for a +Drive pool directory that a unit with nothing ever sent to the +Drive never has, so every take was refused there. `[emu]` (gated; not verified on hardware)

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / OS release history (dn2-cfw `notes/dn2-release-history.md`, dnfw `docs/os-versions.md`)
text: Porting: 1.11 and 1.12 MAIN images share only their first 28 bytes; about 48.7 % of 48-byte windows from 1.11 appear verbatim in 1.12 but at 535 different offset shifts - fixed-address patches do not port; locate hook points by masked byte patterns (`find`/`expect` fields) and pin every mod to its build by hash. Units already at bootstrap 0x0201 will not be upgraded again. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-release-history} {dn2-os-versions}

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / OS release history (dn2-cfw `notes/dn2-release-history.md`, dnfw `docs/os-versions.md`)
text: Rules for a new OS version (dnfw): compare decoded content (`dnfw diff`), never compressed bytes; use `--strings` as a filter only; read the densest change blocks first (a relink gives many small blocks, a rewrite one large one); check bootstrap and updater separately (the updater matters for recovery); re-locate every patch via `find`/`expect` and name the target build; examine unfamiliar sections (id 8) before relying on the image; mangled storage-struct names show which persisted state changed. The compression and signing scheme was unchanged in 1.11 and the codec limits were measured on 1.11. `[doc]` {dn2-os-versions}

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Bootstrap and the recovery path (dnfw `docs/bootstrap.md`, 1.10E image)
text: Section 2 is 30,302 bytes; header `[u32 payload_size = 0x7656][u32 0x80010000]` (the second word is not the load base); load base `0x800003fc` incl. the 8-byte header, payload runs at `0x80000404`; status strings READY TO RECEIVE `0x80006603`, RECEIVING... `0x80006614`, UPGRADING... `0x800065e6`, "BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE" at payload offset `0x602c`. `[doc]` {dn2-bootstrap}

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Bootstrap and the recovery path (dnfw `docs/bootstrap.md`, 1.10E image)
text: Receive phase: start marker `0x7F` (kind 1) records the total packet count and starting sequence number; data packets `0x7E` are sequence-checked, their checksum verified over 119 bytes and 101 decoded bytes copied to the buffer; end marker (kind 2) verifies totals. The progress bar measures reception only (`received * 128 / total`). A bad sequence number or checksum sets the state to 0 and the transfer silently stops - no retransmit. Transport is one-way DIN MIDI at 31,250 baud. `[doc]` {dn2-bootstrap}

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Bootstrap and the recovery path (dnfw `docs/bootstrap.md`, 1.10E image)
text: Write phase: the receive buffer is RAM at `0x40000000` holding `[u32 size][u32 checksum][container]`; the container check sums `(word_index ^ word)` over `size/4` words from `0x40000008`; flash is erased in 256 KB blocks from `0x80000` and the raw container is written in 512-byte chunks. No decompression happens here - the updater and MAIN OS decompress sections on the next boot (which is why the in-place loader margin matters). The page does not mention any seal/signature verification in this path. A different routine (`FUN_80011844`) flashes a single small section with a CRC (residue `0xDEBB20E3`) and 64 KB caps - not the recovery path. `[doc]` {dn2-bootstrap}

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Arpeggiator vs MIDI tracks (dn2-cfw `notes/T2.2-arp-midi-v2.md`, OS 1.12, static analysis only)
text: The arp is part of the voice interrupt; its only output is the internal voice allocator `FUN_4002a6a2`, nothing on that path creates a MIDI event. Barriers: UI gating by `FUN_40031274` (isMidiTrack) at the ARP key `0x4005f9b6`, menu auto-close `0x400187ea`, LED `0x40060dde`; the step handler `FUN_400d99de` sends MIDI tracks to `FUN_400d8cbe`; live keys on a MIDI track go straight to the MIDI task via `FUN_4012bb90`. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-arp}

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Arpeggiator vs MIDI tracks (dn2-cfw `notes/T2.2-arp-midi-v2.md`, OS 1.12, static analysis only)
text: Data: arp settings per track sound record at `kit+0x34+t*0x48b` (`+0x15f` mode, `+0x160` speed, `+0x161` range, `+0x162` note length, `+0x164` step mask, `+0x166..0x175` offsets); track MIDI mask s16 at `kit+0x5cda`; events are 0x6c bytes (alloc `FUN_40138cb6`, schedule `FUN_40138e3c`), MIDI events 0x60 bytes, MIDI task queue `0x445ff870`, free list head `0x4460f4b8` (2,048 entries), MIDI output byte count `0x44600ca0` (8-bit). The arp self-tick is a type-9 event every 90,000 units (1/60 step); one interrupt pass is ~0.67 ms. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-arp}

section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Arpeggiator vs MIDI tracks (dn2-cfw `notes/T2.2-arp-midi-v2.md`, OS 1.12, static analysis only)
text: Hazards for any MIDI-generating mod: the event allocator `FUN_4012a6e8` does not check for an empty free list (test `0x4460f4b8` first); MIDI events take the untransposed note (the task transposes); source byte `[0xd]` 1 = sequencer (subject to mute/solo), 2 = live; length `0x7f` (INF) hangs notes in the MIDI task; the 8-bit output count wraps above 255 bytes per message; latency ~one pass plus DIN serialisation (~0.96 ms per 3-byte note); vector 191 (voice interrupt) is not modelled by the emulator by default. Design options range from UI-only (~0 bytes) to sequenced trigs with p-locks (~850 bytes). `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-arp}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / SHARC address map of the boot stream (digikit `docs/SHARC-ADDRESS-MAP.md`, from dn2_firmware_explore, DN2 1.11)
text: `load = exec * 2 + 0x28000000`. Code addresses count 16-bit parcels (VISA), and the entry `0x001c12e2` lands exactly on a loaded region; all 591 of 591 `0x1c`-space jump targets fit. The `0xb8` space (1,025 targets) needs the other mapping (L2 code at `0x20000000`, see the firmware map). `[doc]` {digikit-sharcmap}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / SHARC address map of the boot stream (digikit `docs/SHARC-ADDRESS-MAP.md`, from dn2_firmware_explore, DN2 1.11)
text: Regions (DN2 1.11, section 7 836,956 B): L2 `0x20000000-0x2001e880` code (125 KB), `0x2001e888-0x2008823c` data; L1 `0x282403f0-0x2826f000` and `0x282c0000-0x282dd52c` rodata, `0x283825c4-0x2839bffc` code (105 KB); DDR `0x80000018-0x8052fbe0` 5.4 MB, almost all fill. About 240 KB of the 837 KB section is code. `[doc]`

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / SHARC address map of the boot stream (digikit `docs/SHARC-ADDRESS-MAP.md`, from dn2_firmware_explore, DN2 1.11)

These addresses never appear as plain 32-bit words; a word scan finds nothing. You need a SHARC disassembler. `[doc]`

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / A. Adding machines (elekloader machines-dn2, OS 1.12 only)
text: Added SHARC synths appear in the native FUNC+SYN selector and added filters in the FLTR category. Synth menu order: stock synths, then added synths by ID, then MIDI; filters: stock filters, then added filters by ID. `[doc]` {elekloader-machines-dn2}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / A. Adding machines (elekloader machines-dn2, OS 1.12 only)
text: Each added synth shows the stock OS a host type of FM TONE, each filter a host type of LOWPASS 4; the companion sets the host and a mod cannot choose it. A synth inherits FM TONE's track permissions, parameter ownership and MIDI numbers; a filter inherits LOWPASS 4's FLTR page, defaults and parameters. Identity reads, saving and the audio frame keep the custom ID, so the mod's own kernel runs. `[doc]` {elekloader-machines-dn2}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / A. Adding machines (elekloader machines-dn2, OS 1.12 only)
text: IDs: synth IDs 5-31, filter IDs 6-31, separate namespaces, permanent; the linker rejects conflicts even if a mod omits a resource claim; there is no global ID allocator, authors must agree manually. Unused IDs never enter the cached list. `[doc]` {elekloader-machines-dn2}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / A. Adding machines (elekloader machines-dn2, OS 1.12 only)
text: Missing mods: with the companion installed, a saved synth whose mod is absent keeps its ID, shows as MISSING and is omitted from the selector; its DSP type maps to MIDI (silence) and its CC/NRPN do nothing. Without the companion, stock OS clamps an unknown saved type to FM TONE on load. `[doc]` {elekloader-machines-dn2}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / A. Adding machines (elekloader machines-dn2, OS 1.12 only)
text: Parameter pages: synth pages add rows after the stock 321 entries. At boot the companion copies the table at `0x401f83a4` to RAM, repoints its 56 references and raises its 54 row bounds by 41 (adds 40 synth knobs plus a filter's G); the sound-load bound accepts IDs through 31. Other addresses: owner map for note-on `0x40288306 + 0x14*v`, value-class accessor `0x400c257c`, CC/NRPN lookups `0x400dc978` / `0x400dca5a`, FLTR knob lookups `0x4006efcc` / `0x4006f004`. The audio frame is indexed by allocated voice slot, not by track. `[doc]` {elekloader-machines-dn2}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / B. Linking DSP code (elekloader sharc-dn2, OS 1.12)
text: One mod can run code on the DSP at the master output; a build contains either selectable machines or one master-output mod, not both. DSP = ADSP-21569, SHARC+ VISA instructions; silicon stepping not observed. The writer replaces one stock instruction (the profile's single hook) with a call into a bridge; the bridge occupies a fixed range; mod code sits in L2 starting at PC16 `0xbc8000`; mod data uses byte addresses. `[doc]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / B. Linking DSP code (elekloader sharc-dn2, OS 1.12)
text: Section 7: 602,076 bytes stored, 836,956 decoded, 95 boot records forming two boot images; later loads overwrite earlier ones in order; the writer keeps record order and bytes except for the one hook and bookkeeping for added records. With no SHARC mod, section 7 stays stock. `[doc]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / B. Linking DSP code (elekloader sharc-dn2, OS 1.12)
text: Regions (half-open, loader byte addresses): bridge and state `[0x282dd600,0x282dda00)`, bridge pitch table and padding `[0x282dda00,0x282dde00)`, mod (L2) `[0x20090000,0x20098000)`, replaced stock instruction `[0x2838489a,0x283848a0)`, excluded from new code/data `[0x200fa000,0x20100000)`. The mod's 32 KiB splits 16 KiB code + 16 KiB data in the examples; the last 64 bytes of code are a NOP guard (16,320 bytes of instructions). Stack is separate: bridge declares 116 bytes, a mod may declare up to 428 (544 total). `[doc]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / B. Linking DSP code (elekloader sharc-dn2, OS 1.12)
text: Addressing: L1 loader address = core byte address + `0x28000000`; PC16 addresses count two-byte parcels (the stock hook at PC16 `0x1c244d` is loader byte `0x2838489a`); the stock data pointer `0x268438` maps to loader byte `0x28268438`; the last stock byte loaded into L2 is `0x2008823c`. An address that exists, or that maps onto another, is not thereby free. `[doc]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / B. Linking DSP code (elekloader sharc-dn2, OS 1.12)
text: Machine callbacks run on their own stacks (elekloader machines-dn2): synth `0x2de000-0x2df000`, filter `0x2df000-0x2e0000`, 4 KiB each in L1. A callback may declare at most 2,048 bytes; the rest is for interrupts, because an interrupt taken during the call, and a FreeRTOS context switch's 516-byte register save (partly through the PM bus), push onto the running stack. A guard word at each stack's base is checked before and after every call; once broken, the machine is no longer called and its slots play silence. `[doc]` {elekloader-machines-dn2-voice}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / B. Linking DSP code (elekloader sharc-dn2, OS 1.12)
text: Writing B7 also loads I7. To switch stacks, write B7 first, then I7 and L7 = 0 (linear), with interrupts off for those instructions, and restore stock's I7, B7 and L7 afterwards. `[doc]` {elekloader-machines-dn2-voice}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / B. Linking DSP code (elekloader sharc-dn2, OS 1.12)
text: Stock constants to keep: M6 = 1, M7 = -1, M13 = 0, M14 = 1 and both stacks in stock's circular configuration; the master-output bridge saves R0-R8, PX, I4, I5, I12, L4, L5 and the ASTAT/STKY pairs, and everything else is the mod's to preserve (MODE1, MODE2, IMASK, cache configuration, the hardware PC, loop and status stacks). The same constants appear in the DT2/DN2 voice code ([`../common/dt2-dn2-limits-and-audio-chain.md`](../common/dt2-dn2-limits-and-audio-chain.md)). `[doc]` {elekloader-sharc-abi}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / B. Linking DSP code (elekloader sharc-dn2, OS 1.12)
text: A 64-byte NOP guard ends every code segment of a mod: the VISA alignment buffer and fetches in flight can run past the last instruction (SHARC+ programming reference 1.5, sections 4-5, 4-6). elekloader states it as a conservative rule, not a proof. `[doc]` {elekloader-sharc-abi}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / B. Linking DSP code (elekloader sharc-dn2, OS 1.12)
text: Size limits, each checked separately: section 7 stored `0x100000`, decoded `0xfffff`, update including its 8-byte preamble `0x200000`, flash up to `0x380000` with the container starting at `0x80000`. The section 7 limits come from the stock sender's staging buffers; the update limit is a cautious figure measured over USB, not a proven buffer size. None concern mod RAM or stack. `[doc]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / B. Linking DSP code (elekloader sharc-dn2, OS 1.12)
text: Tests in the suite: SHA-256 of the OS 1.12 SysEx and of section 7 (stored and decoded) pinned in the Python and TypeScript profiles; boot record structure; a no-change write reproduces the stock file; the stock sender's 828 bytes at `0x400cf4b0` hashed against a published analysis; the writer checks packing, the seal, flash bounds and that the main OS unpacks in place safely. `[doc]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / B. Linking DSP code (elekloader sharc-dn2, OS 1.12)
text: Evidence ladder in that doc: static analysis found no direct access, data reference or resolved pointer range touching the mod's 32 KiB (2,979 pointer rows resolved, 192 unknown, of 25,878 indirect accesses - not a complete proof); an emulator canary kept unmodified stock intact over 44 checkpoints and 5,136 DSP blocks and detected a deliberate corruption (cannot see same-value writes, reads, or writes undone before the next checkpoint, nothing about the real cache); C and assembly builds gave identical 99,904-frame captures; on hardware (USB, one unit) sine variants ran, an L2 variant ran ten minutes over notes 36-84 (392 note/release pairs), pattern/page/send/project-load checks were limited. Not established: program safety, DAC behaviour, heavy-project stress, real cache and interrupt behaviour, total DSP load, cycle margin. `[hw]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / C. dn2mk2 sampler and +Drive layout (OS 1.11; most numbers are version-specific, v0.13-v0.31)
text: Samples travel over USB as SysEx (`dn2samples.py`: hello, send, save, load, forget, lib-send/list/delete/info; Elektron Transfer must be closed). They are written first to a mirror in ColdFire RAM, then fed to the DSP over a TDM "fast link" at about 0.7 MB/s (about 124 words per packet, 1,500 packets/s). Frames are sent first and the directory last so no slot points at missing audio; each 64 KB chunk loaded into the DSP is checked with a VERIFY sum and resent on failure. `[doc]` {dn2mk2-sampler}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / C. dn2mk2 sampler and +Drive layout (OS 1.11; most numbers are version-specific, v0.13-v0.31)
text: +Drive regions: pool image from sector `0x600000` (3 GiB) with a header sector (`DN2P` in v0.15, `DN2Q` in v0.16) holding length and checksum - the stock storage code does not use anything above 2,224 MiB; library from sector `0x700000` to the end of the device (~20 GB) with a superblock (`DN2L`), an index of 2,048 64-byte entries and up to 64 folders; each library sample is checked with adler-32 before its index entry is written. `[doc]` {dn2mk2-sampler}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / C. dn2mk2 sampler and +Drive layout (OS 1.11; most numbers are version-specific, v0.13-v0.31)
text: A DSP command handler that reads fields of every command can be set by the wrong one (dn2mk2 v0.39, 2026-11-03): the DSP recorder took words 2-4 of every new link command as its source, channel and threshold. When v0.38 started sending a check command at each take's start, every recording kept 96 frames of its source and then the empty input. Fix: only the recorder's own commands (ARM, NOW, STOP, MONITOR, ARM_PLAY) set those fields. `[hw]` {dn2mk2-v039}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / C. dn2mk2 sampler and +Drive layout (OS 1.11; most numbers are version-specific, v0.13-v0.31)
text: The DSP plays a pool slot only below the directory's count (dn2mk2 v0.38, 2026-11-02). Since v0.33 a live add or a recording went into the first empty slot, which is past the count in a pool without gaps, and only a whole-directory load (power-on, project load) carried the count; so new samples stayed silent until a restart. Fix: update the count with every live entry. Per-project sample lists now sit at +Drive `0x6D0000-0x6E02FF` (two checked copies each), Direct Jump's state at `0x6FF000`. `[hw]` {dn2mk2-v038}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / C. dn2mk2 sampler and +Drive layout (OS 1.11; most numbers are version-specific, v0.13-v0.31)
text: DSP RAM pool: base at DSP address `0x84000000` in the 512 MB DDR; directory magic `SMP1` (count + 128 entries of address, frames, rate, spare) then the frames. A power-on RAM check (`CMD_PROBE`) fills and reads back 256 KB blocks at 143 MB and 256 MB+; if it fails or gets no answer within 4 s the pool stays at 128 MB. Pool sizes by version: 5 MB (v0.14-v0.15), 128 MB (v0.16: 96 MB samples + 32 MB recordings), 400 MB (v0.22+: 0..96 MB and 128..400 MB samples, 32 MB between for recordings, no more than ~5.5 min of recordings). Up to 122 user slots (SAMP 1..122), 124..127 for the recorder. `[doc]` {dn2mk2-sampler}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / C. dn2mk2 sampler and +Drive layout (OS 1.11; most numbers are version-specific, v0.13-v0.31)
text: Formats: inputs 8/16/24/32-bit PCM or 32-bit float at any rate, mono or stereo; stored as int16 frames in the pool (the doc is inconsistent - an older section says float32); each sample plays at its own rate; recordings 48 kHz int16, peaks between 64 and 32,700 are normalised to 32,700. Slices (max 64): from cue points, `grid:N`, onsets or none; stored with the sample (format word bits 8..15 = count) or, for slices made on the instrument, in a 768-byte area in the last 128 KB of the recordings area (bit 16 marks it). `[doc]` {dn2mk2-sampler}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / C. dn2mk2 sampler and +Drive layout (OS 1.11; most numbers are version-specific, v0.13-v0.31)
text: Power-on: the RAM check runs first; the pool loads whole in 64 KB chunks; from v0.31 the samples used by the current kit load first and the waveform shows LOADING n%; about 30 s for 20 MB. `[doc]` {dn2mk2-sampler}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / D. dn2mk2 emulator notes (digikit via patched Unicorn)
text: Models enough to boot the control processor, render the panel and take input; storage is not served (eSDHC/eMMC identification only, CMD18 returns zeros). Boot ladder snapshots at 60M/120M/200M/280M/400M instructions; on 1.11 only the 400M rung draws frames. DMA timer 3 at 30 Hz and PIT2 are required or the main task blocks forever. Cold boot plays no notes, turns no encoders, loads no project - emulator zeros cannot refute a crash diagnosis. `[doc]` {dn2mk2-emulator}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / D. dn2mk2 emulator notes (digikit via patched Unicorn)
text: 1.11 section sizes: bootstrap 30,302 bytes (dest `0x02010000`), updater 32,768, blob 836,956, section 8 159,948, meta 15; main application task priority 6, entry `0x4002e688` (on 1.10E). Panel: 55 buttons and 10 encoders; code = channel*8 + bit + 1 for buttons, channel + 1 for encoders; channel 6 is non-linear (code 0x00 is shared by (6,2) and (6,3)); the wire carries a whole-channel state mask and the firmware XORs it against the last state to detect edges; 1024-byte framebuffers flushed by `panel_diff`. `[doc]` {dn2mk2-emulator}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / E. Field incidents reported by dn2mk2 users (lessons for any DSP/voice work)
text: DSP time overruns cut all audio until power cycle. Every voice that does not rest costs time. Dynamic voice allocation spawns voices faster than old ones die away, so eight tracks can need far more than eight voices; locking each track to one voice avoids it. A guard (v0.27) silences voices that do not fit and a CPU indicator shows when it fires. `[hw]` {dn2mk2-reports}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / E. Field incidents reported by dn2mk2 users (lessons for any DSP/voice work)
text: A removed table silenced everything: AMD read a sine table that a later version had removed, so it read uninitialised DSP memory; fixed with a unit test that every table is loaded (v0.30.1/v0.31). `[hw]` {dn2mk2-reports}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / E. Field incidents reported by dn2mk2 users (lessons for any DSP/voice work)
text: A guard that wipes with the wrong register (R0 used as loop counter wrote counts instead of zeros) left voices that went non-finite silent until power-on (v0.33 report; fix planned). Non-finite values (inf/NaN) from engine parameter sweeps (e.g. VO-6 at some CONS/CLEN values) are the likely root; the output guard hides them. `[hw]` {dn2mk2-reports}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / E. Field incidents reported by dn2mk2 users (lessons for any DSP/voice work)

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / E. Field incidents reported by dn2mk2 users (lessons for any DSP/voice work)
text: Stock behaviour users expect to be mirrored: FUNC+turn jumps values to set positions (NOTE by octaves, LFO DEPTH to -128/0/127.98, SPEED to fixed steps; slices count from C1, not C0). Stock mute only drops a muted track's *new* trigs on the ColdFire, so custom voices get no note but sounding notes end via note-off through the stock AMP. `[hw]` {dn2mk2-reports}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / E. Field incidents reported by dn2mk2 users (lessons for any DSP/voice work)
text: After an install MD and Monomachine tracks went silent until the track was cleared (intermittent, suspected stale voice-slot state or state carried from an older version's project) - always test an old project after an install. A YES on the OS-update prompt could open the app's own pop-up instead of the update question (keys must be routed to stock questions). `[hw]` {dn2mk2-reports} ([I21](../INCIDENTS.md#i21-md-and-monomachine-tracks-went-silent-after-an-install))

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / E. Field incidents reported by dn2mk2 users (lessons for any DSP/voice work)
text: Custom pages must hand YES/NO back to stock's own questions. With a custom machine page open, the OS's "update?" question (OS sent over USB) and the stock sound preview (TRIG + YES) opened the mod's pop-up or lock menu instead, so the update could not be accepted. Fix: when a stock question or pop-up is up (found in the screen's view list), its keys go to stock. `[hw]` {dn2mk2-reports}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / E. Field incidents reported by dn2mk2 users (lessons for any DSP/voice work)
text: DDR holds garbage, including NaN, until written. Delay lines in DDR are zeroed at power-on. `[doc]` {dn2mk2-dsptime}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / E. Field incidents reported by dn2mk2 users (lessons for any DSP/voice work)
text: A deadline that follows the stock tail (dn2mk2 v0.32): instead of a fixed 0.6 of the frame, each frame measures how long stock's work after the custom voices takes, holds its peak (easing over ~3 s), and sets the limit to min(0.6 P, max(P - tail - P/8, P/4)). Without a reading it stays at 0.6 P. Voices left out are counted, and the newest note always plays. `[emu]` (stress-tested at 3x slower clock) {dn2mk2-dsptime}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / E. Field incidents reported by dn2mk2 users (lessons for any DSP/voice work)
text: Cost estimate per voice (dn2mk2 v0.33, SHARC runner): instructions + 4 x L2 accesses + 10 x DDR accesses, against 666,667 cycles. The dearest voice (a DigiPRO double-draw) estimates at ~16 % of the frame; most Machinedrum voices at 3-5 %. Moving voice state from DDR to L2 `0x200A0000-0x200A8000` (a range other mods proved on units) was their largest expected saving. The unit's meter is the measure; the estimate only ranks. `[emu]` {dn2mk2-dspcost}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / E. Field incidents reported by dn2mk2 users (lessons for any DSP/voice work)
text: Process: dn2mk2 forked dnfw at commit `8c40698` (2026-10-01), enforces the safety preflight inside `dnfw mods apply`, tightened its DSP limit to the uploader's actual check, runs `scripts/ship_gate.py` on the exact file of every build, and its `CLAUDE.md` requires the ship gate on every build. Versions v0.4-v0.7 were withdrawn for exceeding the 2 MiB USB limit; v0.17 turned PERC into the Machinedrum (25 machines), v0.18 added the Digitakt II sample engine, v0.19 SLICE. `[doc]` {dn2mk2-changes} {dn2mk2-firmware-md}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / Reading a DSP stop, and what the silicon enforces (dnfw, DN2 1.11)
text: Which traps are armed: startup enables only ILOPI (illegal opcode, bit 4) and PARI (L1 parity, bit 3) besides the RTOS timer and software interrupts. FP-exception interrupts (FIXI, FLTOI, FLTUI, FLTII) are not enabled: a NaN in TRUNC/FIX sets only a sticky flag. `[doc]`

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / Reading a DSP stop, and what the silicon enforces (dnfw, DN2 1.11)
text: EMUI, PARI and ILOPI record an error code and return address (DN2 1.11 at DM `0x26ef88-0x26ef94`: `0x507` EMUI, `0x502` PARI, `0x501` ILOPI), then jump to `idle; jump .` inside the handler, forever. `[doc]`

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / Reading a DSP stop, and what the silicon enforces (dnfw, DN2 1.11)
text: How to tell a stop from the sound `[hw]` (inferred from the handler, matching every failed build): Silence (or a buzz from replayed pages) means a trap. The core sits in a high-priority handler, so the audio service can no longer run. A stuck tone (the output DMA replaying its last two pages, ~750 Hz) means a task-level stall, such as an endless loop, while the audio interrupt still runs. In both cases the ColdFire and UI keep running.

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / Reading a DSP stop, and what the silicon enforces (dnfw, DN2 1.11)
text: ILOPI is what toolchains miss: an encoding that selas emits and every decoder accepts, but the chip rejects. Examples are negative shift immediates and selas's 48-bit `Rn = <sysreg>` (Type 5a), which put the wrong source code for every register from PC up, so `R0 = EMUCLK` became `R0 = LCNTR`. Use the compressed forms. `[hw]` {dn2-stall} ([I27](../INCIDENTS.md#i27-an-encoding-every-decoder-accepts-raised-ilopi-on-the-chip))

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / Reading a DSP stop, and what the silicon enforces (dnfw, DN2 1.11)
text: L1 block 2 is not free just because the image leaves it empty: the PM data cache lives in L1 block 2 (and the I-cache in block 3), sized at boot by `SHL1C_CFG`. Code ending exactly at the last written word lets the sequencer prefetch never-written L1, which can raise a parity trap. Keep written memory after your last instruction. `[hw]` {dn2-dspstop}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / Reading a DSP stop, and what the silicon enforces (dnfw, DN2 1.11)
text: DSP DDR on the DN2: 512 MB, and `0x80531000-0xa0000000` (~507 MB) is free. This was measured on the instrument by filling that range with a pattern at boot and scanning it during heavy playback, pattern/kit changes, FX extremes and a save; nothing wrote there. Stock uses the first ~5.2 MB. `[hw]` {dn2-ddr}

section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / Reading a DSP stop, and what the silicon enforces (dnfw, DN2 1.11)
text: DN2 stock load from the idle task: ~63-65 % flat, whatever plays. The frame handler's own count (word 0) is ~416k cycles, and a held voice adds only ~8k: the engine renders every voice every frame. Bursts of +40-49 % of a frame come every 15-30 s (more with note starts), also on stock WaveTone. No frame was missed. `[hw]` {dn2-sharcload}

section: Digitone II OS 1.11 - function and data map (from the digitone-2-modding-skill sources) / The static checks, exactly (from `hwrules.py`, `encodecheck.py`, `shapecheck.py`)
text: LOOP-ISA: last 11 instructions of a hardware loop (all of a short loop) must be legacy 48-bit ISA - stock 1.11 obeys it in all 286 loops ([rule A45](../AGENT-RULES.md)). LOOP-END: nested loops must not share an end address. LOOP-LCE: no `IF NOT LCE` in the last 11 instructions of a counter loop. LOOP-CALL: no CALL in the last 5 instructions of a loop. BRANCH-12: at least 12 valid 48-bit instructions' worth of code after every branch. BRANCH-WIN: no two branches in one 48-bit (3 short-word) window. DAG-SAME: no same-DAG DAG-register store and no post-modify same-DAG DAG-register load ("the root cause of silent units"; stock real code has zero of either). PRM references 4-14, 4-41, 4-42, 4-44. The checker reports only violations not present in a stock baseline. `[hw]`

section: Digitone II OS 1.11 - function and data map (from the digitone-2-modding-skill sources) / The static checks, exactly (from `hwrules.py`, `encodecheck.py`, `shapecheck.py`)
text: Encoding census: for every instruction you add, its shape (registers and constants blanked) is looked up in stock real code; bits that are constant in every stock instance must match - catches encodings a decoder accepts but stock never emits (the negative-shift sign-bit case). Shape census: lists instruction shapes stock never uses - not an error, but each must be justified from the PRM. The skill's assembler decodes every emitted instruction and compares it with the intended text, and its 48-bit packer schedules loop bodies so they stay hwrules-safe. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-scripts}

section: Digitone II OS 1.11 - function and data map (from the digitone-2-modding-skill sources) / Talking to the running unit over USB (MIDI RPC, as used by Transfer/Elektroid and the skill)
text: Framing: `F0 00 20 3C 10 00 <8-in-7 encoded body> F7`; body = sequence (2 bytes, big-endian), `00 00`, opcode, payload; the reply opcode = request OR 0x80. Opcodes seen: `0x01` ping (device name and opcode list), `0x04` screenshot, `0x50` OsUpgradeStart (u32 size big-endian, "sysex", auto-commit byte), `0x51` OsUpgradeWrite (2 KB blocks with CRC32), `0x52` OsUpgradeEnd (1 commit / 0 cancel). OS 1.11's RPC handlers read every u32 big-endian. Upstream documentation: dnfw `docs/midi-rpc.md` (derived from Elektroid). `[doc]` {dn2-skill-scripts}

section: Digitone II OS 1.11 - function and data map (from the digitone-2-modding-skill sources) / Talking to the running unit over USB (MIDI RPC, as used by Transfer/Elektroid and the skill)
text: Upload pitfall `[hw]`: with auto-commit the OS posts "upload complete" to the upgrade view as the last block is parsed; on the first upload after a boot that view is not open yet, the event is lost and the unit sits on "OS UPGRADE / Receiving". The skill therefore sends Start without auto-commit, all blocks, waits a few seconds, then End(1) - the End handler checks every byte arrived and posts the event itself; the stock OS then validates the container and asks UPGRADE OS NOW? (press YES). Keep USB silent while it writes flash (~90 s), then ping until it answers; one upload, no retries. Raw OS SysEx sent over USB to the running OS is ignored. Python + mido can hang at exit in CoreMIDI. `[hw]` {dn2-skill-scripts} {dn2-skill-setup} ([I4](../INCIDENTS.md#i4-auto-commit-upload-loses-its-complete-event-on-the-first-upload-after-boot))
