section: Digitone II OS 1.11 - function and data map (from the digitone-2-modding-skill sources) / Build pipeline (`cfmod.py`, `dspblocks.py`, `zcache.py`)
text: C/asm is compiled with m68k GCC `-mcpu=5475 -Os` (no libc) and linked at `0x46800000` (free on 1.11) by `dnfw.patch.cbuild`; dnfw's 138-byte startup loader copies the appended `DNFW` area there at boot and calls your init; every hook site is checked against the stock bytes before it is overwritten - a wrong address fails the build; `context()` asserts bytes a hook relies on without writing them; section 3 is recompressed and the container re-signed. API shape: `jsr(addr, stub, stock=...)` (6 bytes), `jmp(addr, stub, displaced=N)` (the stub replays the displaced bytes), `patch(addr, old, new, why)`. `[hw]` Same toolchain as summarised in [`digitone-2-os111-reference.md`](digitone-2-os111-reference.md).

section: Digitone II OS 1.11 - function and data map (from the digitone-2-modding-skill sources) / Build pipeline (`cfmod.py`, `dspblocks.py`, `zcache.py`)
text: Flash space is the binding limit (2 MiB upgrade buffer): dnfw's packer is greedy with a one-step lazy look-ahead over a 32-deep match chain; a 192-deep chain packs MAIN OS 0.8 % and section 7 0.5 % smaller within the same format and window (depth 1024 packs worse); pure-Python aPLib costs ~20-50 s per section in CPython, ~3 s in PyPy; a content-keyed cache skips unchanged sections. `[hw]` {dn2-skill-scripts}

section: Digitone II OS 1.11 - function and data map (from the digitone-2-modding-skill sources) / Build pipeline (`cfmod.py`, `dspblocks.py`, `zcache.py`)
text: Examples: `double_time` hooks `move.l 0x402a0dec,%d0` (6 bytes) at `0x40027ac0` with `jsr dt_stub`, keeps the live d1/a0/a1 via `lea -12(%sp),%sp; movem.l ...,(%sp)`, and caps the doubled step under one 96 ppqn subtick per block (112,000 units); `track_trim` adds an L2 code block, a CALL hook and an fxdsl kernel (-6 dB on track 1, A/B ratio 0.5000).

It runs UI, sequencer, parameters, p-locks, LFOs and builds the 2688-byte frame sent to the DSP for every audio block. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-firmware}

section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / Hardware as described
text: One DSP block = 32 samples at 48 kHz = 1,500 blocks/s, budget about 666,667 cycles per block; stock idles at roughly 63-65 % load on the unit. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-firmware} {dn2-skill-sharc}

section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / Free memory
text: ColdFire: `0x46700000..0x46900000` unused by stock (as the skill states; wrong at its bottom end, settled in [CONFLICTS S17](../CONFLICTS.md)); cfmod links at `0x46800000`, dnfw uses `0x467c8000..0x467fffff` (the skill's figure; dnfw's chunks actually span `0x46708000-0x46f00000`, see [who uses this RAM](../common/memory-maps.md)). More RAM above is plausible but must be verified (fill, reboot, read). `[doc]` {dn2-skill-firmware}

section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / Free memory
text: SHARC L2 (contested between projects: [CONFLICTS O19](../CONFLICTS.md)): usable `0x20088400..0x200B0000`; stock loads L2 code only up to `0x2008823c`. Not above `0x200B0000` (stock data points to `0x200C0008` and `0x200C1F84`; `0x200FA000..0x200FDFFF` is non-cacheable DMA buffers; L2 is shared with the boot ROM and one block there stopped a unit from starting). New boot blocks: code at `0x20090000` (sw `0xBC8000`), data at `0x20098000` onward - hardware-proven. `[hw]` {dn2-skill-firmware} {dn2-skill-sharc}

section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / Free memory
text: SHARC DDR (512 MB): stock references go up to `0x8052FBE0`; `0x80800000` and above read back untouched on hardware. Large tables can live in DDR blocks (sw `0x800000` on, byte `0x80A00000` on) but every fetch is slow. The delay's L/R rings are masked to 2^18 samples; their upper halves are free if delay time is capped. `[hw]` {dn2-skill-firmware} {dn2-skill-sharc}

section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / Free memory
text: Power-on DDR is garbage (`0xFFFFFFFF`, a NaN, is common). A NaN that reaches a feedback state (send FX, say) silences the unit until restart. The emulator zero-fills DDR and hides this: fill new DDR with `0xFFFFFFFF` in tests. `[hw]` {dn2-skill-firmware} ([I8](../INCIDENTS.md#i8-power-on-ddr-holds-garbage-often-a-nan))

section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / ColdFire-to-DSP frame (per voice, big-endian halfwords; the DSP swaps halves of each 32-bit word)
text: Side channels: the DMA moves 1374 halfwords; the 30 halfwords after the 2688-byte frame (data halves of TX entries 1344..1373) are never rewritten by the stock driver and reach the DSP - write packets there from a hook just before the driver call (header word + checksum, round-robin if larger). Return: reply word 0 = the DSP's cycle count for the block (a load meter), +0x16 = master compressor gain reduction, `+0xa9c..+0xabc` (ColdFire `0x80005e40`, 16 u16) is unused by stock and free as a DSP -> ColdFire channel. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-firmware}

section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / ColdFire-to-DSP frame (per voice, big-endian halfwords; the DSP swaps halves of each 32-bit word)
text: Timing: the DSP renders on the codec clock and does not wait for the ColdFire. A frame that arrives after render started is dropped and the previous frame repeats, including its note-on masks ("the trig lights, no sound"). This is what happens when the ColdFire audio ISR overruns. `[hw]` {dn2-skill-firmware} {dn2-skill-coldfire}

section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / ColdFire-to-DSP frame (per voice, big-endian halfwords; the DSP swaps halves of each 32-bit word)
text: Voices are not tracks. The DSP renders 16 voices; the ColdFire allocates them per note and copies the track's sound into the voice record; unison uses several voices per note. Note path, lock applier, LFO evaluator and per-voice mirror blocks all work per voice - map voice -> track everywhere. The skill calls this the #1 bug source. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-firmware} {dn2-skill-coldfire}

section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / ColdFire hook rules
text: Hooks are `jsr stub` / `jmp stub` over N displaced bytes; the build asserts the displaced bytes match stock. Arguments on the stack, result in d0 (GCC ColdFire convention); d0, d1, a0, a1 are scratch. A hook in the middle of a function must preserve d0, d1, a0, a1 for the code after it; a hook replacing a function's entry must preserve the callee's exit d0, d1, a0, a1 and copy every stack argument. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-coldfire}

section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / ColdFire hook rules
text: `movem` accepts only `(An)` or `d16(An)`: push with `lea -12(%sp),%sp; movem.l %d1/%a0-%a1,(%sp)`; recount `sp@(n)` after every push. Every symbol a hook references must be an entry or `--gc-sections` drops it. No libc: zero-initialised locals become `memset` calls and the link fails - use static const data or field-by-field stores. Appended asm after `.bss` lands in zeroed memory and the boot dies in the exception reporter. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-coldfire}

section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / ColdFire hook rules
text: Compiler: m68k GCC `-mcpu=5475 -Os`; build system `dnfw.patch.cbuild` with `cfmod.Mod` as startup loader. cfmod's loader cave: 138 bytes at `0x4028da6e` (copies the appended area to its load address at boot and calls your init); proven asm cave: 170 bytes at `0x4028ea02`; never use the ~64 KB of zeros near `0x402e2000` (the `.data` initializer). `[doc]` {dn2-skill-coldfire}

section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / ColdFire hook rules
text: Audio ISR budget `[hw]`: period ~0.67 ms per block; stock already uses ~64 % during playback; code at `0x46xxxxxx` costs roughly 4x more cycles per instruction than stock (DDR + cache misses) while SRAM at `0x8000xxxx` is cheap. Keep ISR C short, non-blocking, allocation-free; defer per-note work; count DDR accesses, not instructions. A laggy UI usually means ISR work is too heavy. `[hw]` {dn2-skill-coldfire}

section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / ColdFire hook rules
text: Slot bounds: every stock value, lock and LFO routine bounds `slot <= 100`; slots 0, 65 and 100 are holes; a sound stores 101 u16 values at `sound + 0x14 + 2*slot`. A new slot means hooking every one of those routines. Your own p-lock record headers need an ID no stock slot uses, and copy/paste/recount/clear routines must skip them. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-coldfire}

section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / ColdFire hook rules
text: Pitfalls: a new parameter record needs a guard record after the last entry (the drawer reads one past); enum formatters print ERR past their table; every per-sound side table needs a reset hook (sound reset and kit creation reuse memory); sound save rewrites LFO DEST words in slots 4, 12 and 20; skipping the stock redraw request can add ~1 s UI latency on hardware (the emulator does not show it); never draw the stock screen and then patch it (panel can receive a frame mid-draw); a new machine type means re-entering every per-type accessor bounded by `type <= 4`. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-coldfire}

section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / Emulator coverage (skill's view)
text: SHARC (`sim.py`/`simc.py`, ~200 blocks/s with the C core, ~7 on PyPy, ~1 on CPython): logic and arithmetic in the real frame, stock-vs-mod A/B, memory footprint, the PRM rules it encodes. Cannot cover timing, caches, stalls, interrupts, DMA, branch predictor, ECC, boot-ROM loading, power-on memory contents; "instruction counts under-predict the unit's load". One-time boot ~4 min (`dn2setup.py --boot`). `[doc]`

section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / Emulator coverage (skill's view)
text: ColdFire (digikit + `fastemu.py` + `cfkit.py`, 10-30 M instr/s): main OS in Unicorn with HLEs for flash, SD, panel, screen; boots to the main screen (~1 min first time, cached). Divergences: idle skip fires widget timers far more often (redraws look smoother than the unit's ~1/s); encoders register in bursts (single detents do nothing, use `turn_to` with 11-detent messages); holds need >= 12 M instructions; keys right after encoder bursts may drop; Python hooks do not fire under the fast stepper; panel TX ring is never drained; no DTCN2 timer; plain Unicorn halves fractional EMAC results (use digiemu's patched Unicorn); test from several start offsets - a real bug fails at every offset. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-emulators}

section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / Emulator coverage (skill's view)
text: Measuring on hardware: a screenshot RPC (`dn2rpc.c shot`) lets a mod publish a debug page; DSP load = reply word 0; ColdFire ISR time = DTCN2 stamps at hook entry and before the RTE (`0x40027bbe`). `[doc]` {dn2-skill-emulators}

section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / Flashing notes from the skill's setup
text: Flash with `scripts/rpc_flash.py IMAGE.syx` over USB or Elektron Transfer and confirm on the unit. Keep USB quiet for ~90 s during the flash write. The first upload after boot is lost with auto-commit; kill stale flasher processes before rerunning. Python + mido can hang at exit on CoreMIDI. Avoid flashing or measuring during heavy local jobs (USB MIDI timing). Raw SysEx over USB to the running OS is ignored (only the update protocol works). Recovery: FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4, DIN MIDI, ~12-15 min. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-setup}

section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / Flashing notes from the skill's setup
text: Toolchain: `gcc-m68k-linux-gnu` / `binutils-m68k-linux-gnu` with `-mcpu=5475` on Linux/WSL; on macOS build GCC 13 and binutils 2.42 from source; PyPy 3.10+, `cffi`, `mido`, `python-rtmidi`; dnfw from angellinares/dn2_firmware_explore; digikit (the skill clones m-dwyer/digikit and applies `scripts/digikit-local.patch`). The stock-file check: SHA-256 starts `2af43e65` and ends `72e0` (the full value is `dn2paths.STOCK_SHA256`; elsewhere in this repo: `2af43e65e3d8390b41c9f66222620f8cce027d73ed87db00c80b440f628472e0`). `[doc]` {dn2-skill-setup}

section: Digitone II / From the official manual (OS 1.12; first part only - the MIDI appendix C was not reachable)
text: 16 tracks, each audio (SYN machine) or MIDI; 16 audio voices (one per track) each with SYN machine, bit reduction, filter, amp and LFO; 12 V DC via PSU-3c; balanced/unbalanced 1/4" I/O, inputs also over USB; MIDI IN, OUT/SYNC A, THRU/SYNC B (SYNC outputs can send DIN sync); USB type B, class compliant, audio + MIDI, Overbridge. Wait at least 30 s after power-off before powering on again; ambient max 40 deg C. `[doc]` {dn2-manual}

section: Digitone II / From the official manual (OS 1.12; first part only - the MIDI appendix C was not reachable)
text: Data model: +Drive holds up to 128 projects and a library of 2,048 presets; a project = 128 patterns (8 banks x 16), 16 songs, a 128-preset pool and general settings; a pattern holds up to 16 presets (one per track), sequencer data, TRIG page settings, BPM, length, swing, time signature, MIDI track parameters; a preset holds SYN1, SYN2, FLTR, AMP and LFO pages. Digitone I projects can be imported but patterns may differ - re-save on Digitone II before exporting. `[doc]` {dn2-manual}

section: Digitone II / From the official manual (OS 1.12; first part only - the MIDI appendix C was not reachable)
text: MIDI in: notes 0-15 trigger tracks 1-16 (default channels), notes 16-84 (E2-C7) play the active track chromatically (C5 = 60 is middle C), program change 0-127 selects patterns A01-H16, tap tempo by note C0 on the FX CONTROL channel; MIDI tracks: up to 16 notes per step, pitch bend, aftertouch, 16 assignable CCs (CC1-8 on the FLTR page, 9-16 on AMP); the lowest-numbered track wins when tracks share a channel. TRIG modes: TRACKS, VELOCITIES (TRIG 1-15 = velocity 8..120 in steps of 8, TRIG 16 = 127), RETRIGS (1/1 ... 1/64). `[doc]` {dn2-manual}

section: Digitone II / From the official manual (OS 1.12; first part only - the MIDI appendix C was not reachable)
text: Appendix C groups (numbers not extracted): C.1 Track, C.2 Trig, C.3 Source, C.4 Filter, C.5 Amp, C.6 Euclidean, C.7 FX, C.8 MOD, C.9 Send FX, C.10 Mixer, C.11 VAL, C.12 MISC. Startup menu entries: TEST MODE, EMPTY RESET, FACTORY RESET, OS UPGRADE, EXIT (other sources: TRIG 4 = OS UPGRADE). `[doc]` {dn2-manual}

section: Digitone II / Architecture
text: ColdFire main CPU (big-endian code, GCC-built, C++ RTTI names remain); SHARC+ audio DSP. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw} {dn2-firmware-explore}

section: Digitone II / Architecture
text: `MAIN OS` section: 3,085,696 bytes on 1.10E and 3,192,192 bytes on 1.11 (unpacked), loads at `0x40000400`. `[doc]` {dn2-firmware-explore}

section: Digitone II / Architecture
text: Container signed with HMAC-SHA256 with a key derived from the image itself, so the tools re-sign modified images ([`../common/firmware-container.md`](../common/firmware-container.md)). `[doc]` {dn2-firmware-explore}

section: Digitone II / Architecture
text: The OS keeps its C++ RTTI, enough to name most code: on 1.12, 12,350 functions and 1,624 types (752 classes, 872 lambdas), 741 with vtables; about a third of all instructions sit in a function that RTTI names. A function that loads a vtable is a constructor or destructor; a `std::function` lambda's typeinfo names its enclosing method with the signature. The DSP has no application RTTI. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-firmware}

section: Digitone II / Architecture
text: 1.11 to 1.12: sections 2, 4, 7 and 8 are byte-identical (the DSP did not change); section 3 is relinked (+4 KB, BSS +0x1000, DMA alias +0x8000). Overtone ships on 1.12 by translating every 1.11 patch address through a code map built from anchors of 10 matching instructions. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-firmware}

section: Digitone II / Architecture
text: Cache map (OS 1.11 and 1.12): the bootstrap leaves the data cache off (CACR `0x000cc100`), but the main OS start-up at `0x40000554` writes CACR `0xa50ce100` and ACR0 `0x4007e020`: `0x40000000-0x47ffffff` is cached copyback, everything else uncached, including the SSI DMA buffers at `0x4e6e7100`. Reading those buffers byte by byte from a mod is slow enough to stall the sequencer: Digiwerk's first multichannel USB build (UM01) packed the SSI slots with byte-wise uncached reads and lagged until unusable; reading each of the 14 slots once as a 32-bit word (UM02) ran on the unit with busy sequences and no lag. Checking only the bootstrap's CACR gave a wrong "cache off" conclusion first, corrected the same day. `[hw]` {dn2-cfw-handoff} {dn2-cfw-usb} ([I10](../INCIDENTS.md#i10-byte-wise-reads-of-uncached-dma-buffers-stalled-the-sequencer))

section: Digitone II / Architecture
text: DSP works per block; the stock handler can be interpreted offline (sharcvm); new effects are portable C, compiled with selache/selcc and spliced into the DSP section. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw}

section: Digitone II / Architecture
text: Board PCBA0109B, read from photographs of the parts (dnfw `docs/hardware.md`, 2026-09-12) {dn2-hw}. The same board number as the Digitakt II is reported. CPU: ColdFire MCF5441SCMJ250 (MCF5441x, 250 MHz). Not the V4e that older notes inherited from the Octatrack. RAM: NANYA NT5TU128M8HE-AC, 128 MB DDR2. Flash: Winbond W25Q128JV (16 MB SPI NOR, by the ColdFire). Storage: Kingston EMMC32G-TX29 (32 GB eMMC). DSP: ADSP-21569 (KBCZ10) with its own Kingston DDR3 beside it. Codec: AKM AK4621EF, 20 MHz crystal by the SHARC. There is no flash chip by the DSP: the ColdFire boots the SHARC (section 7 is its boot stream). `[hw]` (photos)

section: Digitone II / Architecture
text: Flash-part mismatch worth knowing: the bootstrap's DYB sector protection (`0xE1`) is applied only on a Spansion S25FL (`0x01 2018`), and digikit's DT2 reading names that part. On a unit with the Winbond part, that lock has no effect (Digiwerk T1.5/T1.4). Do not count on hardware write protection of the bootstrap. `[?]` {dn2-hw} {dn2-cfw-t15}

section: Digitone II / Architecture
text: Third-party claim about the family (not measured): Digitone mk1: two MCF54415 plus a Spartan XC3S50A. Digitakt mk1: one MCF54415. Digitakt II: one MCF54415-class part plus the ADSP-21569. Syntakt: two MCF54415, XC3S50A and XC3S200A (the latter driving the analog side). digikit's Syntakt 1.42 reading (an FPGA section, a second ColdFire program) fits. `[?]` {dn2-hw}

section: Digitone II / Architecture
text: Cross-device transplant (armio's R012, DN2 1.11): the Digitakt II 1.16 sample machines and their UI (ONESHOT, WERP, STRETCH, REPITCH, GRID, SLICE, stereo samples, sample browsing) run on a Digitone II. Donor routines are extracted from the official DT2 file and relocated at build time. `[doc]` {armio-r012} The same build makes USB AUDIO class-compliant with 42 capture channels (48 kHz/24 bit, 21 stereo pairs) and a stereo return. Digiwerk's USB01 note sketched this. `[doc]` {armio-r012} R013 (2026-11-05) adds the missing sample-storage setup: SYSTEM > FORMAT SAMPLES creates a sample filesystem in an area the stock OS does not expose as sample storage, and erases that area (including other mods' data there). Formatting, restart, Transfer capacity (about 20 GB on the tested DN2) and uploads afterwards passed on the unit. `[hw]` {armio-samples}

section: Digitone II / Architecture
text: Two independent 42-channel USB audio builds now exist for the DN2, on different OS versions: armio's (1.11, above) and Digiwerk 0.3.0 (1.12, USB MULTI/MIDI as a fourth USB CONFIG choice; UAC 2.0, 48 kHz/24 bit; inputs 1-32 the 16 tracks, 33-34 main, 35-40 delay/reverb/chorus returns, 41-42 the inputs; used with a Mac and with AUM on an iPhone). Digiwerk's USB addition changes only the main OS, leaving each build's DSP section unchanged. `[hw]` {dn2-cfw-030} {dn2-cfw-usb} Historical size estimate (UM03): the USB addition's code and BSS added about 2.6 KB to the existing 1 MB mod region. `0x47e00000-0x47e075a4` describes the combined used span, not the USB addition alone; this is not a size measurement of the later UM04 implementation shipped in 0.3.0. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-um03} Recorder adds recording/resampling, source selection, normalization, trimming, audition, saving to +Drive and optional track assignment. VOICE cycles Voice Setup, Sample Manager and Recorder. Exact trimmed-file comparison and full Recorder-source coverage remain unverified. `[doc]` {armio-recorder} R012 requires only the two official OS files. Native and browser builds verify the final SHA-256; the browser builds locally without uploads. No sample bank or factory library is required; historical exact T1E2/R003/R008/R011 builds still need their original private bank. `[doc]` {armio-r012} {armio-browser} R012 stable is owner-confirmed for stock audio, samples, Recorder and USB audio, including after project changes. This is not exhaustive workflow or endurance validation. `[hw]` {armio-r012}

section: Digitone II / Architecture
text: USB audio repeating old audio after a project change (armio, R007-R011; fixed 2026-11-03): USB audio froze or repeated while headphones and UI kept working; accepted publications stopped, rejected ones rose by 16,392 in about 10.9 s, and USB transfers kept running. Cause: the render-time TX selector follows RX completion and is not a TX ownership grant, but the build had bound the retained queue head to a destination derived from that older phase. R011 picks the candidate from the current DMA START and leaves the ownership guards to decide; the owner confirmed playback after project changes, and R012 is the stable build. Endurance and end-to-end USB latency are unmeasured. `[hw]` {armio-usb} {armio-r011} ([I13](../INCIDENTS.md#i13-usb-audio-repeated-old-audio-after-a-project-change))

section: Digitone II / Sampler port lifecycle findings (DN2 OS 1.11, 2026-11-06)
text: Incremental working-state updates are a separate persistence path from whole-project saves. In armio's port, sample load/unload updates a separate identity companion and sends the native ProjectSettings notification. Its queued worker `0x400469E2` calls settings serializer `0x400DF57A` at `0x400469FE`; it does not pass through whole-project serializer `0x400E1494`. The extension had been attached only to the latter, so the native settings mirror advanced while the added sample mirror stayed stale. The alternating boot snapshots at sectors `0x40000` / `0x48000` are separate from explicitly saved project slots (see the existing [storage map](../common/memory-maps.md)). R020 replay reproduced a new identity absent from the prepared backup and from a fresh emulated boot. R022 updates the working companion at the narrow settings-worker callsite under the existing project mutex, checking destination, owner, readiness and matching UIDs; explicit saved companions remain untouched. Unchanged identities skip the 16 KiB copy/CRC. Load, unload, fresh-boot restore and failure guards passed native replay; physical shutdown and freeze recovery are unverified. These extension defects are not evidence of a stock DN2 autosave bug. `[emu]` {armio-r022} ([I52](../INCIDENTS.md#i52-new-project-samples-were-missing-after-reboot))

section: Digitone II / Sampler port lifecycle findings (DN2 OS 1.11, 2026-11-06)
text: A Machine change can leave a port's old SYN view attached even when the Sound has changed. Native selection reselects the view when audio/MIDI classification changes; stock synth to a ported sampler remains an audio track. Generic Project, ActiveTrack and Sound notifications redraw but do not replace the view. R020 replay reproduced knob D reaching the stock handler after switching to all six samplers. R021, included in R022, reconciles the exposed SYN view through the existing factory and native selector on the next UI poll, deferring during modal ownership, selected-trig edits, construction and expired ownership. Ten transitions and nine guards passed. Earlier tests explicitly selected SYN before turning D and therefore repaired the state they were meant to test. Hardware confirmation is pending. `[emu]` {armio-r022} ([I51](../INCIDENTS.md#i51-the-sample-popup-did-not-open-after-switching-machines))

section: Digitone II / Parameter table
text: 1.12: one OS table of 321 rows, no free space after it. dn2-cfw's patch GT00 copies it at start-up into free memory with room for 384 rows; GT01 adds 17 hidden rows (3-band compressor). `[hw]` {dn2-cfw}

section: Digitone II / Parameter table
text: Projects store values by slot, not by row, so moving the table keeps the saved format; new rows follow `docs/parameter-table-growth.md` (not read yet). Table growth was first done on 1.11 for the LFO4 mod in dn2_firmware_explore. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw}

section: Digitone II / Parameter table
text: Overtone: LFO 3's storage holds ARP 2, so a sound that used LFO 3 loses it; ENV3/LFO3 no longer exist in Overtone. `[doc]` {overtone}

section: Digitone II / Parameter table / Parameter table details (OS 1.12; dn2-cfw `docs/parameter-table-growth.md`)
text: Each parameter is one 60-byte row. Table base `0x401f83a4`, stock 321 rows. Offsets: `+0x00` group (set/page family), `+0x04` k (the slot that holds the value in its set), `+0x08..0x14` min/max/default/bipolar, `+0x18` MIDI CC, `+0x1c` NRPN, `+0x20` Overbridge id, `+0x28..0x38` names/formatter/suffix. A separate RAM display table holds glyph, lock flags and randomiser data. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-param-table}

section: Digitone II / Parameter table / Parameter table details (OS 1.12; dn2-cfw `docs/parameter-table-growth.md`)
text: Row ids are not saved; projects store values by slot k through fixed k-to-stored-id tables. Slot maps and CC/NRPN maps are rebuilt from the table at each boot (`0x400dc634`); page records are built at boot from code constants (`0x400c2c4e`). Moving the table does not change project storage; new rows do, via their k and display flags. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-param-table}

section: Digitone II / Parameter table / Parameter table details (OS 1.12; dn2-cfw `docs/parameter-table-growth.md`)
text: Grown table at `0x47D00000`, room for 384 rows (`0x180`), copied at boot by `pg_boot` (called from `0x40000568`). New row ids `0x141`-`0x17f` (63 ids); the same-length-edit ceiling is `0x1e0` (480 rows). 56 address operands in 53 functions had to be redirected; 57 row-count compares changed (`#0x141`->`#0x180`, `#0x140`->`#0x17f`; five look similar and stay). The display-table reader at `0x400c257c` has its first 10 bytes turned into a jump plus two nops. The MIDI input cache (33 constants in five functions) grows by 12,852 bytes. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-param-table}

section: Digitone II / Parameter table / Parameter table details (OS 1.12; dn2-cfw `docs/parameter-table-growth.md`)
text: The grown table ran on a unit (Digiwerk GT00/GT01, OS 1.12, 2026-10-13): boot, cold start, +Drive project save and load were all reported fine, and GT01 added 17 hidden rows for the 3-band compressor that later shipped (CMP3). In the emulator, not one instruction read the stock table after the boot copy. Since projects store values by slot k, and stock saves FX k 25-69 only, values in new slots k 70+ need their own storage (the 3-band compressor uses 28 FX-record words that stock never writes or reads). Whether such a project opens cleanly on a stock OS has not been reported. `[hw]` {dn2-cfw-t65}

section: Digitone II / Parameter table / Parameter table details (OS 1.12; dn2-cfw `docs/parameter-table-growth.md`)
text: New rows carry Overbridge ids of `0x400` and up. Each is sent to the plugin as soon as its value changes; what the plugin does with an id it doesn't know is not known. `[emu]` {dn2-cfw-t65}

section: Digitone II / Parameter table / Parameter table details (OS 1.12; dn2-cfw `docs/parameter-table-growth.md`)
text: Map builders hold 101 entries each, so k must stay in range (0..100 for sound/FX/MIDI, 0..25 for trig). Stock saves FX k 25-69 only; FX k 70+ and sound k 65 and 100 are not saved. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-param-table}

section: Digitone II / Parameter table / Parameter table details (OS 1.12; dn2-cfw `docs/parameter-table-growth.md`)
text: Rules for a new row: use a free k in the set's table, one row per k (the last row written wins and can silently replace a stock knob); value 0 must keep classic behaviour (existing projects store 0 in slots stock has no row for); send-FX rows set `flags_set = 8` so they are never lockable; synth rows use free saved k values (FM Tone 34, 49; WaveTone 50-64; FM Drum 55-64; Swarmer 33-64); no randomiser; MIDI: no CC already in the set's map, none in 32-63, none taken by the CC parser (1, 2, 6, 64, 66, 94, 98, 99, 110, 120, 121, 123), NRPN 398 at most; Overbridge id outside stock's 0..387 (e.g. `0x400`+n, untested with the plugin). `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-param-table}

section: Digitone II / Parameter table / Parameter table details (OS 1.12; dn2-cfw `docs/parameter-table-growth.md`)
text: P-lock trap: a row is lockable when display flag bits 0 and 3 are clear; locks are stored as (track, k), so an FX row with k 70 could create a lock on a sound's slot 70, which stock would play back. A bad row can write past map tables, replace a stock knob, or leave stray p-locks that persist after returning to stock. A project saved on a grown build and loaded on stock 1.12 is untested on hardware. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-param-table}

section: Digitone II / Parameter table / Parameter table details (OS 1.12; dn2-cfw `docs/parameter-table-growth.md`)
text: Checks used: brick checker 12/12 for GT00/GT01 ("a pass is not proof for code changes"), `scripts/t65_build.py check_rows` for FX rows, `pg_boot` only skips ids outside `0x141`-`0x17f` (it does not check k, flags, CCs or Overbridge ids), an emulator run of 7,100 MIDI messages giving the same 991 parameter sets as baseline. Never flash `param-test-dn2` or `fx-page2-dn2`. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-param-table}

A frame guard silences voices that no longer fit (limit 0.6 of the frame, estimated, not measured). `[doc]` {dn2mk2-firmware-md}

section: Digitone II / Sample memory (dn2mk2)
text: Pool of 400 MB (368 MB user samples + 32 MB recordings, ~5.5 min), up to 122 slots, RAM-checked at power-on (~0.7 s); +Drive library ~20 GB in a region the stock OS does not touch, up to 2,048 samples; slices up to 64 per sample, stored in a 128 KB area. Power-on load grows with stored samples (~30 s for 20 MB). The 400 MB pool has never run on hardware per FIRMWARE.md v0.22. `[emu]` {dn2mk2-firmware-md}

section: Digitone II / Sample memory (dn2mk2)
text: A stock DN2 has no sample filesystem, and a mod that mounts one must also create it (armio R012, 2026-11-03). R012 mounted an existing sample filesystem but did not create one on a unit that never had it; on such a unit Transfer showed 0% Free / 0 bytes, uploads stalled and connections failed. The author says stock FORMAT +DRIVE, EMPTY RESET and FACTORY RESET do not create it and can erase projects. The bug was found by new users; the author's own unit had storage prepared during development, which is why owner testing missed it. A test on a freshly flashed stock unit is the only check that catches this. `[doc]` {armio-samples} ([I12](../INCIDENTS.md#i12-a-sample-machine-mod-could-not-create-the-storage-it-needed))

section: Digitone II / Sample memory (dn2mk2)
text: Stock eMMC TRIM can fail with TRIM ERROR on a busy card (OS 1.11). A unit running dn2mk2 v0.39 stopped with TRIM ERROR at two different sector ranges while erasing mod data. dn2mk2's reading of the stock code: TRIM `0x4012c4b2` fails only when CMD35/36/38 get no answer (command timeout); after CMD38 the busy wait arms the DAT0 edge interrupt (`0x4012c53e`) before testing DAT0 (`0x4012c544`), so a short TRIM whose card finishes in between leaves a stale semaphore post (`0x4461b6c0`), the next TRIM on a really busy card returns at once, and the call after it gets no answer. The driver has no timeout. v0.40's fix: read the eSDHC present-state register `PRSSTAT` `0xfc0cc024` before every TRIM and verify read and call only when the card is idle; retry a failed call five times (TRIM is idempotent); report ERASE PAUSED and continue on request. The error is `[hw]`; the race is a static reading of stock code, not seen on the bus. Anything that issues TRIMs through the stock driver on a DN2 (and, not checked, a DT2 with the same driver) should do the same. `[hw]` {dn2mk2-v040} ([I1](../INCIDENTS.md#i1-stock-emmc-trim-fails-with-trim-error-on-a-busy-card))

section: Digitone (mk1) / Digitone Keys / The board and the second ColdFire (taktone, DN1 1.43 with DT1 1.53/1.54 applications)
text: The Digitone mk1 is a Digitakt mk1 plus six keys, a second ColdFire and an FPGA. taktone runs Digitakt 1.53/1.54 main OS builds on Digitone hardware by replacing only section 3 and adapting the panel, LEDs, codec start-up, autosave GPIO and shutdown copy. Four 1.53-based builds were reported working on hardware. `[hw]` Both main CPUs set up 128 MiB DDR at `0x40000000-0x48000000` (cached and uncached aliases are the same RAM). `[doc]`

section: Digitone (mk1) / Digitone Keys / The board and the second ColdFire (taktone, DN1 1.43 with DT1 1.53/1.54 applications)
text: How the main CPU drives the second ColdFire (board interface, from taktone-extended, which ran its own engine on it): Reset: PB6 held low. Releasing it starts a serial boot. Upload: the main CPU is DSPI2 slave (eDMA 29, vector 149) and the secondary supplies the clock. Section 6 (a 1,504-byte loader stream; dnfw's section table lists it as 1,492 bytes and "unidentified") loads section 7, which runs at secondary `0x40000400` from entry `0x40000B92`. Shared SRAM: FlexBus, main at `0x10000000`, secondary at `0x00000000`. Native use is below offset `0x7a0`: a 928-byte parameter packet at `0x000-0x39f`, then eight mono voices of 32 signed 32-bit samples at `0x3a0-0x79f`. Handshake: the secondary writes `HO`/`HA`; the main writes 1 to +2 before `B0` to +0. The stock secondary then writes `A5A5` at +4. Render request: a PA4 edge triggers the secondary's DTIM0 capture (vector 96). The secondary signals back through EPORT4 (vector 68). One block of pipeline: ~0.667 ms. Clear stale shared words at start, because they can survive a main reset. Never wait in the audio IRQ for late output, and bound the start-up polling. `[hw]`

section: Digitone (mk1) / Digitone Keys / The board and the second ColdFire (taktone, DN1 1.43 with DT1 1.53/1.54 applications)
text: The FPGA bitstream is in section 7: decompressed from `0x400077A0` to `0x40009000`, 54,664 bytes, sent as 16-bit words over the secondary's DSPI1. This is the same size as the Analog Heat +FX's and Analog Four MKII's FPGA sections, a strong lead for research map T12. Stock FPGA polling can stall forever, so keep a main-side timeout. `[doc]`

section: Digitone (mk1) / Digitone Keys / The board and the second ColdFire (taktone, DN1 1.43 with DT1 1.53/1.54 applications)
text: Two SysEx addressings: the startup menu's OS UPGRADE receiver always expects Digitone-addressed SysEx (device `0x0d`). A running Digitakt-based application expects Digitakt addressing (`0x0a`). So recovery to stock Digitone always goes through the startup menu over DIN. `[hw]` (first install confirmed over USB)

section: Digitone (mk1) / Digitone Keys / The board and the second ColdFire (taktone, DN1 1.43 with DT1 1.53/1.54 applications) / Writing your own engine for the second ColdFire (taktone-extended's contract)
text: Split the work: keep sequencer, locks, LFOs, menu and storage on the main CPU; render on the secondary from a complete control snapshot. Compile secondary code for `-mcpu=54418 -msoft-float`, freestanding.

section: Digitone (mk1) / Digitone Keys / The board and the second ColdFire (taktone, DN1 1.43 with DT1 1.53/1.54 applications) / Writing your own engine for the second ColdFire (taktone-extended's contract)
text: Shared protocol (taktone's, versioned): a ready tag, committed/completed sequence words, eight 28-byte controls and an XOR checksum; outputs as eight 32-frame int32 mono blocks at `0x3a0`; only aligned longword writes with readback: no byte writes to shared RAM, and any mismatch disables submission; one packet outstanding, never block the audio callback, and shut down after 64 consecutive misses.

section: Digitone (mk1) / Digitone Keys / The board and the second ColdFire (taktone, DN1 1.43 with DT1 1.53/1.54 applications) / Writing your own engine for the second ColdFire (taktone-extended's contract)
text: Hook points on the main CPU (Digitakt 1.53 application): triggers are captured at `0x40077F8E`, before stock source processing consumes them; voice PCM is substituted at `0x40077FBA`, before filter, AMP and mix. On the secondary, init is patched at `0x40000B7A` and the stock engine init at `0x40000B80` is skipped.

section: Digitone (mk1) / Digitone Keys / The board and the second ColdFire (taktone, DN1 1.43 with DT1 1.53/1.54 applications) / Writing your own engine for the second ColdFire (taktone-extended's contract)
text: Memory: taktone shrinks the native buddy heap from 16 to 8 MiB to reserve `0x4319D6B0-0x4399D6B0` for its runtime, with guard words at both ends. The sample pool (`0x43BAF5F0-0x47BAF640`) and the audio-input ring (`0x47C00000-0x48000000`) stay untouched. This is the same heap-reservation idea as SyntHack's modarea on the Syntakt. `[hw]` (Sophie on the secondary ran on units) / `[doc]` (addresses)

section: Digitone (mk1) / Digitone Keys / Caches at startup (digitone-arp-mod, OS 1.44, emulator trace and the NXP manual)
text: Stock MAIN then writes CACR `0xa50ce100` at `0x4000055a`, after its copies. That write invalidates the instruction, branch and data caches and turns caching on. The same CACR value appears on the Rytm and A4 MKII.

text: Code your mod copies before that write is safe. Code copied later must be followed by an explicit invalidation, because instruction-cache contents can even survive a reset. This is the ColdFire twin of rule A28.

section: Digitone (mk1) / Digitone Keys / Load on the main ColdFire, from a master-effects suite (Tone+FX, OS 1.43/1.44)
text: Budget: 250 MHz, so 166,667 cycles per 32-sample block. In the emulator's cycle model, stock plus Tone+FX with all effects off peaks at ~101k cycles per block. With its three heaviest effects on it peaks at ~160k, which leaves 4 % at worst (the p99 is better). The mods' RAM pool is 1.25 MB. `[emu]`

section: Digitone (mk1) / Digitone Keys / Load on the main ColdFire, from a master-effects suite (Tone+FX, OS 1.43/1.44)
text: The emulator and the unit disagreed: The unit's CPU meter went from ~70 % to ~87 % at idle between two releases, while the emulator's cycle model said the render had become *faster*. Suspects are what the model leaves out: EMAC mode switches (each handler flipped MACSR between integer and fractional, 12 switches per block), DDR bursts for a 24-bit delay line, instruction-cache pressure from inlining, and UI redraws. Still unresolved. `[hw]`

section: Digitone (mk1) / Digitone Keys / Load on the main ColdFire, from a master-effects suite (Tone+FX, OS 1.43/1.44)

A "fused" single-pass insert, meant to save loads and stores, measured +15 % on the unit. Every optimisation is A/B'd on hardware before it lands. `[hw]`

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60)
text: joelanders/gearmulator-md-mm source (`source/elektron/md/mdLib`: memory map, types, board scheduler comments). Key {gearmulator-md-mm}. Projects: [../../catalog/machinedrum.md](../../catalog/machinedrum.md), [../../catalog/monomachine.md](../../catalog/monomachine.md). The short version: an early-2000s three-chip design (an old ColdFire plus two Motorola DSP56303s). It is nothing like the DT2/DN2: no SHARC, no FreeRTOS budget model, and no USB. Its flash updater lives in a boot sector that the OS itself can rewrite.

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Machinedrum silicon
text: CPU: ColdFire MCF5206E. It runs the OS (UI, sequencer, MIDI, kits, parameter conversion, flash, DSP control). Older notes say MCF5307; the board model and the MAME driver both identify an MCF5206E. `[doc]`

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Machinedrum silicon
text: DSP2 ("producer"), a DSP56303: renders the 16 machine voices, one 32-sample mono block per track per audio block. It holds the machine code, the stock sample data and the sample RAM. Custom machines run here.

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Machinedrum silicon
text: DSP1 ("mixer"), a DSP56303: track effects, mix, master delay/reverb/EQ/dynamics, and the six-output codec. Custom-machine work leaves it untouched.

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Machinedrum silicon
text: Links: ColdFire to each DSP over the HI08 host port. The DSP-side handler takes an address and a count and DMAs the words into Y memory; this is how parameters reach a voice. DSP2 to DSP1 over ESSI0 (one block per track); codec on ESSI1. MIDI on ColdFire UART1; front panel on UART2. The old idea that the ColdFire plays voices through a DSP SCI port is wrong. `[doc]`

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Machinedrum silicon
text: Timing: 44.1 kHz, 32-sample blocks. DSP1 at 101.6064 MHz = 73,728 cycles per block. DSP2 at 98.784 MHz = 71,680 cycles per block. Its program never sets the PLL, so the boot stub's setting stays. The emulator clocks it at DSP1's rate and so overstates the budget. The two budgets cannot be pooled. `[hw]`

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Machinedrum budget facts (DSP2)
text: The whole producer pass (16 renders plus dispatch, updates, interrupts and DMA waits) must fit in 71,680 cycles. A severe overrun on hardware first crackled, then lit every LED and left the engine silent. `[hw]`

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Machinedrum budget facts (DSP2)
text: Per-track floor of ~3,290 cycles (measured on hardware): each track's 32-word block travels to DSP1 over ESSI0 at ~100 cycles a word, double-buffered. Track k's transfer runs during track k+1's render, so a track costs `max(render + ~40, ~3,290)`. Time saved below the floor is lost, not banked. Making a cheap machine cheaper gains nothing. `[hw]`

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Machinedrum budget facts (DSP2)
text: Planning numbers (emulator): an idle track 3,438 cycles; stock TRX/EFM/E12/P-I voices ~2,000-3,200. `[emu]`

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Machinedrum budget facts (DSP2)
text: External-memory wait states (the emulator ignores them; measured on hardware): ~1 wait state in areas 0-2, ~5 in area 3 (`0x1C0000+`). A machine with many external accesses costs several thousand cycles more on hardware than in the emulator. `[hw]`

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / How full DSP2 is with stock kits (MModule research 04, OS 1.63, emulator)
text: In emulated cycles, a busy kit costs 38,789 per block (54 % of 71,680), and the most expensive stock kit, 16 ROM machines, up to 67,309 (94 %). `[emu]`

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / How full DSP2 is with stock kits (MModule research 04, OS 1.63, emulator)
text: Kitbasher measured that pipeline interlocks alone add a median 26 % on hardware, so the dearest stock kits sit close to the limit. Treat these numbers as a floor.

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / How full DSP2 is with stock kits (MModule research 04, OS 1.63, emulator)
text: MModule found `$020000-$0FFFFF` of the emulated DSP's shared P/X/Y never written by the 1.63 program (found by poisoning memory and playing all 104 machines). That is emulator memory: check what a real unit decodes there before relying on it (compare the `P:0x400` lesson below). `[emu]`

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Emulator vs unit (Gearmulator's Machinedrum board model)
text: Flash appears at both `0x0` and `0x10000000` in the emulator. On hardware, after the OS remaps CS0 nothing decodes the low window: images with low-window flash pointers boot in the emulator and hang on the unit. Link and point through `0x10000000`, and scan images for low pointers. `[hw]` ([I38](../INCIDENTS.md#i38-low-window-flash-pointers-boot-in-the-emulator-and-hang-on-the-unit))

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Emulator vs unit (Gearmulator's Machinedrum board model)
text: `P:0x400-0x4FF` on DSP2 is not internal memory on hardware (the cache is on, so internal P ends at `0x3FF`). Early prototypes put code there. `[hw]`

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Emulator vs unit (Gearmulator's Machinedrum board model)
text: No pipeline interlocks, no wait states and no instruction-cache timing in the emulator. Bit-exact tests can't see any of them.

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Emulator vs unit (Gearmulator's Machinedrum board model)
text: A coarse CPU/DSP time slice (125 µs) produced false "missed blocks" that look exactly like overruns. Use a 30 µs quantum before blaming your code. `[emu]` Rule A23 ("success is no proof") applies with force here.

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
text: ColdFire ISA: `movem.l d0-d1,-(sp)` is a 68000/68020 form ColdFire lacks. Emulators run a 68020 core, and the first trigger of every new machine froze the unit. Kitbasher allows only ISA_A for the MCF5206e (no MAC in added code) and decodes the final image from every entry point (rule A42).

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
text: Boot-time memory: Ordinary stores to flash relocation sites hung the unit at the boot screen; the emulator ignored them. Boot writes from `0x2bd000` up froze a MKII +Drive UW at the logo, while the same image without them booted. Use only hardware-proven RAM ranges. Boot code must not push registers before the OS has set up a stack.

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
text: The host port to the DSPs holds about two words; the emulator buffers thousands. A sender whose poll timed out left DSP1's handler armed, so the next stock send was shifted by two words. A loader interleaving its writes with the OS's put a thousand words at a wrong address. Send exactly as stock does (interrupts masked) and own the port for the whole transfer.

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
text: The per-step trigger loop is hot: a hook doing a table lookup and register save on every call froze the audio with 12-16 tracks triggering (CPU! lit). It was found only by a hardware bisect. Cache, then exit early.

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
text: Never remove stock DSP pacing. Replacing a 480-cycle DSP1 pad contributed to that freeze. Letting DSP2 skip ahead on silent tracks starved the ColdFire's stream and lost triggers.

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
text: No long `rep` on a DSP path: `rep #$600` (clearing 1,536 words) overran the CPU on the first P-I bass-drum trigger. Changing it to `rep #1` proved the cause; two stores per `do` pass fixed it. This is the same rule as on the Octatrack.

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
text: The stock DSP1 watchdog: DSP1 counts blocks that DSP2 delivered late. On the third in a row it stops the output DMA and spins, silent until a power cycle. Half a percent over budget for three blocks is enough.

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
text: DSP correctness traps: Nested `do` loops sharing an end address left state on the real hardware stack, and DSP2 hung. An inherited modulo register wrapped a 384-word clear into 32 words. DSP2 external RAM holds power-on garbage (the emulator reads zero), so init must clear everything it reads, and every block must write all 32 samples.

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
text: Machine ids 124-127 fall inside the OS's "control machine" range tests.

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
text: Pin data assumptions: after a firmware update, wavetable models went silent because older UW sample sets were shorter than the new build expected. Declare minimum lengths.

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
text: What the emulator does not show, in numbers: DSP56300 pipeline interlocks add a median ~26 % (12-47 % per model). Instruction-cache misses and wait states: 16 copies of one model fit in the emulator and stalled on the unit. The emulator's default 441-sample slicing invents host-port spins of ~13,000 cycles. Use 64- or 8-sample slices, and don't "fix" spins it invents.

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / DSP56300 pitfalls (from building custom machines)
text: `move #16,a` loads a fraction (`a1 = $100000`), not 16. Write integers into data-ALU registers in the long form `#>16`. Address registers and the ALU immediates (`cmp`, `add`, `sub`) take integers.

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / DSP56300 pitfalls (from building custom machines)
text: Moving an accumulator to memory saturates: `move b,a` limits, `tfr b,a` doesn't. After `and #mask,a` take `a1` explicitly.

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / DSP56300 pitfalls (from building custom machines)
text: The reference assembler (mborgerson/dsp56300) accepts overlapping `ORG`s silently, so validate its output before packing: one contiguous segment, inside its bank, no warnings, entry points inside. A DO loop's end label goes on the instruction after the last loop instruction. `[doc]`

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / OS update and recovery (Machinedrum)
text: The OS `.syx` carries flash from `0x4000` up (stock 1.63: 939,744 bytes), in 2+7+7-packed 64-byte packets with a checksum and two terminators. It never carries the 16 KiB boot sector.

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / OS update and recovery (Machinedrum)
text: The boot-ROM updater stages the whole image in RAM and checks it before the first erase, so an interrupted or corrupt transfer changes nothing. `[doc]` (code reading)

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / OS update and recovery (Machinedrum)
text: It refuses a version not newer than "140", and halts on one flash part ID.

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / OS update and recovery (Machinedrum)
text: An exporter must include everything up to the last non-`0xFF` byte below `0x100000`. Custom code near `0xFE000-0xFFFFF` sits after the blob chain, and stopping at the last blob boots with pointers into erased flash. `[doc]`

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / OS update and recovery (Machinedrum)
text: The trap: the OS rewrites the boot sector. On every boot, MainOS checks the magic word at flash `0x3FFE`. If it isn't `0x224B`, MainOS erases the boot sector and rewrites it from a copy embedded in MainOS. A modified OS that alters that check or that copy can destroy the updater on its first boot; after that only an external flash programmer helps. Same pattern as the A4 MK1, so rule A38 applies. `[doc]`

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / OS update and recovery (Machinedrum)
text: Recovery otherwise: enter the boot ROM's upgrade mode and send the stock `.syx` over DIN MIDI (the unit has no USB). Rule A36. `[doc]`

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Monomachine (thin)
text: Monomodule runs the Monomachine's own sound engine in an emulated DSP56300 and matches the hardware sample for sample. So the sound engine is DSP56300 code taken from the OS file (OS 1.32B, `Elektron_SFX6-60_OS1.32B.syx`). `[doc]` {monomodule}

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Monomachine (thin)
text: Board, as Gearmulator models it (joelanders' gearmulator-md-mm, which boots the unmodified MnM OS 1.32B on the same board model as the Machinedrum, `[emu]` {gearmulator-md-mm}): the same ColdFire MCF5206E (modelled at 40 MHz) and two DSP56300-family DSPs; the same address map: flash at `0x10000000` (8 MiB OS images for both machines), main RAM `0x200000-0x2fffff`, each DSP's HI08 host port at `0x500000` / `0x600000`, internal SRAM at `0x1000000`; the SFX-60 MKII keeps user DigiPRO waveforms in a 2 MiB flash window at `0x10200000`.

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Monomachine (thin)
text: What differs from the MD in that model: the ColdFire services the DSP host port through the hardware receive latch rather than the MD's HREQ-to-IRQ4 wire; the two DSPs are coupled by their own link handshake. These are emulator-level facts. Nothing in our sources has measured a unit's clocks. `[emu]`

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Monomachine (thin)
text: Custom OS saved-data hazard: em's firmware reclaims song slots for extended data (MnM: slots 13-24; MD: 13-32). Songs left in those slots are corrupted on boot, so back them up first. The same can happen with any mod that changes saved-data layouts (compare section E of AGENT-RULES). `[doc]` {ems-fw}

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Monomachine (thin)
text: em's firmware carries features from jmamma's MDX (new machines, tunings, LFO shapes, MIDI fixes) with credit. `[doc]` {ems-fw}

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Monomachine (thin)
text: Screen dump (ems-monomachine-firmware 26B09): the request `F0 00 20 3C 03 00 64 F7` returns 16 SysEx chunks of 7-bit-packed data, 64 bytes each once decoded: the native LCD bitmap, 128x64, 1 bit, column-major, bottom to top, MSB first. Whether stock 1.32B answers it is not stated. The firmware is now compressed, so boot is slower. `[doc]` {ems-mnm-changelog}
