text: The Monomachine's clocks and DSP budgets on a unit (only the emulator's board model exists).

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Open
text: The Machinedrum's hardware wait states per area (only two areas measured).

section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Open
text: Why arithmetic stalls cost so little on hardware while AGU interlocks cost about their estimate (the kit lists this as open).

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Platform
text: CPU: ColdFire MCF54415CMJ250 (chip marking read 2026-09-30): MCF5441x, V4 core with EMAC, 250 MHz, no separate DSP. All audio is ColdFire assembly. It is the same CPU family as Digitakt mk1, Digitone mk1, Rytm and A4; the Octatrack is the exception. The MCF54418 reference manual applies. `[hw]`

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Platform
text: Audio: 6 tracks, rendered per 32-sample block (0.67 ms) in the audio interrupt. The stock OS already takes about 77 % of each block, even when stopped, because all tracks and effects are computed every block. Peaks reach 99 % with heavy added engines. `[hw]`

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Platform
text: EMAC runs with MACSR = `0xa0` (signed fractional), and Unicorn gets it wrong (the same pitfall as Syntakt, Octatrack and DN2). The project ships its own EMAC model. `[doc]`

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Platform
text: Container: ELE3, text header plus section table (16-byte aligned), with a trailer of zero padding, 4 zero bytes and an HMAC-SHA256 at a 16-byte-aligned offset. The key is re-derived from the image itself, so checksums and HMAC can be recomputed. `[doc]`

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Recovery
text: The startup menu lives in flash that OS updates never write. Hold FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4 = OS UPGRADE, "READY TO RECEIVE". It listens to MIDI IN only, never USB.

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Recovery
text: Model:Cycles' MIDI IN is a 3.5 mm TRS jack (type A and B both work). A mono TS cable does not work. Use the supplied DIN adapter if your interface has DIN.

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Recovery
text: Takes 5-10 minutes; the unit restarts by itself.

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Recovery
text: If it stays on "RECEIVING..." a packet was lost: power cycle and send slower (Modded Cycles' flasher pace 1.4 by default, 2.0 when it fails). `[hw]`

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Free space and payloads
text: Free space is scarce. The project's main source of code room is freed sprite masks: Groups of byte-identical `0xFF` bitmap masks are each referenced by one 32-bit constant. Redirecting that constant to a kept copy renders identically and frees the others. 10 groups, 164 freeable masks, 104-1,024 bytes each. Never write into a kept copy. A registry tool tracks which mod owns which mask.

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Free space and payloads
text: Other `0xFF` caves are refused when stock code points into them.

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Free space and payloads
text: Large code is appended to the image and copied to SDRAM at boot by one shared boot hook (Syntakt engines and MACRO at `0x43000000`, Model-TG at `0x46700000`). A new payload joins the chain rather than adding its own hook. `[doc]`

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Free space and payloads
text: Settings that must survive a save go into proven-unused bytes of the pattern, project or sound structures (examples: pattern-track byte +512, sound slots 18/27/30/31), declared in a registry so that two mods cannot claim the same bytes. `[doc]`

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Free space and payloads
text: Syntakt engines run on a Model:Cycles: Modded Cycles reads them from a Syntakt 1.41/1.42 file at build time and places them as a payload. The Syntakt's CPU #2 and the Cycles' CPU are the same core family. `[doc]`

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Free space and payloads
text: The same OS can be installed on a Model:Samples; the project marks this route experimental. Returning from the Cycles OS on a Samples needs a MIDI interface. `[doc]`

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Load and USB lessons from Supermodel / Modded Cycles (AveyCole, OS 1.13; notes 23 and 35, in French)
text: Every stock voice is rendered every block, playing or not: about 7,600 instructions each, so six idle voices cost ~45,800 per block. Stock audio takes ~77 % of the CPU at rest, measured on a unit with a diagnostic load counter (the same figure as in Modded-Cycles' notes). Skipping silent voices cut 77 % of the voice-loop instructions in the emulator; the unit test is still open. `[hw]` / `[emu]`

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Load and USB lessons from Supermodel / Modded Cycles (AveyCole, OS 1.13; notes 23 and 35, in French)
text: Ported Syntakt engines cost about the same instructions as stock voices (-7 % to +43 %), yet three or more made the unit slow and glitchy. The likely cause is their much larger memory footprint (cache misses), which the emulator does not time. Another case of rule A34. `[hw]` (symptoms) / `[?]` (cause)

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Load and USB lessons from Supermodel / Modded Cycles (AveyCole, OS 1.13; notes 23 and 35, in French)
text: Units report peaks of 101-108 % of the block budget, with clicks, while the average sits around 73-77 %. Peaks, not averages, decide. `[hw]`

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Load and USB lessons from Supermodel / Modded Cycles (AveyCole, OS 1.13; notes 23 and 35, in French)
text: Stock voices start accumulating into ACC0 without clearing it, so they rely on an empty accumulator at entry. Leave ACC0 at 0 (as on the Syntakt). `[emu]`

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Load and USB lessons from Supermodel / Modded Cycles (AveyCole, OS 1.13; notes 23 and 35, in French)
text: USB multitrack glitches (reported on Reddit after 15-20 minutes): Cause: the OS sends each block to USB right after rendering it, and the 6-channel mod's queue tolerated only 0.2 ms of jitter. With variable engine load (muted tracks, effects off) frames went missing. Fix: send at a fixed time at the start of the next interrupt, align the queue at start-up, and use a 9-slot ring instead of 8. Zero defects in the simulator afterwards. General rule for USB streaming mods: decouple the send time from a variable render time. `[emu]` (cause read in the OS, fix simulated)

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / A load governor that works, and one that didn't (Supermodel notes 30 and 36, Model:Cycles OS 1.13)
text: Thresholds seen on units: the sound crackles when a block nears 100 % of its time; a single block at 91 % did *not* crackle; the UI was still fluid at ~86 % sustained load and slows above that. `[hw]`

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / A load governor that works, and one that didn't (Supermodel notes 30 and 36, Model:Cycles OS 1.13)
text: Mistake 1: reacting to one heavy block. Peaks are isolated: a step where several tracks start (the sequencer takes up to ~7 % of a block), or caches the UI flushed between blocks (+4.6 points). By the time the governor sees such a block, it is already over; cutting a voice can't rescue it and is audible. The fix reacts only to a peak that lasts two blocks, or to sustained load. On a unit: "works well", 6 tracks with effects at 89 % peak / 78 % average, no crackle. `[hw]`

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / A load governor that works, and one that didn't (Supermodel notes 30 and 36, Model:Cycles OS 1.13)
text: Mistake 2: an integer moving average that never moves. `slow += (load - slow) >> 8` with load and average in whole percent rounds every step to 0, or to -1 below the average. The "sustained load" rule therefore never fired on a unit. The emulator test hid it because it pre-set the average. Keep fixed-point averages in scaled units (e.g. load << 8), and test them from a cold start. `[emu]`

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / A load governor that works, and one that didn't (Supermodel notes 30 and 36, Model:Cycles OS 1.13)
text: Mistake 3: stealing the quietest voice before the mixer. That ignores track volume, sends and mute, so a naturally quiet but loud-mixed track (hi-hat, a long tail) always went first, and a muted but still computed track was never preferred. Pick by audibility after the mixer, and prefer muted tracks. `[doc]`

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / A load governor that works, and one that didn't (Supermodel notes 30 and 36, Model:Cycles OS 1.13)
text: EMAC wrappers are not free: wrapping the reverb kernels in helpers that saved ACC3 and MACSR around every product cost +20-48 % instructions. Save the EMAC state once per block. `[emu]`

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / A load governor that works, and one that didn't (Supermodel notes 30 and 36, Model:Cycles OS 1.13)
text: Finding the worst block on the unit (note 217, results pending): Seven markers in the audio interrupt read the DMA timer (`0xFC07000C`), and the stages of the worst block are kept for display. One block is 90,112 timer ticks. The same method as digihealth (Digitakt mk1) and dnfw's loadmap (DN2): measure before optimising. `[doc]`

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / MIDI map, voice internals and SOLID (model27 notes 65, 71-73, OS 1.13, 2026-11-11)
text: CC lookup (Model:Cycles): the CC-to-descriptor table is built at `0x4005a8ce`; CC 16-23 are looked up only in the row of the track's machine, so a shared descriptor on CC 20-23 is never reached, while CC 75-78 reach shared descriptors on all six tracks (`[emu]`, interpreter). CC values are not scaled: the handler `0x4000b568` writes value x 256 and the setter `0x4000b274` clamps to the descriptor's range. Edits send their CC through `0x4000b942`, which reads the stock table at `0x4010dce0`. `[doc]`

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / MIDI map, voice internals and SOLID (model27 notes 65, 71-73, OS 1.13, 2026-11-11)
text: Stock MIDI map (Model:Cycles): CCs that reach a track descriptor: 3, 7, 10, 12-19, 65-67, 70, 80, 93 (Solo, by code reading), 102-110; on the FX channel 3, 14, 15, 85-88, 102-110. Stock NRPNs: 1:26-1:30, 1:32-1:39, 3:0, 1:100-1:103. Free next to 74/71: CC 72, 73, 75-79. `[doc]`

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / MIDI map, voice internals and SOLID (model27 notes 65, 71-73, OS 1.13, 2026-11-11)
text: Model:Samples knob CCs from its descriptor table at `0x40109048`: Pitch 16, Loop 17, Flip 18, Start 19, Length 20, Cutoff 74, Reso 71, Decay 80. `[doc]` (code reading, not run)

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / MIDI map, voice internals and SOLID (model27 notes 65, 71-73, OS 1.13, 2026-11-11)
text: No CC goes out for a knob until TRACK SETUP MOUT is on for that track (with ENCS at I+E); stock behaviour, not a bug. `[hw]`

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / MIDI map, voice internals and SOLID (model27 notes 65, 71-73, OS 1.13, 2026-11-11)
text: Voice internals (Model:Cycles): amp envelope `0x400a9252`, decay table `0x4011d84c` (DECAY 127 is about 15 s to -60 dB); the VCA `0x400a9430` clears the level in a trig's block, which clicks on a retrig; PUNCH `0x400a967a` (with PUNCH off a TONE track's output is x1/8); the voice loop `0x400a7d4a` keeps trig and release flags for one block only, runs the EMAC with MACSR `0xa0` and leaves acc0 uncleared; per-track velocity gain at `0x40fe4c90 + 2*track`. `[doc]`

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / MIDI map, voice internals and SOLID (model27 notes 65, 71-73, OS 1.13, 2026-11-11)
text: Cost per 32-frame block in Unicorn (instructions, not cycles): TONE 5,291, PERC 6,079, METAL 6,431, KICK 7,429, SNARE 7,158, CHORD 8,300; model27's SOLID (an eight-mode struck-body machine on the EMAC) 3,588 for one ringing voice, 51,589 for six tracks of sustained noise. `[emu]`

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / MIDI map, voice internals and SOLID (model27 notes 65, 71-73, OS 1.13, 2026-11-11)
text: On a unit (2026-11-11): SOLID with every other model27 card ran on a Model:Cycles; six SOLID tracks, each with a Track FX, and POTS on the delay send averaged about 60 % CPU with peaks up to 75 %. Track FX answered CC 75/76 and NRPN 1:22/1:23. `[hw]`

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / MIDI map, voice internals and SOLID (model27 notes 65, 71-73, OS 1.13, 2026-11-11)
text: Where SOLID sits: at `0x43000000` when it is the only added machine (13,216 bytes of code, 2,832 of variables), or as machine 7 at `0x43009680` beside SAMPLE; this is the same SDRAM payload area the Syntakt engines and MACRO use ([RAM-TENANCY.md](../RAM-TENANCY.md)). It takes 80 bytes of the shared freed mask at `0x4016cae8`, now 1,016 of 1,024 bytes used. `[doc]`

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / The +Drive sample store (model27's sample uploader, OS 1.13)
text: A sample in use is locked. Once a track uses a sample, the Model:Cycles refuses to delete it; a restart unlocks it only if no track uses it anymore (tried on a Model:Cycles with one SAMPLE track, 2026-11-10). An uploader should delete what it can and name the locked files rather than stop. `[hw]`

section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / The +Drive sample store (model27's sample uploader, OS 1.13)
text: Uploads become 48 kHz mono samples; Chromium decodes neither AIFF nor 64-bit float WAV, so model27's page converts those itself before handing them on. `[doc]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Silicon
text: CPU: ColdFire MCF5445x (board photos read MCF54454VR266 or MCF5445AVR266), 32-bit big-endian. The firmware stores 264 MHz; internal bus 132 MHz (UARTs, PIT, DSPI), FlexBus 66 MHz, 24 MHz crystal. 128 MB SDRAM at `0x40000000`; NOR flash on CS0, 8 MB decode. `[hw]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Silicon
text: Audio DSP: Freescale Symphony DSP56721, two DSP5636x cores in one chip, 200 MHz each, with no external memory. Each core has its own P memory. A 64 K-word shared window at `$030000` is reachable by both cores; P, X and Y alias there. Tracks 1-4 run on core 1 and tracks 5-8 on core 0 ("inverted from old assumptions"). Each track's FX1 and FX2 run on its own core. `[hw]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Silicon
text: Storage: CompactFlash (FAT16/32) through an ATA stack (PIO task-file registers at `0x90000000`).

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Silicon
text: The kernel is a proprietary preemptive microkernel (banner "ElektronOctatrack DPS-1"), not FreeRTOS.

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Cycle budget (measured with a burn probe on units)
text: 4,532 cycles per sample per core at 44.1 kHz (199.9 MHz measured). The older 4,160 / 183 MHz is retracted.

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Cycle budget (measured with a burn probe on units)
text: About 3,120 cycles/sample are usable for DSP work; stock takes ~1,410.

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Cycle budget (measured with a burn probe on units)
text: Planning number: ~500 cycles on top of the current reverb with 4 FX1 FILTERs, ~900 with 2. One FX1 FILTER costs 192 cycles/sample. `[hw]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Cycle budget (measured with a burn probe on units)
text: Stock FX2 costs per sample (one MKII, 1.40C), dearest first: DJ EQ ~340, LO-FI ~310, SPRING ~300, CHORUS ~295, FILTER ~285, DARK ~255, PLATE ~250, PHASER ~240, EQUALIZER ~190, FLANGER ~145, COMB ~125, COMPRESSOR ~100, SPATIALIZER ~80, DELAY ~0. `[hw]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Cycle budget (measured with a burn probe on units)
text: Words are not cycles: `move x0,a` 2 cycles, a one-word displaced `move x:(r7+$15),a` ~4, a two-word displaced ~6. Static word counts are a floor; only a burn sweep measures the ceiling. `[hw]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Cycle budget (measured with a burn probe on units)
text: ColdFire access costs (one unit, 132 MHz, inside the frame interrupt, stock cache settings): register/SRAM/cache hit ~2.9 ns, uncached SDRAM store 36 ns, load 69 ns, cache miss ~80 ns, `cpushl` 46-80 ns. SRAM is 12-28x cheaper than SDRAM, and caching a transmit buffer does not help. `[hw]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Cycle budget (measured with a burn probe on units)
text: USB costs: one recording buffer is about 6 points of the ColdFire's frame share, USB streaming about 12. Six buffers plus streaming drop frames. `[hw]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / FX slots
text: Every track runs `FX1 -> FX2 -> gain`. FX1 has 3,072 words of Y, FX2 16,384, which is why reverbs and delay are FX2-only.

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / FX slots
text: Both menus share one DSP dispatch table indexed by the raw id. A module on a stock effect's id replaces that effect in both slots, and removing an effect from a menu frees no space. The reclaimable pool is FX1's ten effects, 3,384 words. `[doc]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / OS format, update and recovery
text: Elektron ships the same OS as `.bin` and `.syx` (the MKI and MKII files are byte-identical for 1.40C). `.bin` = ELUP header + seed + XOR-feedback-obfuscated `[len] + ELEK(aPLib(MAIN OS))` + checksum. `.syx` = SysEx-packed ELEK container. The MAIN OS is 1,112,560 B. No cryptographic signature in any layer. `[doc]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / OS format, update and recovery
text: Validation on update returns: -1 IO, -2 not a valid OS, -3 length (more than 1 MB + 12 B), -4 checksum, -5 MK1 not allowed (version code below "0156"), -6 cannot downgrade (below "0178"). octabam images keep code 0178. `[doc]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / OS format, update and recovery
text: The card path: OS UPGRADE lists `/*.BIN` on the CF, validates, programs NOR from `0x4000` and verifies it word by word. Stock then shows "PLEASE REBOOT!" and never resets the unit itself.

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / OS format, update and recovery
text: Recovery: hold FUNC at power-on, TRIG 3 = MIDI UPGRADE (not TRIG 4 as on the small boxes), send the stock `.syx` over DIN MIDI. `TRIG 2` (EMPTY RESET) clears battery-backed RAM and settings, not the card. Pace about 7,460 messages at DIN rate. Filter MIDI clock on that port and merge nothing else into it: a MIDI-hub preset caused a CHECKSUM ERROR. If the unit loses sync, send again slower (60-300 ms between messages). The unit may update its bootstrap after the flash. `[hw]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / OS format, update and recovery
text: How stock writes NOR (1.40C, Modwerk's reading, `[doc]` {modwerk-ot-traps}): OS UPGRADE reads the whole card file into RAM, then erases and programs NOR from there (sector erase `0x40020628`, 256-byte page program `0x400206f4`, the 37 sector starts listed at `0x400a95c0`). The layout is 8 KB boot sectors from `0x4000`, then 64 KB sectors up to `0x1f0000`. Both routines poll the chip themselves and mask interrupts only around the command bytes, so a mod can call them from a task without breaking the frame interrupt. The bootloader below `0x4000` is never written. It depacks NOR from `0x4012` without checking anything, so an image that doesn't boot is recoverable over DIN MIDI only. The startup menu's MIDI UPGRADE checks the received file, not NOR. `[hw]` (testers' units)

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / OS format, update and recovery
text: Don't verify a running image against its own RAM: once running, stock rewrites bytes inside its bootloader copy (`0x400e201e-0x400e2108`) and reuses the RAM after the image. Compare against digests taken before stock started. `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-traps}

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / OS format, update and recovery
text: After flashing a build that changes an effect's parameter layout, old projects need their stored values stamped. A select value outside its count stalls the sequencer on first play. `[hw]` ([I28](../INCIDENTS.md#i28-a-select-value-outside-its-count-stalled-the-sequencer))

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Memory and code placement
text: The free ROM is small: zero runs in `0x400c0000-0x400d8000` total ~8.4 KB, shared by every mod. The zero region above `0x400d8000` is the PROJECT subsystem's RAM. A menu table placed in a 15 KB zero run at `0x401087e4` crashed a unit. ([I48](../INCIDENTS.md#i48-a-menu-table-in-a-free-zero-run-crashed-the-unit)) Larger code goes to a loader-copied area: octabam's loader is a stub at `0x4010fdf0`, right after the OS image, reached from the boot site. `[hw]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Memory and code placement
text: DSP code that does not fit a core's P memory (ends `P:0x1fff`) runs from the shared window `P:0x30000-0x3ffff`. This was proven on a unit (PEXT probe, 2026-10-25). `[hw]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Memory and code placement
text: DSP scratch: r7 scratch `$00-$83` is the per-instance block, and `$84+` hangs the unit. Stock effects scratch `X:0x20-0xff`, and the hardware dispatcher passes the audio block at X:0. `[hw]` ([I29](../INCIDENTS.md#i29-dsp-scratch-at-84-and-up-hung-the-unit))

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / DSP56300 assembler and emulator traps (from octabam's trap register; each cost real work)
text: `dsp_asm` silently mis-encodes: `tfr a,b` as `rnd b`, and any `mpy` operand order it does not know as `mpysu`. `lua (rN+d),rM` takes d in -64..63 and silently wraps larger values. Labels resolve by prefix, so a new label may not have an existing label as its prefix.

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / DSP56300 assembler and emulator traps (from octabam's trap register; each cost real work)
text: DSP56300 semantics: A logical op on an accumulator leaves the extension byte stale, so the next store saturates to full scale. `move a,b` limits; `tfr a,b` moves all 56 bits. A Tcc pair sharing one compare breaks with any arithmetic in between. `asr #n,a,a` shifts into a0, and Z is set only when all 56 bits are zero. Reading a0 exposes the fractional left shift that a1 hides.

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / DSP56300 assembler and emulator traps (from octabam's trap register; each cost real work)
text: No `rep` in an effect's init or proc (it cannot be interrupted, and the host-command handlers need to run). No dense X work in a DMA's 8K block.

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / DSP56300 assembler and emulator traps (from octabam's trap register; each cost real work)
text: Instruction-form rule, as on the SHARC: a DSP form ships only if a stock payload runs it or a hardware probe approved it.

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / DSP56300 assembler and emulator traps (from octabam's trap register; each cost real work)
text: Stock Unicorn halves every ColdFire fractional-mode multiply and adds where `msac` subtracts (the firmware runs EMAC with MACSR = 0x20), and its MAC-with-load decode has three defects. MACSR S/U is bit 6, and in fractional mode it selects 16-bit rounding. These are the same EMAC pitfalls as on the Syntakt and DN2 (rule G-series, `common/toolchain-and-emulators.md`). `[hw]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / DSP56300 assembler and emulator traps (from octabam's trap register; each cost real work)
text: The emulator (`ot_emu`) charges one step per instruction, with no cache or memory timing. A change can be cycle-identical in the port and several percent worse on the unit.

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / USB device side (both octabam and Modwerk, measured on units)
text: No EP0 reply or OUT data stage may be a whole multiple of 64 bytes. A reply of 64/128/192/256 bytes left a stale zero-length packet, and the next request returned 0 bytes (once, the unit froze). Stock leaves zero-length termination on in the EP0 OUT queue head, so a 128- or 192-byte OUT stage never completed. Send one byte less, or clear ZLT when priming. `[hw]` Rule A39. ([I5](../INCIDENTS.md#i5-ep0-data-stages-of-a-multiple-of-64-bytes-stall-or-freeze-stock-usb-driver))

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / USB device side (both octabam and Modwerk, measured on units)
text: About one EP0 OUT stage in 50-100 goes unanswered on a MKII: completed inside the ISR after stock's poll, or stopped part-way. Modwerk runs a 60 Hz tick that finishes a completed stage, or stalls EP0 after 0.5 s so the host resubmits. `[hw]` ([I6](../INCIDENTS.md#i6-about-one-ep0-out-stage-in-50-100-goes-unanswered))

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / USB device side (both octabam and Modwerk, measured on units)
text: DMA reads RAM, not the copyback cache. A value the CPU stores rarely stayed stale for minutes in USB replies, while values stored every frame looked live. Copy a reply through the uncached alias and send it from there. `[hw]` (Same idea as A28 on the SHARC.) ([I35](../INCIDENTS.md#i35-usb-replies-stayed-stale-for-minutes))

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / USB device side (both octabam and Modwerk, measured on units)
text: A soft reset leaves the USB controller and PHY as they were: one RAM boot in about six came back with no USB until a power cycle. Stop the controller (USBCMD.RS = 0) and wait ~50 ms before resetting; that gave 20 of 20 good boots. `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-traps} ([I7](../INCIDENTS.md#i7-a-soft-reset-leaves-the-usb-controller-running))

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / USB device side (both octabam and Modwerk, measured on units)
text: Never post key events into stock's queues directly (two crashes minutes later). Feed the panel parser its own bytes instead. `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-traps} ([I30](../INCIDENTS.md#i30-key-events-posted-into-stocks-queues-crashed-the-unit-minutes-later))

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / ColdFire load (Modwerk's meter on a MKII, Oct 2026)
text: The Modwerk base with nothing installed shows ~42-47 % CPU. That is mostly stock's own tasks; there is no clean stock baseline yet. `[hw]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / ColdFire load (Modwerk's meter on a MKII, Oct 2026)
text: An FM synth module costs ~8 points just by being installed, plus ~5 while a track plays it. Small effects cost 0.5 points or less on the ColdFire, but their DSP cost lands on their core (BBD on T6: core T5-8 went from ~44 % to 54 %). `[hw]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / ColdFire load (Modwerk's meter on a MKII, Oct 2026)
text: Uncached module code is expensive: Analog BD on one track cost ~20 points. 93 % of each call was a write lease whose owner check read the module header through the uncached alias (~0.6 µs a read). With one lease per frame it dropped to ~10 points. Lesson: take locks only where a call writes, at most once a frame, and keep uncached reads out of hot paths. `[hw]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / ColdFire load (Modwerk's meter on a MKII, Oct 2026)
text: UI-task edits can cost milliseconds: a 64-step MIDI rewrite took 3.9 ms per knob turn, mostly stock's lock-index rebuild. Updating only the own track's bits brought it to 0.5 ms. Audio frames stayed ~406-417 µs apart throughout, because it all ran on the UI task. `[hw]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / ColdFire load (Modwerk's meter on a MKII, Oct 2026)
text: The DSP peak meter shows the busiest single frame of a 1,024-frame window. A self-test or sync leaves it at ~99.7 % while the mean is flat and the audio fine. Judge overload by the longest frame of a real load, not the peak. `[hw]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / ColdFire load (Modwerk's meter on a MKII, Oct 2026)
text: Frame budget from the field (Modwerk beta, 2026-11-08): audio frames are 363 µs apart (16 samples), and the DSPs starve once a gap passes about 515 µs. A unit left stopped and connected for about 23 hours with 6 modules showed 42 % CPU and a longest gap of 423 µs, with no freeze. `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-beta}

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / ColdFire load (Modwerk's meter on a MKII, Oct 2026)
text: Settled: the silence after USB DISK MODE was Modwerk's, not stock's (finding 72, 2026-11-10): stock pauses the DSP while USB DISK MODE is open; Modwerk's base took that pause for a stalled DSP, and its recovery kept the audio stopped until a power cycle. Fixed in the base; on the owner's MKII (1.40C) PROJ > USB DISK MODE, about 10 s, NO, PLAY now plays. Not tested: the walk on a flashed base, a file copy in that mode, an OS upgrade from the card. A mod that watches for DSP stalls must tell stock's own pauses from a stall (rule C12: it was never reproduced on a stock unit). `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-unit-1110}

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / ColdFire load (Modwerk's meter on a MKII, Oct 2026)
text: Field stalls with modules (Modwerk beta, 8-10 Nov): stalls still come within about a minute of installs or restores, before any module code is placed (finding 71), and on a heavy self-test Part (FILTER and DELAY on every track plus FLANGER and PHASER) 1 run in 21 stalled on the live base, 0 in 5 on the lighter Part; only a power cycle recovered. The base's longest fully masked span measured about 14 µs, far under the roughly 200 µs that stops core 0, so masked ColdFire code is unlikely but not ruled out for the stall itself. One field crash record: vector 3 inside a module's ColdFire code. A unit with 6 modules stayed up 70 hours (longest frame gap 424 µs). `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-beta-1110} {modwerk-ot-unit-1110}

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / More DSP and boot traps (measured on units)
text: An effect's `init` must preserve r1: the FX1 dispatcher keeps the effect id there and calls `proc` through it. An init that moved r1 jumped to the reset vector and killed the core at project load. octabam's build refuses an init that writes r1/n1/m1. `[hw]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / More DSP and boot traps (measured on units)
text: A persistent slot that `init` does not clear holds the previous effect's leftovers. The emulator boots with zeroed RAM and cannot show it. `[hw]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / More DSP and boot traps (measured on units)
text: Resident window code must sit in `0x33da3..0x37eff`: payload B's boot loop clears `Y:0x37f00..0x3ffff`, and DARK REV writes up to `0x33da2`. `[emu]` (both cores faulted at boot in the port)

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / More DSP and boot traps (measured on units)
text: A DSP frame counter past `$7fffff` saturates in `move a,nN`, which stopped a frame engine after 50.7 minutes. Mask counters to 23 bits. `[hw]` ([I32](../INCIDENTS.md#i32-a-dsp-frame-counter-saturated-after-507-minutes))

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / More DSP and boot traps (measured on units)
text: Core 1's load-meter counter is at `X:$2840` on Modwerk USB bases; module state there gave a jittery pitch. `[hw]` ([I33](../INCIDENTS.md#i33-module-state-on-a-load-meter-counter-gave-a-jittery-pitch))

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / More DSP and boot traps (measured on units)
text: Cold starts: an early-startup change passed emulator boots and quick power cycles but stalled at the logo after several minutes powered off. Keeping the activation helper resident in the OS image fixed it; the mechanism is unknown. Qualify startup changes after a long power-off (rule A40). `[hw]` ([I34](../INCIDENTS.md#i34-a-startup-change-stalled-at-the-logo-after-a-long-power-off))

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / More DSP and boot traps (measured on units)
text: A write-watch on cached addresses is blind to a clear through the uncached alias. A "free 8.8 MB" region turned out to be the stock delay rings. Before trusting a null result, ask what the instrument cannot see (rule A31). `[emu]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / From KYOTI (Zac-Kyoti/octatrack-kyoti-fw, OS 1.40C)
text: A core's crash threshold, found on hardware in KYOTI's own cost model: stock's heaviest effects plus the sidechain compressor model at ~3,516 cycles per sample. The core crashed somewhere between ~3,760 and ~3,830. With DJ EQ in both slots on T5-T8, one extra REPITCH voice (~240) was clean; adding a second (RPS9 ~77 or RPSP ~240) crashed. KYOTI's bar: a feature must not break any configuration that is clean on stock. So beside stock's heaviest effects a core has room for about one heavy voice. Note that these "modelled cycles" are KYOTI's estimate, not octabam's measured 4,532 cycles per sample. Compare figures only within one model. `[hw]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / From KYOTI (Zac-Kyoti/octatrack-kyoti-fw, OS 1.40C)
text: The DSP shared window in work RAM is volatile: at boot, `0x401086f4` is copied to `0x80000000` (`0x3e88` bytes) and the rest is zero-filled up to `0x80004000`. Nothing of yours survives there across a boot. `[doc]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / From KYOTI (Zac-Kyoti/octatrack-kyoti-fw, OS 1.40C)
text: One image for MKI and MKII: the OS probes `0x46c8d18c` and shows 15 (MKI) or 16 (MKII) PERSONALIZE items. `[doc]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / From KYOTI (Zac-Kyoti/octatrack-kyoti-fw, OS 1.40C)
text: KYOTI keeps a merged, confidence-tagged 1.40C address map (`reference/kb/memory-map.md`) that cross-references octabam. It is a good second reading. `[doc]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Debugging on the unit by writing a log to the CF card (OctaMax, MKII, OS 1.40C)
text: When the emulator cannot run the code you need to see (here, the EMAC-heavy frame builder), log from the unit itself. OctaMax added two detours that call the firmware's own file primitives (open `0x40016864`, write `0x400166b8`, close `0x4001677c`, sprintf `0x40013a08`) and write `/HOTDBG.TXT` to the CF card. Pull the card and read it. It works on hardware, and it showed that values seeded in the emulator had been guessed wrong (a voice type byte of 1, not 4). `[hw]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Debugging on the unit by writing a log to the CF card (OctaMax, MKII, OS 1.40C)
text: The DSP never plays on its own: every frame the ColdFire builds a per-voice packet in shared RAM (double buffer at `0x80000000`, selector `0x800000e0`) and pokes the DSP. A voice that stops being fed goes silent without any "stop". `[doc]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Debugging on the unit by writing a log to the CF card (OctaMax, MKII, OS 1.40C)
text: Recorder buffers live in a paged RAM pool (base `0x40a955e0`, ~89 MB) that survives a project change; the voices are torn down and rebuilt by the load. `[hw]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Debugging on the unit by writing a log to the CF card (OctaMax, MKII, OS 1.40C)
text: Restoring state every frame is safe only for CPU-side bookkeeping. Overwriting data the DSP reads corrupted the audio. `[hw]` ([I31](../INCIDENTS.md#i31-restoring-dsp-read-state-every-frame-corrupted-the-audio))

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Debugging on the unit by writing a log to the CF card (OctaMax, MKII, OS 1.40C)
text: An Octatrack emulator built on QEMU (ColdFire MCF54455) plus dsp56300, octemu by markandrus, targets firmware development including USB MIDI and audio; PassOS uses its 20-channel USB audio work. `[doc]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Where code and data may go: KYOTI's cave ledger (OS 1.40C, `reference/kb/caves.md`)
text: The parameter-page descriptor table is live data, zeros included. It is 31 entries of `0x192` bytes at `0x400d2e52-0x400d5f00`, and a zero entry means "the default". Never place code or data there unless the entry is proven unreachable. `[hw]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Where code and data may go: KYOTI's cave ledger (OS 1.40C, `reference/kb/caves.md`)
text: The canary test (from octalab) before anything ships in a new region: 1. Fill the range with a pattern, or a 32-bit counter so that partial overwrites show. 2. Use the unit for a full session: load, record, change patterns, save, power-cycle, load again. 3. Read the range back and compare. octamax lost tables to a heap tail and probe counters to a region restored on every load. See rule A43. `[hw]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Where code and data may go: KYOTI's cave ledger (OS 1.40C, `reference/kb/caves.md`)
text: Scratch RAM `0x80006a40+` is not safe under live audio: a magic word at `0x80006a60` was overwritten by the next key press on a real MKI while recording; the emulator, which runs no DSP/audio path, kept it forever. `[hw]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Where code and data may go: KYOTI's cave ledger (OS 1.40C, `reference/kb/caves.md`)
text: Past the image's ceiling, two routes: append a runtime after the OS image (octabam's loader stub; proven on an MKI); put a position-independent payload with a relocation table on the CF card and load it at run time. octemu does this for USB audio (four UAC2 descriptors, iso servicing and a 36 KB ring against ~408 B of slack). `[doc]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
text: AMP envelope: the DSP's AMP envelope restarts from zero at every trig START, so with any ATK above 0 a sound that plays across trigs drops out and fades back in, a click on every note. A ColdFire machine holds the DSP at ATK 0 / HOLD INF / REL INF and shapes AMP itself, as SYNTH MACHINE does. Measured laws (Tim Hastie): ATK is a linear ramp of 3.85 ms x 2^(ATK/8.53), at least 16 frames; REL is exponential with tau 0.295 ms x 2^(REL/8.53). `[hw]` {octabam-wavecf} (I58)

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
text: Crossfader: stock maps the crossfader through one table of 128 Q15 values at `0x400bcd90`; the panel handler `0x40061e40` and the MIDI CC 48 handler `0x400626ba` rebuild the per-track weights at `0x80003c60` from it. Replacing the table changes scene locks, XVOL and the morph alike; MIDI SCENES mixes linearly on its own. `[hw]` {octabam-xfcurve}

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
text: Demand loading: the loader copies a whole effect block (MODULATION, 1,561 words, an estimated ~31k of the 72,512 cycles in a frame) inside one DSP frame hook; the DSP-busy meter reads 99.7 % in that window `[hw]`. The frame interrupt has two waits with no time limit (the loader's wait before each host word, and stock's spin at `0x4000ab26` until the DSP takes the frame's `0x8c` host command); if the DSP stops taking host words, the ColdFire can spin forever `[?]` {octabam-dl} (I57, H22).

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
text: CF write throughput (STEM REC, MKII): write time per KB grows with the number of files written at once: 54-92 us/KB for one file, 423 us/KB for eleven (212 after writing whole 32 KB clusters only). Samples streamed by Static machines from the same card slow writes further (252 -> 387 us/KB for ten files); eleven 24-bit files need 2.9 MB/s. `[hw]` {octabam-stemrec}

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
text: Test host: octabam's hardware tools run on Linux and on WSL2 with usbipd; MIDI, transport and the load meter work there, but USB-audio capture over usbip delivered only about a quarter of the frames. `[hw]` {octabam-hwtest}

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
text: Key bus (Modwerk): the key bus moved from Y `$800-$9FF` to Y `$7E00-$7FFF` on each core, the tail of the first internal FX2 slot, which frees Y `$7F0-$9FF` for a DSP machine's voice. An FX2 effect that fills the whole 16,384-word buffer is then refused on T1/T5; Mini Verb, E-Verb (15,870 words) and BBD still fit. A keyed duck lands within one 5 ms window of the kick, on the same core and across cores; in the DSP simulator the cross-core key arrives exactly two blocks late. Four RINGMOD SC plus four BBD while playing: CPU 85.1 %, core peaks 66/74.5 %. `[hw]` (MKI 2026-10-30, MKII 2026-11-10), memory survey `[emu]` {modwerk-ot-keybus}

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
text: Module cost (Modwerk survey): module DSP code runs at 1.4-1.7 cycles per instruction against about 1 for stock, and installed but unused modules add frame-interrupt time (23.3 % -> 28.2 % stopped with 26 installed). `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-options}

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
text: Internal SRAM has no free holes: `0x80000000-0x80008000` is the program's `.data`/`.bss`, filled at boot from the image tail; `0x80006964-0x80007574` is the work buffer of the stock audio-analysis task, which writes up to 768 words from `0x80006974`. This explains the KYOTI scratch-word loss at `0x80006a60`. OCTAMAX keeps patch state in DDR at `0x40af0000-0x40af0600`, inside a reserve stock never references, cleared by its boot stub. `[hw]` {octamax-notes} (I59; boot-fill extent disputed, CONFLICTS O23)

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
text: Sequencer state: current bank/pattern at `0x800065bd/be`, the cued pair at `0x800065bf/c0` ("nothing cued" when both pairs are equal); cueing the playing pattern cancels in stock, and a switch to the same pattern is a restart with no Part reload. Active bank `0x80000002`, active Part `0x80000003` (disputed, O23); whole-Part apply `0x40009094`. `[hw]` {octamax-notes}

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
text: Step timing (KYOTI): the sequencer schedules each step one step ahead, so a Part change sent to the engine in the landing tick sounds a step early; a per-track apply must wait one of the track's steps `[hw]`. The whole-Part apply posts a kernel message and belongs on the UI task; a storage job's done-callback runs on the UI task, which ticks at 1/60 s `[emu]`. Copies with interrupts masked click (I60). {kyoti-reload}

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam findings (2026-11-11)

The module now refuses a seventh instance. `[hw]` {octabam-cxosc}

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam findings (2026-11-11)
text: Stock icon blit (`0x400128a8`, a 13-row column word with mask `0xfff80000`): bit 31 is the bottom row and bit 19 the top, so a left shift moves the picture down. Five flashes went into one pixel before this was written down. `[hw]` {octabam-traps}

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam findings (2026-11-11)
text: FLEX slices (DRUMMER, OS 1.40C): in slice mode the voice start `0x4000f450(track, slot, flags)` plays slice `min(STRT >> 1, count - 1)`; the slice table is 64 entries of 12 bytes from +312 of the FLEX slot record `0x100b14f0 + 0x448*slot` (octabam's own STORAGE note said 20 bytes; the code multiplies by 12). `[emu]` {octabam-drummer}

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam findings (2026-11-11)
text: Adding and moving trigs: the sequencer builds each step about 912 samples after the step counter changes, one step ahead; a detour right after the builder (`0x400a2d82`) can add a trig on an empty step or rewrite its micro-timing (one unit is 1/24 of a step). Locks staged for an added trig are ignored, and its lock block holds zeros at boot unless the mod fills it (all 32 lane values of the track went to 0 until DRUMMER wrote `0xff` there). `[emu]` {octabam-drummer} DRUMMER ran on the author's MKII from these sites; two bugs found after the first unit test are I72. `[hw]`

section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam findings (2026-11-11)

section: Syntakt / Recovery (SyntHack OS `RECOVERY.md`)
text: Mod data written for defaults slows project load and save (Synfact, OS 1.41): a user saw a project load slowly when switched to from another project and save more slowly than usual; a reboot straight into it loaded normally. The export was valid. The ARP mod wrote and sealed a 320-byte carrier for every kit even with default settings, so load checked all 1,664 bindings; leaving default carriers absent cut the emulated serialization from 24.8 M to 4.8 M instructions (81 % fewer). The slowness is a user report; the cost is `[emu]`, the wall-clock gain not yet measured. `[doc]` {synfact-lifecycle} ([I50](../INCIDENTS.md#i50-mod-data-written-for-default-settings-slowed-project-load-and-save))

This run recovered a working unit; recovery of a unit that does not boot is still untested. section: Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.41 static-analysis facts (Humgic/syntakt-machine45-research - README and handoff dated 2026-10-28; no hardware run, no firmware)
text: Address rule `VA = file offset + 0x40000400`; ColdFire big-endian (ISA-C/EMAC). MAIN is 3,438,480 bytes, section 7 is 383,760 bytes. `[doc]` {machine45-handoff}

section: Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.41 static-analysis facts (Humgic/syntakt-machine45-research - README and handoff dated 2026-10-28; no hardware run, no firmware)
text: Stock public Machine IDs are 0-44, stored as a BYTE in each track's machine payload (`P[t]+0xA2`); runtime records `R[t] = model + 0x6C + 0x3C0*t`, `P[t] = *(R[t]+0x10)`; the setter is at `0x40025594` (store at `0x40025620`). 505 parameter descriptors of 52 bytes; only MAIN digital tracks 0-7. `[doc]` {machine45-handoff}

section: Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.41 static-analysis facts (Humgic/syntakt-machine45-research - README and handoff dated 2026-10-28; no hardware run, no firmware)
text: Section 7 selector: a signed BYTE with a 46-entry map (negative -> 0, 0-45 kept, above 45 clamped to 45); stock maps 0-7 to the same-numbered engine family and 36->8, 37->9, 38->10, 44->11, everything else (incl. 45) to family 0. Stock tables: render pointers `0x400148F0` (12 entries), prep pointers `0x40014920`, the 46-byte map at `0x40014950`. A compact handoff moves MAIN `[0x80002000,0x800021B0)` through a 27x16-byte eDMA transfer (TCD47, channel 47); each track then receives a 20-byte copy into `T[t] = 0x80003C40 + 0x8E*t`. Dslot is 8 x `0x708` = 14,400 bytes. `[doc]` {machine45-handoff}

section: Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.41 static-analysis facts (Humgic/syntakt-machine45-research - README and handoff dated 2026-10-28; no hardware run, no firmware)
text: Persistence confirmed statically: the current-kit Sound-v7 save/load keeps the machine byte (raw 0-45 and 255 retained, 46-254 map to 0); Pattern-v11 stores the byte at row `+0x2EC` and its restoration is not closed; Sound locks, p-locks, held trigs, migration, clipboard and undo not qualified. Evidence labels in that repo: confirmed by static analysis / verified in emulator (none for the whole device) / verified on hardware (none) / hypothesis. `[doc]` {machine45-handoff}

section: Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.41 static-analysis facts (Humgic/syntakt-machine45-research - README and handoff dated 2026-10-28; no hardware run, no firmware)
text: Open: safe executable storage for native DSP on "CPU 2" (the loader boundary is unresolved); composition with SY FM4 (engine 4, A-table entry overlap) and other descriptor mods; resource IDs 254-261 are unclaimed in the registry but have MIDI CCs, 505+ have no native allocation. `[doc]` {machine45-handoff}

section: Syntakt / Platform: two ColdFires, an FPGA, an analog mixer (SyntHack OS docs, OS 1.41)
text: Two ColdFire MCF5441x (V4, EMAC, no FPU, ~250 MHz, so 166,667 cycles per 32-sample block), with 64 KB SRAM at `0x80000000`. RAM shared between the CPUs is at `0x10000000`. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / Platform: two ColdFires, an FPGA, an analog mixer (SyntHack OS docs, OS 1.41)
text: Sections of OS 1.41, stored in the order 5, 2, 1, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8: | Section | Content | Size | Note | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | FPGA bitstream | 149,516 B | never touch | | 2 | bootstrap with the STARTUP menu | 30,782 B | never touch | | 3 | MAIN OS for CPU #1, at `0x40000400` | 3,438,480 B | patched by mods | | 4 | updater | 32,776 B | raw; never touch | | 5 | meta | | | | 6 | ColdFire boot stub | 1,744 B | raw; never touch | | 7 | voice engine for CPU #2, at `0x40000400`, entry `0x40001070` | 383,760 B | raw; patchable | | 8 | the shared ARM Cortex-M image (not a second FPGA; CONFLICTS S15) | 159,948 B | identical in size to the DT1/DN2/Rytm/A4 image whose hash is known | Stock 1.41 SHA-256: `8e2488f4...b9ed19e`.

section: Syntakt / Platform: two ColdFires, an FPGA, an analog mixer (SyntHack OS docs, OS 1.41)
text: Signing conflict `[?]`: SyntHack describes an HMAC-SHA256 over the container for 1.41, with the key derived from the image. digikit found no HMAC trailer in 1.42 (the last 32 bytes are zero). Check the trailer of your own file before you decide.

section: Syntakt / Platform: two ColdFires, an FPGA, an analog mixer (SyntHack OS docs, OS 1.41)
text: Boot unpack limit: the bootstrap loads compressed section 3 at `0x40200000` and unpacks it to `0x40000400`. The margin (decompressed minus compressed) must stay below ~`0x1FFC00` at every point of the stream. Stock 1.41 has a margin of +99,938 B. A build padded with zeros to `0x40350000` (-8,751 B) did not boot, tested twice and hung on the logo. Zero padding is the worst case; already-compressed payloads raise the margin. SyntHack refuses builds under 4 KB of margin. `[hw]`

section: Syntakt / Platform: two ColdFires, an FPGA, an analog mixer (SyntHack OS docs, OS 1.41)
text: The Syntakt accepts rebuilt images (recompressed section 3) over USB and DIN. `[hw]`

section: Syntakt / Memory map of CPU #1 (OS 1.41)
text: Hardware lesson `[hw]`: SyntHack up to v0.8.0 kept mod code at `0x46000000`. Projects with SP TWINSHOT samples then crashed at boot. Since v0.8.1 the mod code (compressed, appended to section 3 at `0x40348000`) is unpacked into a 64 KB block that a hook at the end of heap init (`0x4010358E`) reserves first. ([I20](../INCIDENTS.md#i20-mod-code-at-a-free-address-crashed-projects-with-certain-samples))

section: Syntakt / Memory map of CPU #1 (OS 1.41)
text: Conflict to watch `[?]`: SY FM4 (OS 1.40A) copies its code to `0x47000000`, which it describes as "above the BSS end, below the stack, addressed by nothing". That is the region SyntHack found to be overwritten by sample loading on 1.41. Treat any use of RAM above the BSS as unsafe until it is tested with sample-heavy projects.

section: Syntakt / Memory map of CPU #1 (OS 1.41)
text: Boot: entry `0x400004E8`; static constructors loop `0x40082500` (136 entries); the intro animation task `0x40087E6A` gates boot, so never make the intro longer. Screen: 128x64 1 bpp, column-major, double buffer at `0x402D6DC4`/`0x402D6DC0`; frame loop `0x4000A0E6` redraws when `*(0x444E1334)+96` is set. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / Audio path
text: CPU #2 (section 7): all work runs in the audio interrupt `0x40000934` (vector 96, DMA timer 0 capture). Per block it copies `0x1B0` bytes of parameters from shared RAM and renders 8 digital voices (`0x40004324`). It returns 8 x 32 int32 over eDMA channel 47 and does no mixing. 12 engines: tables at `0x400148F0` (render), `0x40014920` (update), `0x40014950` (machine id -> engine). Order: BD MODERN, SD BASIC, CY ALLOY, PC CARBON, SY TONE, SY CHORD, SD VINTAGE, CP VINTAGE, SY TOY, SY BITS, SY SWARM, SP TWINSHOT. SY CHORD reads a 512 x int32 wave at `0x4001A300`. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / Audio path
text: CPU #1 (section 3): the per-block routine `0x400A3856` runs CV/gain, ADC deinterleave, then master/FX `0x4008F1CA`. Delay `0x40096890` and reverb `0x40096E3C` are the same code as on the Digitakt mk1. Buffers: digital tracks from CPU #2 at `0x80003D50`. ADC channels at `0x80003950`: 0-3 analog tracks, 4-5 external in, 6-7 the FX-track bus. USB/Overbridge: 20 channels per frame at `0x80004760`. The final mix is analog: digital buses go out through DACs into an analog mixer, with nothing digital after them. 40 control voltages go out over DSPI1 with eDMA channel 15; CV 35/36 are the FX-track bus VCAs. `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / Audio path
text: CPU #1 load: ~89 % at rest (sequencer stopped), measured on the device with DTIM0 (`0xFC07000C`) at interrupt entry and exit. The UI gets the rest, so a few thousand instructions per block make the UI lag. `[hw]` SY FM4 reports its main-CPU render at 85.8k of 166.7k cycles per block (stock 85.0k). That is a different span of the same interrupt. `[?]`

section: Syntakt / Audio path
text: Digital filter and amp run on CPU #2; the cutoff is computed on CPU #1. Analog voices and the FX track drive a hardware envelope generator with 20-bit rate codes. Measured curves: the digital biquad f0 = 4.918 Hz x e^(0.0655 x FREQ); the analog filter f = 14.645 Hz x e^(0.0574 x FREQ). Tempo is at `0x402D7010` (BPM x 120). `[hw]` (analog curves measured)

section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
text: Section 7 is byte-identical in 1.41 and 1.42 (SHA-256 `daf6451c...783bc2`). It is ColdFire ISA-C with EMAC, MCF5441x-class: compile with `-mcpu=54418`, disassemble with `-m m68k:isa-c:emac`. CPU #2 has its own 128 MB SDRAM at `0x40000000` (SP `0x48000000`, entry `0x40001070`). `[doc]`

section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
text: Only 39.8 KB is code (`0x40000404-0x40009f88`: boot, audio interrupt, voice loop, 12 engines, sample loader), followed by 284 KB of tables and data. Code room for mods is almost nil: ~318 bytes in small pieces remained after SynCrackd's images.

section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
text: CPU #2 configures its own FPGA: a packed bitstream at `0x40041060` is unpacked to `0x40042000` (54,664 bytes) at init. That is the same size as the Analog Heat +FX FPGA section, so it may be the same part `[?]`. Keep away from it (rule A22).

section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
text: The sample pool is in CPU #2's RAM: 64 MB from `0x4004f750`, in BSS zeroed at boot. A 64-entry slot table `{u32 frames, u32 pointer}` is at `0x4404f754`. Format: 64 times `u32 frames` + big-endian int16 mono. The main CPU fills it at boot in 2 KB chunks through the shared window `0x800`, with an unchecked 16-bit index. This is the slow boot the manual mentions. Per slot at most 524,287 frames (10.9 s; positions are 20.12 fixed point). The stock UI limits slots to 5 s and "32 MB".

section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
text: Above the BSS, `0x4404f980-0x48000000` (63.7 MB) is not referenced by any section-7 instruction and is used for SynCrackd's state. Leave the top megabyte for the stack (its depth is not measured). This is CPU #2's RAM, not the main CPU's region that sample loading overwrites (CONFLICTS O2). `[hw]` (alpha, one unit)

section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
text: Shared window (CPU #2 `0x0-0x1000` = main CPU `0x10000000`, chip select 0, 16-bit, one wait state): `0x000-0x1b0`: the parameter block, copied to `0x80008000` every block; `0x1b0-0x5b0`: 8 mono track buffers, sent by eDMA 47; `0x5b0-0x800`: unused by stock; `0x800-0x1000`: the sample chunk at boot.

section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
text: SRAM `0x80000000`: 8 voices of 1,800 B, 8 mono int32 output buffers, 8 parameter blocks of 142 B. The highest static reference is `0x8000f670`, so treat SRAM as full.

section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
text: Twinshot (engine 11, machine type 44) reads the parameter slots 18-25: TUN1, SMP1, FLT1, MIX, TUN2, SMP2, loop flag, DEC1. A sample select below the centre plays the slot in reverse. `[emu]`

section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
text: SynCrackd replaces Twinshot (and CY ALLOY) with a 64-slot stereo sampler, loops, slices, time stretch and transient triggers. It is OS 1.42 only, alpha, tested in emulation and on one unit, MIT.

section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
text: Synfact (OS 1.41) adds DT mk1 sample machines, a per-project pool, polyphony across tracks and a third LFO. It ships its firmware change as a zlib-compressed XOR mask against the official file, pinned by hash. It needs a second mods file (515,808 B) sent with its own transfer tool after the flash. Boot is confirmed on a unit (core 1.4 and 1.7.2, 2026-11-09); the safe-boot rollback is not yet tested on hardware. `[hw]` {synfact} {synfact-core}

section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
text: Each change is stored with the SHA-256 of the original bytes, so a different OS version fails the build instead of crashing. Every mod runs in a Unicorn emulator next to the original code before flashing. Stock Unicorn gets signed fractional EMAC wrong (the audio comes out silent), so EMAC instructions are trapped and executed in Python from the NXP manual. Use CPU model "ANY" (the code needs FF1, MVS/MVZ, SATS).

section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
text: Hooks: replace at least 6 bytes with `jsr` plus `nop` padding, and the trampoline replays the replaced instructions. Save every register; replay replaced EMAC instructions first. If your code uses EMAC, set MACSR yourself and leave ACC0 at 0, because the OS sum routines start from it. One-time setup goes in a hook in the page initializer (`0x401885D2...`), never in boot time.

section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
text: Mod code: gcc/as with `-mcpu=54418`, no `.bss` (put variables in `.data`), no libgcc (`nm -u` empty). ColdFire limits: `muls.l` takes no absolute address, there is no `exg`, `movem` takes only `(An)`/`d16(An)`, short branches reach ±127 B.

section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
text: Spare storage the OS saves without knowing: per track: engine word +106 (hidden id 72); per kit: unused words of the pattern kit at `*0x800030BC` (ids 0, 0x1A, 0x24, 0x27, 0x29, 0x2A, 0x37, 0x46, 0x38). Store values XOR their default, so old projects load with defaults; kit words 41-43 of the 12 per-track kit blocks (Digitakt MIDI-track data, unused here); 256 bytes in the project settings file. A "free" parameter id can be an alias the OS shows in some modes, so audit it.

section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`

Ramps must snap to their target or the effect never goes idle. Limit how far a modulated delay moves per block. section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
text: Where mod code lives at run time (SyntHack modarea, v0.8.1+): The OS image has only ~2 KB free, and everything after it is zeroed at boot. So mod code is appended to section 3 compressed (SHLZ, at `0x40348000 + offset`). At boot it is unpacked into the first 64 KB block of the OS heap: buddy allocator `0x4010350C`, 16 MB pool at `0x444E38C0`. The block is reserved by a call right after heap initialization, so it always gets index 0, and the OS never hands it out again. The earlier home above the BSS (`0x46000000`) was overwritten whenever samples loaded (SyntHack issue 4), which settles conflict O2. `[hw]` {synthack-mods}

section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
text: Kit and project storage that round-trips through stock code (SyntHack kitstore/projstore): Kit words 41-43 of the 12 per-track blocks go into 6 file bytes that stock's writer zeroes and its reader ignores. 256 bytes go into the project settings block (`+0x227..+0x3FF` is zeroed by the writer and ignored by the reader), behind an `SH` marker. Tests run the real writer and reader with and without the hooks. Zero must mean "default", because stock-saved files load as zero. `[emu]` {synthack-mods}

Its UI uses the Digitakt MIDI-track "CC Select" ids 262-268, which the Syntakt never uses. Cost: ~100 instructions per block when off, ~600 when on. Checked on the device (v0.9). `[hw]` {synthack-mods}

section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 5. The DT2 audio chain per block (planar floats, 32 L then 32 R; voice blocks mono)
text: At H2/H3 SIMD is off and no DO loop is active. The stock FX state lives in DDR: chorus `0x80459388`, delay `0x8005912c` (rings of 524,288 floats, max 8 s), reverb `0x80000018`. FX rings wrap by index arithmetic; FX units never write B or L registers, but the voice renderer does and restores them. Static FX cost: chorus 7.1k, delay 6.0k, reverb 17.2k instructions per block. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 5. The DT2 audio chain per block (planar floats, 32 L then 32 R; voice blocks mono)
text: The stock machines share almost no code (each machine is one large function). Only the post-voice chain and a few maths helpers are shared between DT2 and DN2. `[doc]`

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 1. Shown on both units `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 1. Shown on both units `[hw]`

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 1. Shown on both units `[hw]`
text: NaN or Inf in stock FX feedback silences everything until reboot: on a DT2 from an LFO at large depth on TUNE (digikit) and in the owner's builds; on a DN2 from never-written DDR, which powers on as garbage such as `0xFFFFFFFF` (the DN2 skill). Same failure, two triggers: guard every value you feed into a feedback path, and fill new DDR in emulator tests with `0xFFFFFFFF`. {digikit-f51} {own-dt2-notes} {dn2-skill-firmware}

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 1. Shown on both units `[hw]`
text: Shared stock DSP code, by the bytes: the DT2's six wavetable render stages are in the DN2 image too. Three are byte-identical; in the other three every differing byte is a PC-relative call offset (same target) or one table-pointer literal. All call the same reciprocal helper at sw `0x1c06ba` in both images (RECIPS plus Newton steps, the helper behind A35's divide cost). A fix or measurement on one of these stages carries over. `[doc]` {digikit-f11}

DN2: usable `0x20088400-0x200b0000` per the DN2 skill, and one block in L2 stopped a unit from starting. section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 4. Different on the two devices
text: DSP DDR: on the DN2, `0x80531000-0xa0000000` (~507 MB) was never written in a fill-and-scan test on a unit. On the DT2 that range is the sample pool: its window runs from `0x8422b9c8` to `0x9d22b9c8`. Do not carry the DN2's "free DDR" over to the DT2. The DT2's SHARC image also zero-fills 32 MiB at `0x80a00000` and a `0x1c4`-byte control block at `0x82a00000` that the DN2 image lacks, and the SHARC functions that use them have no DN2 twin. {dn2-ddr} {dt2-lab-flex-mem} {dn2-drive}

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 4. Different on the two devices
text: How stock spends the block: the DN2 engine renders every voice every block (~63-65 % flat by dnfw's idle-task method, a held voice adds ~8k cycles; elekloader reads ~80 %, conflict O15). The DT2 engine scales with what plays and governs its own load: with 8 heavy tracks it ran at 99-100 % for whole windows and missed no block. Budgets measured on one device say nothing about the other. {dn2-sharcload} {own-dt2-notes}

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 4. Different on the two devices
text: What an overrun does: on the DT2 a late block is exactly one missed block, and even 54 provoked misses did not leave lasting damage. dn2mk2 users saw custom-voice overruns on the DN2 cut all audio until a power cycle. These are not the same experiment (sustained overload by added voices vs. single late blocks), so they do not contradict each other. A test that settles it: provoke single late blocks on a DN2 the way the DT2 test did. {own-dt2-notes} {dn2mk2-reports}

section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 4. Different on the two devices

On the DN2 the DN2 skill uses it as the DSP load, while dnfw reads the frame handler's own count (~416k cycles) from it. Compare both methods on one DN2 before using word 0 there. {own-dt2-notes} {dn2-skill-emulators} {dn2-sharcload}

section: Ecosystem lessons - how the 2026 custom-firmware wave is built, verified and what goes wrong / Failure modes
text: Bricking is usually recoverable when the bootloader is untouched; the danger is projects that modify boot code or lack a documented recovery path. Subtle DSP/bus timing bugs are more likely to ruin a session than bricking. One mod developer bricked an Akai MPC Sample in September (video). Verified bricks in the wave are described as rare. `[?]`

section: Ecosystem lessons - how the 2026 custom-firmware wave is built, verified and what goes wrong / Failure modes
text: Version lock-in: each mod targets exactly one OS build; official updates break mods until ported. Abandoned solo repos leave users stuck on old builds. Web patchers and installers run with full privileges and are rarely audited. `[?]`

section: Ecosystem lessons - how the 2026 custom-firmware wave is built, verified and what goes wrong / Legal and policy points as the article describes them (not legal advice)
text: Elektron's 16 Sep policy bans sharing/requesting/linking to firmware mods, tools, repos or guides on Elektronauts and its social channels; a next-day amendment extended it to discontinued legacy machines; general discussion stays allowed; development moved to Discord, independent forums and GitHub (see the policy page itself in AGENT-RULES B4). `[doc]` {elektronauts-policy}

section: Ecosystem lessons - how the 2026 custom-firmware wave is built, verified and what goes wrong / Legal and policy points as the article describes them (not legal advice)
text: Developers distribute patches or scripts, not firmware, and warn users not to share compiled `.syx`/`.bin` outputs. The article cites US DMCA section 1201 exemptions (research, repair, interoperability; active through October 2027, generally not distribution) and the EU Software Directive's narrow interoperability allowance; neither has been tested over a music-hardware mod. Paid firmware (Groove OS, $29) and unlocking paid features on current hardware raise legal risk; first takedowns are expected for commercial mods. Warranty: expect denial for faults caused by third-party firmware, depending on country. `[?]` {dubspot}

text: Tool: build `make`; Linux/macOS native, Windows via WSL (work in the Linux home directory, a filename in the tool repo contains `?`). Commands: `-i` summary + checksum check, `-v` detail, `-o dir` extract all, `-d ID` extract one section, `-c ID file -o new.syx` replace a section and repack, `-r` repack unchanged (self-test), `-V` version string, `-l 0..3` compression level, `--emit-container`. Sound/pattern/project dumps are `.syx` too but the tool rejects them as non-firmware. `[doc]` {em-tutorial}

section: Ecosystem lessons - how the 2026 custom-firmware wave is built, verified and what goes wrong / Safe byte-level editing rules (elektronmods tutorial by the forum admin, using elektron-firmware-tool)
text: The Digitone II 1.11 example file has 18,668 SysEx messages, 8-in-7 encoding, per-packet checksums, a container with model/version/overall checksum and an HMAC-SHA256 signature the tool recomputes on repack. Section 3 (MAIN OS) is the usual target; leave 2 (bootstrap) and 4 (updater) alone because the bootloader holds the recovery menu; section 8 appears as `?` (no known name); section IDs differ on other devices, so `-i` is authoritative. `.raw` sections are copied as-is, `.bin` sections are decompressed. `[doc]` {em-tutorial}

section: Ecosystem lessons - how the 2026 custom-firmware wave is built, verified and what goes wrong / Safe byte-level editing rules (elektronmods tutorial by the forum admin, using elektron-firmware-tool)
text: Editing rules: overwrite bytes only, the file size must not change (later addresses shift); replacement text must be the same length and use characters already present; keep the terminating zero byte; always edit a copy in `work/` and keep `extracted/` untouched; verify with `cmp -l` (exactly the intended number of changed bytes) and by re-extracting section 3 from the new file and comparing it byte-for-byte; `-V` must not exceed the original version string length (e.g. 4 characters like `1.11`). The repacked file is smaller than Elektron's because the tool compresses slightly better (level 3 took ~14 s, level 0 is ~18x faster and ~3 % larger). The author states the worked example (replacing "UNTITLED" with "ELEKMODS") was not tested on hardware. `[doc]` {em-tutorial}

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / Sections
text: Digitakt II: section 2 = bootstrap, section 4 = updater (never modify); the DSP program is an ADI boot stream in section 7; ElekLabs digikit's patchkit refuses to change sections 2, 4 and 8.

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / Sections
text: Section 7 is a stream of ADI boot records (the ADSP-2156x hardware reference, boot chapter). Each header is four little-endian uint32s: block code, target, byte count, argument. The block code's top byte is `0xad`; its byte at offset 2 makes the XOR of all 16 header bytes zero; its low 16 bits are flags: `0x0001` LOAD (copy `count` bytes to the target), `0x0101` FILL (fill with the argument), `0x5001` FIRST + IGNORE (starts a boot image; target = entry in PC16, argument = distance from the end of this header to the next FIRST), `0x0801` INIT and `0x8001` FINAL (end the image and the stream). Later loads overwrite earlier ones in order, and stock relies on that (15 overlapping loads and fills on DN2 1.12). To add code, insert records before FINAL and grow only the last FIRST's argument and XOR byte; dt2-machine-lab used FILL records to keep a decoded stream under the size limit below. `[doc]` {elekloader-sharc-boot} {dt2-lab-capicola}

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / Sections
text: Section 7 must stay under 1 MiB, stored and decoded (DT2 and DN2). At boot the ColdFire allocates two `0x100000`-byte buffers, copies the stored section into the first, writes a `0x03` byte at the start of the second and depacks the section after it. The decoded-size check (`len + 1 > 0x100000`, status 3) runs after depacking (DT2 1.16 `0x400cd20c`; the same 828-byte routine on DT2 1.17, DN2 1.11 and 1.12) {digikit-f06} {digikit-f01}. So an oversized stream is not refused cleanly: it overruns the buffer first. A dt2-machine-lab build with a 1,314,460-byte decoded stream hit a ColdFire exception on a unit and was withdrawn; the lab's repair encodes zero regions as fill blocks so the decoded stream fits {dt2-lab-capicola}. elekloader states the same limits for the DN2 ([`../devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md`](../devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md)). Count decoded bytes with a depacker, not the stored size (rule A46). `[hw]` The earlier README named sections 3 and 7 as patch targets. `[doc]` {digikit} {digikit-old}

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / Section 8: one shared ARM firmware image (merged from dnfw, analog-emu, digikit, rytm-fw-re)
text: What is settled: Section 8 is a complete ARM Cortex-M firmware image: a Thumb vector table, and a descriptor naming a 1 MB flash window at `0x60000000` with the image at `0x60042000`. The same 159,948-byte image (sha256 `6943b2f2...`) ships in Digitakt mk1 1.53, Digitone II 1.11, Analog Rytm MKII 1.73 and Analog Four 1.55D. Syntakt and Digitakt II carry a section 8 of the same size. It is not an FPGA bitstream (the FPGA is section 1, or inside section 7 on the Digitone mk1), and it is not code for the device's own CPU. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3} {analog-emu-a4} {rytm-fw-re}

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / Section 8: one shared ARM firmware image (merged from dnfw, analog-emu, digikit, rytm-fw-re)

Against that: the DN2, Rytm and A4 operating systems carry their own panel firmware inside MAIN and re-flash the panel from there.

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
text: Preamble of the decoded byte stream: u32 container size + u32 content checksum, then the container (magic at offset 8). Container size: DN2 1,743,120, DN1 1,102,352 (the sizes of the file pair dnfw analysed). The content checksum is not a standard algorithm: a running 32-bit sum over big-endian words, each word XORed with its one-based index; trailing bytes that do not fill a word are excluded. Compressed sections carry a header with the stream length and a u32 sum of the stream bytes (padding excluded). `[doc]` {dn2-ele3}

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
text: SysEx transport: each message is `F0 ... F7`; the body is either a 126-byte data packet or a 14-byte marker; it starts with the manufacturer ID and a device ID: DN2 `0x15`, DT2 `0x14`, DN1 `0x0D`. Payloads use 8-in-7 encoding (116 encoded bytes carry 101 decoded bytes, last packet zero-padded); packet count = stream length / 101 + 1 (an exact division still adds a packet); a block and sequence counter starts from values in the start marker and wraps at 7 bits; the 7-bit packet checksum sits in the last body byte and uses a base value taken from the start marker, not a constant. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3}

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
text: Trailer: the last 32 bytes of the declared container are an HMAC-SHA256 on the first 16-byte boundary at least 4 bytes past the last section (gap zeroed); it covers everything before it, padding included; the key is derived from material inside the image (a printable string in a decompressed section, found in the bootstrap, plus a fixed constant) - never edit that key material, the device likely verifies with its installed copy. DN1 1.42A is unsigned (trailer all zeros). `[doc]` {dn2-ele3}

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
text: Compression: each section is raw or aPLib-variant compressed (not flagged - inferred by whether the bytes depack): LZ77 with interlaced Elias-gamma codes, a biased offset, a last-offset reuse code and a length bonus for far matches, minimum match 2; Elektron's streams keep the furthest match within 1 MiB and the longest at 2,048 bytes. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3}

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
text: DN1 vs DN2: bootstrap load address DN2 `0x02000000` / DN1 `0x02000800`; blob (id 7) compressed on DN2, raw on DN1; boot (id 6) absent on DN2, present (raw) on DN1; section 5 (meta) is 15 bytes, stored raw, no destination address, identical size on both; section 8 appears in OS 1.11 compressed (it is the Outbox 8 accessory firmware). `[doc]` {dn2-ele3} {dn2-cfw-handoff}

section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
text: After patching, recompute: re-encoded section data and its stream length/sum (+ padding to 4 bytes, table length includes the padding), section table offsets/lengths and 16-byte placement (and the count if sections change), the preamble (container size, content checksum), SysEx packet checksums/counters/packet count, and on DN2 the HMAC over everything before the trailer. The page does not say whether the product code, build string or version string must change, nor whether ids must be renumbered. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3}

text: MIDI DIN runs at 31,250 baud, about 3,125 bytes/s; a 2,209,184-byte image needs at least ~12 minutes (derived, not timed). Do not interrupt. `[doc]` {dn2-flashing}

section: Flash procedure and link pitfalls (Digitone II, as practised by dn2mk2 and dnfw) / Numbers
text: Nothing is written until reception completes. The receiver has no error recovery: a bad sequence number or checksum freezes the progress bar with no message and no retransmit. Checksums and sequence counters are content-independent, so the receiver cannot tell a modified image from stock. `[doc]` {dn2-flashing} {dn2mk2-safety}

Root cause in that case: a Focusrite Scarlett 4i4's MIDI went idle mid-transfer and dropped packets; the stall point varied (30/70/80 %). `[hw]` {dn2-flashing}
