section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
text: CPU fingerprint: NXP MCF5441x (ColdFire V4m with EMAC) - UART8 `0xEC070000`, GPIO `0xEC094000`, eDMA `0xFC044000` (TCDs +0x1000), INTC0-2 `0xFC048000/0xFC04C000/0xFC050000`, DSPI0 `0xFC05C000`, PIT0-3 `0xFC080000-0xFC08C000`, EPORT `0xFC090000`. Stock Ghidra misdecodes EMAC line-A words; digikit uses a separate language spec. `[doc]` {digikit-f08}

section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
text: DDR is 128 MiB (DDRMC writes in the bootstrap; earlier 64 MiB claims are wrong): `0x40000000-0x47FFFFFF` cached (ACR0), `0x48000000-0x4FFFFFFF` an uncached alias of the same DDR used for DMA buffers; reset SP `0x48000000`; 32 MiB C++ heap above `0x44000000`. `[doc]` {digikit-f08}

section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
text: NOR flash 16 MiB, S25FL127S-class (RDID mfg 0x01, id 0x2018); the bootstrap's flash loop uses 512-byte pages and 256 KB erase blocks. The in-OS writer (finding 75) uses 0x100-byte pages and 0x10000 sectors from flash `0x80000` - two code paths, two geometries `[?]`. `[doc]` {digikit-f08} {digikit-f75}

section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
text: UART8 receive is done by eDMA (channel 34), not by reading the data register - an emulator must model eDMA, not just the UART. `[emu]` {digikit-f08}

section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
text: No ColdFire watchdog. Neither MAIN OS (DT2 1.16/1.17, DN2 1.11/1.12) nor the bootstrap names the core watchdog registers (CWCR `0xFC040016`, CWSR `0xFC04001B`), and the watchdog is off after reset. A ColdFire hang therefore stays hung until a power cycle; nothing resets the unit for you. Static reading; computed addresses are not excluded. Third-party MCF5441x code agrees that the core watchdog stays off after a power cycle unless software enables it, and CWCR can be written only once after reset (so a bootstrap write of 0 would also lock it off). `[doc]` {digikit-f17} {netburner-cwt} {nxp-mcf5441x-rm}

section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
text: eMMC part table: DT2 1.16 (`0x402b4a24`) and DN2 1.10E/1.11 (`0x4029f554`) accept the same seven 32-byte entries: Kingston parts `TX2932` and `TS0A32`, both 32 GB, matching the Kingston EMMC32G-TX29 on a DN2 board photo. Shared ColdFire storage code: the block driver, the MmcFs slot store and the transfer routing; the sample filesystem, its request handler and the sample manager are DT2-only. `[doc]` {dn2-drive}

section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
text: eMMC card (both, about 32 GB part, 0x2E1A000 sectors assumed): sectors `0x0-0x457FFF` belong to the firmware (boot, tables, projects, pools, presets); MmcFs refuses writes at `0x457FFF` and above. DT2 1.17: factory sample table "MaGj" at `0x458000` and 1,265 factory samples to `0x5D7FFF` - never touch; +Drive (ekFS) `0x5D8000-0x2DF017F`; `0x2DF0180` to the end unused. DN2 1.12: nothing stock writes at `0x458000` and up; FORMAT trims only up to `0x457FFF`. Unchecked bank ids in the Data API can reach every sector below `0x800000` over USB - put any private store above that line (digikit: DT2 `0x2DF1000+`, DN2 `0x800000+`). Not checked on a real card. `[doc]` {digikit-f59}

section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
text: Card pools inside the firmware area (MmcFs) `[emu]` {digikit-samples}: Fixed slots: projects 0-127 (16 MiB each on both), sounds 0-2047 (DT2 4 KiB, DN2 1 KiB), kits 0-1023 (DT2 64 KiB, DN2 32 KiB). The bitmaps at sector `0x800` are write-protect padlocks, not occupancy. The boot project (magic "COKi") has two copies at sectors `0x40000` and `0x48000`. The working project is at `0x50000` and is rewritten from the boot copy at every start. The DT2 has a path filesystem (ekFS +Drive) for samples. The DN2 has none: only the MmcFs pools. Card layouts are device data (digikit `devices/<device>.toml`).

section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / ColdFire code caves and mod RAM (dnfw `code-caves.md`, `mod-memory-regions.md`, DN2 1.11)
text: RAM aliases every `0x08000000`: a byte answers at nine addresses up to `0x8c000000`. ACR0 caches only the first window, and stock reaches its DMA buffers through the second (`0x4e......`). Scan all nine windows before you call RAM unreferenced. `[doc]`

section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / ColdFire code caves and mod RAM (dnfw `code-caves.md`, `mod-memory-regions.md`, DN2 1.11)
text: Flashed bytes above the reset clear do not survive a reset (DT2 1.16 clears from `0x40312000`; on the DN2 about 3,200 B separate the end of MAIN OS from the clear). Code placed there must be copied up by a loader *after* the clear. digikit, dnfw and elekloader all do this. `[hw]` (bytes lost on a DT2)

section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / ColdFire code caves and mod RAM (dnfw `code-caves.md`, `mod-memory-regions.md`, DN2 1.11)
text: The DN2's code region has no free run of even 24 bytes. Zero runs exist in the constants region, and code there does execute (a boot-path cave printed "CAVE RAN!!!" on a real DN2). One "free" run was an array the code fills at run time: patching it crashed the unit, and the emulator watch read zeros. Two static checks catch most cases: a fixed stride between equal gaps marks an array, and `lea`/`pea`/`move.l #` operands mark referenced space. On 1.11 only 13 runs (4,207 B) pass both, not the "~29 KB" first assumed. `[hw]` ([I19](../INCIDENTS.md#i19-patching-a-free-zero-run-crashed-the-unit))

text: Displaced stock instructions are replayed at another address, so no PC-relative instructions in the displaced bytes. Pick hook sites whose first instructions are absolute. `[doc]`

section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / ColdFire code caves and mod RAM (dnfw `code-caves.md`, `mod-memory-regions.md`, DN2 1.11)
text: dnfw's mods take fixed RAM chunks in `0x46700000-0x47fe0000` (waverider 436 KB at `0x4670c000`/`0x467f0000`/`0x46a00000`, lfo4 `0x46800000`/`0x46900000`, ...). The alternative is the stock 32 MiB buddy heap (`0x4464abf0`), where the allocator records the use but a 12.9 MB project load takes half. Mods that store settings in unused pattern bits must not claim the same bits. `[doc]`

text: Stock does not touch `0x46710000-0x47ffffcc` in emulation. Three independent checks agree: dn2-cfw's write watches over `0x46800000-0x47f00000`, elekloader's canary over `0x46710000-0x48000000` (cold boot, two panel sessions), and digikit's reference scan (`0x4671a000-0x47fe0000` unreferenced, [`dt2-dn2-limits-and-audio-chain.md`](dt2-dn2-limits-and-audio-chain.md)). All three ran in an emulator, so rule A43 (canary on a unit) still applies. `[emu]`

section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Digitone II: who uses the RAM above the reset clear (compared across five projects, 2026-11-02)
text: The range from `0x46700000` up to `0x46710000` is not free. On 1.12 it holds the end of the DMA buffers; on 1.11 the MMC bounce buffer reaches `0x46701300`. dnfw's lfo4 state sat at `0x46700000` until 2026-10-11 and corrupted every project saved on an LFO4 unit (the bounce buffer carries each piece of a project on save and load); it now lives in the first block of stock's heap (`0x4464abf0`). dnfw's remaining `0x4670xxxx` chunks (from `0x46708000`) are above the 1.11 DMA section (`0x466b8000-0x46701340`) but inside the 1.12 one, so they must move for a 1.12 port. The "25.3 MB unclaimed above BSS" figure in dnfw's memory map missed these alias references. The skill's "`0x46700000..0x46900000` unused, hardware-confirmed" disagrees: see [CONFLICTS S17](../CONFLICTS.md). `[doc]`

section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Digitone II: who uses the RAM above the reset clear (compared across five projects, 2026-11-02)
text: The platforms collide. dnfw's lfo4 code, cfmod's default link address and the start of dn2-cfw's mod area are all `0x46800000`; cfkit's scratch at `0x46a00000` is Waverider's chunk. Only elekloader's `0x47f00000` and dn2-cfw's core `0x47e00000` are disjoint from the rest. A mod built for one platform cannot be dropped into another's image without moving its RAM (and its hooks: [`dt2-dn2-limits-and-audio-chain.md`](dt2-dn2-limits-and-audio-chain.md) section 6, [`agent-workflow.md`](agent-workflow.md)). Before picking an address, check this table and declare every range you use. The full register, with every platform's ranges per OS and the overlaps, is [`../RAM-TENANCY.md`](../RAM-TENANCY.md) (task T23).

section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Details per device
text: Digitakt mk1: ELE3, device byte `0x0A` (elekloader's page says `0x14`, which is the Digitakt II's byte; settled by taktone, see the table in [firmware-container.md](firmware-container.md)), six-plus sections, main OS staged at `0x40200000`. DDR is free RAM. Hook sites: no numeric list on the page; the first eight sites of the Digitone mk1 are described as the Digitakt mk1's.

section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Details per device
text: Digitone mk1: ELE3, seven sections, stock gap 403,540 bytes. The OS clears `0x4028E000-0x43229E60`; operands end before `0x43EB0000`; stack from `0x48000000`. First eight hook sites match the Digitakt mk1; the ninth is `ev_voice_on` at `0x4009e928`; render frame `0xB8`. Core `mods/core-dn1`, up to 4.0 (1.44 ported at its own addresses).

section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Details per device
text: Digitakt II: device byte `0x14`, six sections, sealed (HMAC-SHA256). Clear `0x40312000-0x47E28470`; the core takes `0x47F00000-0x47F40000`; SRAM free at `0x80006E80-0x80008000` and `0x8000F100-0x80010000`. Hook events `ev_tick`, `ev_draw`, `ev_key`, `ev_enc`, `ev_settings`, `ev_personalize` (no numeric addresses). Core `mods/core-dt2`; DTIM0 not started.

section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Details per device
text: Digitone II (OS 1.12): device byte `0x15`, six sections, sealed. Hook sites: boot `0x40000538`, `ev_tick` `0x4002e464`, `ev_draw` `0x4002e4ca`, `ev_key` `0x4002f20c`, `ev_enc` `0x4002f256`, `ev_settings` `0x4009ff88`, `ev_personalize` `0x400987a2`. Clear `0x402fd000-0x466b84d0` with a 32 MB heap inside it; SHARC mod area 32 KiB at `[0x20090000,0x20098000)`. USB cap `update_max = 0x200000` (2 MiB, preamble plus container, conservative): CO02 (1,915,960 bytes) was accepted, a 2,147,448-byte build stalled. The page is inconsistent on the core version (0.2 in the file list, 0.1 in the core section).

section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Details per device
text: Octatrack: one image for MKI and MKII (`.syx` and `.bin`); `stage` is `None`, so the in-place unpack is unsimulated. Protected `0x400de1e0-0x400e21e0`. Six hook events (sys tick, composed frame, keys, encoders, MIDI in, frame interrupt); boot site `0x4000050c`; draw gate `0x400c45b0`; image free runs `0x400c45b0-0x400c4702`, `0x400d24e0-0x400d2ce0`, `0x400d64e0-0x400d7c3c`. DSP payload A `0x136cb` bytes, payload B `0x12d05` bytes; the SPATIALIZER range P:0xaa8-0xbac (261 words) is used for mods. Arena 14,602 pages of 6,144 B.

section: How Digitakt II and Digitone II take an OS update from the running OS (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / Acknowledgement and buffering
text: The menu route sends no SysEx reply at all; only the screen shows progress. Pace by time: digikit uses 128-byte messages every 2 ms (about 29 s DT2, 37 s DN2) - 12x slower than the emulated ceiling; not run on hardware.

section: How Digitakt II and Digitone II take an OS update from the running OS (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / Acknowledgement and buffering
text: The whole container is staged in RAM; flash is untouched until the last message. A transfer cut before the footer leaves the screen on "Receiving" and nothing validated, erased or written. Power loss during the flash phase leaves the container area partly erased; the bootstrap (`0x40000`) is never written by this path, so FUNC boot menu and DIN OS UPGRADE stay usable (emulated).

section: How Digitakt II and Digitone II take an OS update from the running OS (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / Validation (before any erase; run up to three times)
text: No "UPGRADE OS NOW?" on the menu route in the emulator: the delegate returns "do not ask", so after the last message the screen goes ERASING FLASH... -> SUCCESS! REBOOTING -> reset with no key pressed. Real hardware may differ (no derived delegate class was found). NO while receiving asks "CANCEL OS UPGRADE?".

section: How Digitakt II and Digitone II take an OS update from the running OS (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / Validation (before any erase; run up to three times)
text: The flash writer ignores erase/program return codes - "Success" is shown whatever the chips did. It erases sector by sector from flash `0x80000` (default sector 0x10000) and programs 0x100-byte pages, waits 3 s, soft-resets via `0x80 -> 0xec090000`.

section: How Digitakt II and Digitone II take an OS update from the running OS (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / Rules that follow
text: Prefer the RPC route with explicit End; send End 0 on every abort. Do not resend Writes blindly; a failed run costs only a new Start.

section: How Digitakt II and Digitone II take an OS update from the running OS (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / Rules that follow
text: A "Success!" screen does not prove the flash was written correctly - verify by version string / behaviour after reboot.

section: How Digitakt II and Digitone II take an OS update from the running OS (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / Rules that follow
text: Never rely on the in-OS path for recovery; it needs a working MAIN OS. The bootstrap route (DIN) is the recovery.

section: How Digitakt II and Digitone II take an OS update from the running OS (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / Rules that follow
text: Digitone II has no build floor in the validator - an older signed image is accepted; Digitakt II refuses builds below 0060.

section: Overbridge over USB (what Overwitch's README reveals) - the only deep source on Analog Heat +FX so far / USB device side of Digitakt II / Digitone II (digikit finding 42, static, DT2 1.16)
text: Controller: MCF5441x USB OTG at `0xFC0B0000`, device mode, external ULPI PHY, high speed (480 Mb/s; descriptors have 512-byte bulk packets; DEVICE_QUALIFIER stalled = HS-only). Only endpoints EP0-EP3 exist. VID `0x1935`. `[doc]` {digikit-f42}

section: Overbridge over USB (what Overwitch's README reveals) - the only deep source on Analog Heat +FX so far / USB device side of Digitakt II / Digitone II (digikit finding 42, static, DT2 1.16)
text: Modes -> descriptors: USB MIDI PID `0x012b` (EP1 bulk pair, 2 cables); USB AUDIO/MIDI PID `0x102b` (UAC2 iso on EP2/EP3 + MIDI on EP1); OVERBRIDGE PID `0x0b2b` (vendor class 0xFF: interrupt EP3 in/out, EP2 OUT bulk 512 + EP2 IN interrupt 64, plus MIDI on EP1); a service mode PID `0xffff` with CDC-ACM. No MS-OS/BOS descriptors - Windows will not bind WinUSB on its own. `[doc]` {digikit-f42}

section: Overbridge over USB (what Overwitch's README reveals) - the only deep source on Analog Heat +FX so far / USB device side of Digitakt II / Digitone II (digikit finding 42, static, DT2 1.16)
text: SysEx throughput is limited by the ColdFire's per-byte handling (about 32 instructions per wire byte just to split USB-MIDI events, two 512-byte receive buffers in flight); digikit estimates 0.8-1.4 MB/s at best for an own SysEx route. Transfer's file-write RPC: OpenFileForWrite `0x40`, WriteFileV1 `0x42` (handle, length, offset, data), CloseFileWriter `0x41`. `[doc]` {digikit-f42}

section: Overbridge over USB (what Overwitch's README reveals) - the only deep source on Analog Heat +FX so far / USB device side of Digitakt II / Digitone II (digikit finding 42, static, DT2 1.16)
text: Samples are not converted on the device: the native file is a 0x40-byte header (+1 stereo flag, +4 length, +8 rate 48000) + big-endian int16 PCM + 16-byte trailer; no WAV parser in the image. The host must resample to 48 kHz and convert. `[doc]` {digikit-f42}

section: Overbridge over USB (what Overwitch's README reveals) - the only deep source on Analog Heat +FX so far / Overbridge refuses a mod whose version field changed (Digiwerk OB01, DN2 1.12)
text: The container's 4-byte version field (header `+0x14`, `1.12` on stock) is sent to the computer by the main OS. A build that writes its own name there (e.g. `CMP1`) makes the Overbridge plugin answer "Device is not running compatible OS Version" and fail to open. The engine itself connects; the refusal comes from the plugin. `[hw]`

section: Overbridge over USB (what Overwitch's README reveals) - the only deep source on Analog Heat +FX so far / Overbridge refuses a mod whose version field changed (Digiwerk OB01, DN2 1.12)
text: Fix: patch the two main-OS sites that send the version so they send a header copy with `1.12`. The flash and the power-on screen keep the build's name. Overbridge and Transfer work again on the unit (2026-10-22). `[hw]`

section: Overbridge over USB (what Overwitch's README reveals) - the only deep source on Analog Heat +FX so far / Overbridge refuses a mod whose version field changed (Digiwerk OB01, DN2 1.12)
text: Rule: keep the version field the device expects, or patch only what is sent out. Overbridge logs on macOS: `~/Library/Logs/Elektron Overbridge/`.

text: Alt setting 3: interrupt endpoint `0x83` IN, 368 bytes, and `0x03` OUT, 88 bytes. Seven frames per packet, a 32-byte header and big-endian int32 words, with input data 24-bit in 32-bit words. The measured cadence is 47,999.5 frames/s.

section: Recovery and flashing / Rules of thumb (all from the sources above)
text: A mod can break the normal USB update path without anyone noticing until the next update. On Overtone 1.0 (Digitone II), an OS sent with Transfer stopped at "Receiving" or "PREPARING..." and wrote nothing. The only way off it was the STARTUP menu over DIN, about 15 minutes. Test "install the next build over USB" as part of every release (rule A36). `[hw]` {overtone} ([I22](../INCIDENTS.md#i22-a-mod-broke-the-normal-usb-update-path))

section: Recovery and flashing / Rules of thumb (all from the sources above)
text: Test your DIN interface before you need it. On a DT2, a generic "USB2.0-MIDI" cable adapter (VID 1a86, PID 752d) delivered nothing, while a controller's DIN out worked. Cheap cable adapters are known to drop or mangle long SysEx; a stock-OS dry run with your exact cable is the only proof. `[hw]` {dt2-lab-coldfire-fix} ([I44](../INCIDENTS.md#i44-recovery-used-on-a-digitakt-ii-after-a-crashing-build-a-cheap-cable-delivered-nothing))

section: Recovery and flashing / Additions from the "read everything" pass (2026-10-31)
text: Digitakt II (digitakt-ii-research `RECOVERY.md`): keep an official stock `.syx`, a physical MIDI interface and cable ready; MIDI OUT of the interface to the Digitakt II's MIDI IN (USB MIDI cannot be used); hold FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4 = OS UPGRADE; in Elektron Transfer open the SYSEX TRANSFER page and choose "OS upgrade via device startup menu"; select the stock file and keep power on until the unit reboots. No durations are given and the author states recovery is not guaranteed if the startup menu or bootloader cannot run, power is lost during a critical write, or storage/hardware is damaged; the page reports no hardware test of the procedure. `[doc]` {dt2-recovery}

section: Recovery and flashing / Additions from the "read everything" pass (2026-10-31)
text: Syntakt (SyntHack OS `RECOVERY.md`): if the OS still boots, flash the stock `.syx` via Transfer's Drop page (works even if a mod misbehaved); if not, MIDI interface with a 5-pin OUT to the Syntakt's MIDI IN ("USB doesn't work from the startup menu"), FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4, Transfer SYSEX TRANSFER "OS Upgrade via device startup menu", tens of minutes at 31.25 kbit/s, the unit restarts itself. Avoid TRIG 2 (empty reset) and TRIG 3 (factory reset) in the startup menu - both erase data. Do a dry run of the DIN procedure with the stock OS before the first flash; flash only files for which `tools/unpack/eft.py info <file>` reports `checksums : ok`; no hardware results are reported on the page. `[doc]` {synthack-recovery}

section: Recovery and flashing / Additions from the "read everything" pass (2026-10-31)
text: Other Elektron devices, from elekloader's BUILDING.md (for reference): Analog Rytm MKII and Analog Four MKII - FUNC at power-on (STARTUP menu), TRIG 4, stock `.syx` over 5-pin DIN MIDI, USB does not work. Octatrack - hold FUNC at power-on, TRIG 3 = MIDI UPGRADE, DIN MIDI; normal flashing from the card (PROJECT > SYSTEM > USB DISK MODE, copy the `.bin`, then PROJECT > SYSTEM > OS UPGRADE, power-cycle once more before judging). Digitakt mk1 / Digitone mk1: FUNC, TRIG 4, legacy mode; the connection is not stated for these two. Per-device notes: [`analog-rytm.md`](../devices/analog-rytm.md), [`digitakt.md`](../devices/digitakt.md), [`digitone.md`](../devices/digitone.md). `[doc]` {elekloader-building}

Recovery from such a stall is a power cycle and the startup menu. `[hw]` {overtone} {dt2-install} ([I23](../INCIDENTS.md#i23-plaits-builds-failed-normal-transfer-updates-at-preparing))

section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Official
text: Each device's manual contains the MIDI implementation (CC and NRPN tables, "Appendix B" in the Digitakt II manual for OS 1.03 per the MCP project). The tables of the current Digitakt II, Digitone II and Analog Heat +FX manuals are transcribed below under "Official CC and NRPN tables". These are the only vendor-documented parts. `[doc]` {digitakt-midi-mcp}

section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Official
text: Elektron Transfer is the official tool for dumps, backups and OS upgrades; its legacy OS-upgrade mode is the DIN-MIDI path. {elektron-dt2-notes}

section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Framing and encoding
text: SysEx frame starts `F0 00 20 3C` (Elektron manufacturer ID `00 20 3C`), then device ID and command. `[doc]` {digitakt-midi-mcp} {syxgrid}

section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Framing and encoding
text: Elektron uses its own 7-bit encoding of 8-bit data, ported from elk-herd into SYXGRID and digi-roll-studio. Decode before analysing dumps, otherwise nothing makes sense. `[doc]` {syxgrid} {digi-roll-studio}

section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Framing and encoding
text: Digitone mk1 device ID is `0x0D`; its pattern format differs from Digitone II and SYXGRID rejects it. The DN2's is `0x15`. All known device bytes: [firmware-container.md](firmware-container.md#sysex-device-byte-per-device-merged-from-the-projects-that-decode-these-files). `[doc]` {syxgrid}

section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Framing and encoding
text: Two protocol generations: the Digitakt II / Digitone II speak "gen-2"; Analog Four speaks "gen-1" with a different pattern format and a slower wire. `[doc]` {digi-roll-studio}

section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Framing and encoding
text: Digitone II library contains Digitone mk1 preset files, which use a second container format (refuse foreign formats by magic bytes). `[doc]` {digi-roll-studio}

section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Framing and encoding
text: Container structure and checksums for older machines are best documented in libanalogrytm (Analog Rytm only; no Analog Heat); the frame, packing and checksum match the newer devices, the type bytes do not (section "Dump messages and device ids across generations" below). `[doc]` {libanalogrytm}

section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
text: One dump frame for every generation compared: `F0 00 20 3C <device> <dev id> <type> 01 01 <index> <packed payload> <checksum hi lo> <count hi lo> F7`. The Rytm writes the same `01 01` version field ("OS 1.02c" in libanalogrytm), the same index byte and the same trailer. `[doc]` {libanalogrytm-sysex} {digi-roll-protocol}

section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
text: The same 7-bit packing: groups of one header byte plus up to 7 data bytes; header bit 6 holds the MSB of the first data byte, bit 0 that of the seventh; a short last group keeps its header. syxgrid's DN2 field "control byte 101506, mask `0x40`, payload 101507" is exactly this rule (first byte of a group). `[doc]` {libanalogrytm-sysex} {digi-roll-protocol} {syxgrid-map}

section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
text: The same checksum and count: checksum = sum of the packed payload bytes (header bytes included) mod 2^14, sent as two 7-bit bytes, high first; count = packed length + 5 (checksum, count and `F7`), also mod 2^14. syxgrid recomputed the checksum over raw bytes `[10, 114113)` and matched the DN2's own on every fixture. A DN2 pattern message is 114,118 bytes, so its count field wraps; tools must not use it as a length. `[doc]` {libanalogrytm-sysex} {digi-roll-protocol} {syxgrid-map}

Fields: track, step, note, velocity (`0xFF` = track default), length index (`0xFF` = inherit), and a signed micro-timing byte (1/384 note, -23..+23). A record is free when its track byte is `0xFF`; nothing terminates the table, so skip and keep scanning. Chords are stored as all primary notes first, then all chord extras.

section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Hardware ports and the hidden service console (DT2 1.16 / DN2 1.11)
text: Maintenance mode (a power-on key combination, or a reboot marker) presents a USB CDC-ACM serial port, VID `0x1935` PID `0xFFFF`. It speaks a line protocol: `#COMMAND\n` text lines, `!` + 4-byte big-endian length for binary frames. About 60 factory commands. Read-only examples: `#HELLO` (answers "HOW DO YOU DO?"), `#STATUS` (reports `PLATFORM PCBA0109..`, `PRODUCT 52;5;15;Digitone II`), `#READ_SERIAL` (the "SERI" record at flash `0x3C0000`). Writing commands change persistent state: `#WRITE_SERIAL`, `#WRITE_TESTED`, `#WRITE_UI_TESTED`, `#WRITE_AUDIO_TESTED`, `#MMC_RECONFIGURE`, `#WRITE`, `#UPGRADE`, `#FULL_UPGRADE` (unchecked flash path, see `os-update-protocol.md`). Agents never send these. `[doc]` (digi-roll-studio's ceremony - copy it) 1. Re-read and back up the whole destination pattern first; abort if the backup fails. 2. The target's OS build must be on an allowlist. 3. The user confirms a dialog listing the changes. 4. Change only the bytes that must change. 5. Read the result back and byte-compare. Also: keep a local stash of overwritten patterns (50) plus pre-restore snapshots (10). `[hw]` {digi-roll-studio}

text: Digitakt (mk1) manual: Appendix A lists sound parameters with CC numbers; high-resolution control needs NRPN, which is four CC messages (CC 99 = NRPN MSB, CC 98 = NRPN LSB, CC 6 = data MSB, CC 38 = data LSB), the MSB/LSB per parameter come from the manual; "Receive CC/NRPN" must be enabled under SETTINGS > MIDI CONFIG > PORT CONFIG. A forum user reports that the Digitakt II manual lists no CC values for the Euclidean sequencer parameters and that some Euclidean NRPNs misbehaved before OS 1.10 ("Some NRPN parameters regarding the Euclidean sequencer didn't work as intended" is in the 1.10 notes). The Octatrack is said to be the only Elektron device that answers a CC request. Manuals are updated with every OS - always use the one for the OS in hand. `[?]` {elektronauts-dt2-sample-slot} {elektronauts-heat-midi} {elektron-dt2-notes}

text: selache pitfalls that halt a real DSP but run in the emulator (elekloader ADAPTING.md, Nov 2026; the first matches 70b185's DT2 finding): A shift by a negative immediate (`LSHIFT R1 BY -16`) is encoded without sign extension. Put the count in a register (`R2 = -16; R1 = LSHIFT R1 BY R2;`). elekloader's lint flags candidates, but it cannot see instruction boundaries, so check each one in the listing. A C function whose locals sit more than ~63 words from the frame pointer is compiled wrongly. One large local array is enough. Keep large buffers static or in the voice state. `[hw]` {elekloader-adapting} {own-dt2-notes}

section: Toolchains and emulators / Compilers and builders
text: Two projects compared selache's VISA decoder with digikit's table decoder on the DN2 stock program, and agree on where each is wrong. The test: walk instruction by instruction between known starts (branch targets, `cjump` sites, DO-loop ends) and see who lands exactly. `[doc]` {dn2-selache} {dn2-cfw-t31} selache's disassembler gives some 48-bit forms as 32-bit (Type 3a `59be`, Type 4a `6a3e`, Type 7a `043e`, Type 16a `9980`) and one 32-bit form as 48-bit (Type 3b `593e`); DO-loop ends land on the table decoder's starts 85 of 85 times, on selache's 64 of 85, and selache prints most DO offsets with bit 23 set. digikit's table had Type 2b wrong (the programming guide's `000000011`, not the reference's `110000000`; selache won 119 to 0) and wrongly ruled out `Type10a_rel` in VISA; both fixed in digikit#31. Its `undoc16/48` forms are still provisional. A two-byte-late start still lands 94.9 % of spans, because VISA resynchronises within a few instructions. A decoder's score means something only against that control.

text: Disassembled text is not a patch format. 11,440 distinct encodings from the DN2's L2 program, each disassembled with selmap and reassembled alone with selas: 83.9 % came back identical; 1,265 kept their width but lost register fields the text does not show (`bitrev`, `modify`, `dm` moves); 216 changed width; 320 printed forms could not be parsed; 40 crashed the assembler. A 48-bit `nop` reassembles as the 16-bit one. Patch from source, and compare bytes (rule A41). `[doc]` {dn2-selache}

section: Toolchains and emulators / Writing fast ColdFire C (digigrain's measured notes, Digitakt mk1, gcc `-mcpu=54455 -O2`)
text: Shift immediates only reach 8. A shift by 14 or 15 costs a `moveq` plus a register shift; a shift by 16 is `swap` (+ `ext.l`). Arrange fixed-point products to land on a 16-bit boundary (e.g. store tables as unsigned Q16 so that `(s*w16) >> 16` equals `(s*w15) >> 15` exactly).

text: EMAC in fractional mode (MACSR `0x20`: signed fractional, truncating, no saturation): save and restore MACSR, ACC0 and ACCEXT01, and clear ACC0 first. Bit-exact Python models must truncate each product as `floor(x*y/2^23)`, keeping 8 bits below the LSB.

section: Toolchains and emulators / More emulators and directory snapshots (2026-10-31)
text: Stock Unicorn 2.1.4 (and QEMU master as of 2026-09-15) gets ColdFire wrong in ways that change results (emu-elektron's patch notes) `[doc]` {emu-elektron-patches}: Condition codes: they are committed lazily, so a hook or a counted stop in mid-block sees stale flags, and the next branch goes the wrong way. MAC/MSAC with load is decoded wrongly in four ways: Ry with bit 0 or 1 set faults as "dual accumulate" on a CFV4E; Rx is always D2; MSAC adds instead of subtracting (this also hits MSAC without load); MASK is applied to every load address. The DT2 main OS reaches one of these at `0x400db9e0`. EMAC fractional and signed arithmetic is wrong (as found by SyntHack and octabam). EMAC saturation with MACSR.OMC gets its sign and constants wrong. Any ColdFire emulator built on Unicorn needs these fixes before its audio or branch results mean anything. emu-elektron carries all of them as patches for five devices.
